## अथ सप्तमाध्यायस्य प्रथमः पादः ।

### BOOK SEVENTH.

#### CHAPTER FIRST.

युवोर्नाको ॥ १ ॥ पदानि ॥ यु-बोः, अन-अको ।

वृत्तिः ॥ यु तु ह्येतयोः स्वप्नविशेषणयोः प्रत्यययोः मयि नयाः स्थाने यथासहस्रय मन अक ह्येतावादेशो भवतः ।

*Kārikā* युवोचेद् ह्येतावादेशो ह्येतो यन्तु प्रसज्यते । अथ चेदेकवज्ञावः कथ पुंवज्रवेदयम् ॥

ह्येतो नैगमिको लोप एकत्वे तुमनित्यता । आशिष्यत्वाद्वि लिङ्गस्य पुंस्य वेहि समाश्रितम् ।

1. For यु and यु (nasalised) in an affix, are substituted respectively अन and अक ॥

यु and यु are taken here as stripped of all other indicatory letters, and the semi-vowels are also to be understood to have been nasalised. The अन replaces यु, and अक replaces यु ॥ Thus ल्यु (III. 1. 134)=अन, as नन्द+ल्यु=नन्दनः रमणः ॥ So also व्यु and व्युल् (IV. 3. 23), as सायंतनः, चिरंतनः ॥ यु we find in व्युल् (III. 1. 133), as कृ+व्युल्=कारकः, हारकः ॥ So also युव (IV. 3. 98) as वायुदेवकः, अर्जुनकः ॥

Why do we say nasalised यु and यु? Observe कर्णाया युस् (V. 2. 123) Here the यु is not replaced by अन, and we have कर्णायुः ॥ So also in सुजिघृकृभ्यां युकलुको ॥ Here the यु of युक् and ल्युक् (Un III. 21) are not replaced by अन; as सृज्युः and घृव्युः ॥ In the affixes above mentioned, the semi-vowel is not considered to have the nasal. There are no visible marks of nasality on any affixes, but the maxim is प्रतिज्ञातुनासिक्याः पाणिनीयाः ॥

The word युवोः is the Genitive Singular of युडु considered as a single word, i. e. a Samāhāra Dvandva compound in the singular, and such compounds are always neuter (II. 4. 17). The Genitive Singular of युडु is therefore युडुनः the augment being added by VII. 1. 73. The anomalous form युवोः shows the existence of the maxim that a rule ordaining an augment is not universally valid (अनियमागमशासनम्) ॥ Or the युडु may be considered as masculine Dvandva, and then it proves the maxim that the gender need not be taught, the usage of the people settles the gender of a word (लिङ्गमशिष्यं, लोकाश्रयत्वाद्-लिङ्गस्य) ॥ If, however, युडु be considered an itaretara-yoga Dvandva compound, then its Genitive dual will be युवोः, one यु is elided as a Chhandas irregularity, or the कृ is elided, and we have the युव+ओः=युवोः an anomalous dual.

SOME SUBSTITUTES.

[ Bk. VII. Ch. I. § 2

*Kārikā* :—If युग is taken as a *dual*, then there ought to be a semi-vowel (i. e. युगोः); if it is considered as Aggregate Singular, then it ought to be neuter, how is then युगोः masculine? (To this we answer), if it be taken as dual युग, then there is elision of the युगवेश (i. e. यु); if it be taken as singular युग, then the augment युग which comes in the Genitive Singular of Neuters, does not come here, proving that the rule of युग augment is Anitya (not of universal application). Or the word युग is taken as masculine, because the Gender depends upon usage.

आयनेनीनियः फटखच्छघां प्रत्ययादीनाम् ॥ २ ॥ पदानि ॥ आयन्-पय-ईन् ईय-इयः, फ-ट-ख-छ-घाम्, प्रत्यय-आदीनाम् ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ आयन् एष ईन् ईय ईय इय्येते आविशा भवन्ति यथासंभव क इ ख छ प इय्येतेषां प्रत्ययादीनाम् ।

2. आयन्, for फ्, पय for ट्, ईन् for ख् ईय for छ्, and इय for घ्, are substituted, when these consonants stand in the beginning of an affix.

Thus फक् (IV. 1. 99) = आयन्, as नङ् + फक् = नाडायनः, चारायणः ॥ डक् (IV. 1. 120) = एष as सौपर्णयः, वैनतेयः ॥ ख् (IV. 1. 139) ईन्, as आड्यकुलीनः, श्रोत्रियकुलीनः ॥ छ् (IV. 2. 114) = ईय, as गार्गीयः, वार्सीयः ॥ घ् (IV. 1. 138) = इय, as सन्धियः ॥

Why do we say 'of an *affix*'? Observe फक्कति, वीकति, खमति, छिनति and पूर्णते, where these consonants are in the beginning of a *root*. Why do we say 'in the beginning'? Observe उरुद्रम्, जातुद्रम्, where घ is in the *middle* of the affix; and remains consequently unchanged.

These आयन् &c, substitutions should be understood to have taken place at the very time the affixes फक् &c, are taught, and these substitutions being made, the rule of accent, which makes an affix acute on the first syllable, applies. Thus ख् is not acute, but ई of ईन् substituted for it. Similarly in IV. 4. 117, the affix taught is घञ् with an indicatory ञ्, showing that the final of the affix ईय will be acute (VI. 1. 163), and not of घ्, for घ would have been acute by the general rule affix.

In शने ईः (Up I. 99), शनैः ख् (Up I: 102), the affixes ड् and ख् remain unchanged, and we have शण्वः, and शंखः ॥ This is explained on the maxim of उणादयो बहुलम् (III. 3. 1). In the *sūtra* ऋतेरीयक् (III. 1. 29), the affix ईयक् has been taught and not छक्, this shows that the rule of substitution herein taught does not apply to the affixes to be added to the verbal roots. Thus एजेः खश् (III. 2. 28), पवरुजविषासुशो पम् (III. 3. 16). Here the ख् and घ् are not be replaced by ईन् and इय ॥ In fact, they cannot be regarded as affixes, but only as इत् or servile letters. By I. 3. 8, the gutturals are इत् except in Taddhita: therefore, the substitutions take place in Taddhita affixes, where the ख् and घ् are not इत् ॥

The final ञ् in आयन् and इत् should not, however, be considered as servile (इत्) though they be final consonants. This we infer from the *sūtra*

BK. VII. CH. I § 5.]

SOME SUBSTITUTIONS.

1317

माध्यमवृत्तान् किं बहुलम् ॥ Here the न् of किं is indicatory, showing the position of the accent. But क is replaced by आयन्, so if the न् of आयन् were also to be indicatory (इत्) there would have been no necessity of adding न् in किं ॥ Hence the fact of this न् in किं shows that the न् in आयन् and इत् are not इत् ॥

शो ऽन्तः ॥ १ ॥ पदानि ॥ शः, अन्तः, ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ प्रत्ययावयवस्य हस्य अन्त इत्ययमादिशो भवति ॥

3. अन्त is substituted for the श of an affix.

The word प्रत्यय is understood here, but not so the word आविः ॥ Thus शि becomes अन्ति and शि becomes अन्त (III. 4. 78). As कुर्वन्ति, सुनन्ति and चिन्वन्ति, so also शयान्ते, the तेऽ of शीः ॥ Thus शी + तेऽ = शी + शप् + आ + श (III. 4. 54) = शी + शप् + आ + श (III. 4. 79) = शी + शप् + आ + श (III. 4. 96) = शी + शप् + आ + अन्ते (VII. 1. 3) = शी + आ + अन्ते = शयान्ते (after guna): as अन्ध इदो विजिग्निमाणाः पतिभिः सह शयान्ते ॥ So also in the Unadi affix शप् (Un III. 126): as ज् + शप् = जन्तः, वेऽन्तः ॥ This substitution does not take place when श is not part of an affix: as उन्निता, उन्नितुम्, उन्नितव्यम् ॥ Here also the accent falls on the substitute, according as it is चिन् or otherwise. Thus the substitute अन्त of श is first-acute by the rule III. 1. 3; but the substitute अन्त of शप् is final acute because of the indicatory च (VI. 1. 763) ॥

अदृश्यस्तात् ॥ ४ ॥ पदानि ॥ अत्, अभ्यस्तात्, ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अभ्यस्तादङ्गादुत्तरस्य हाकारस्य अवित्ययमादिशो भवति ॥

4. अत् is substitute for श after a reduplicated verbal stem.

As ईदति, वदतु, वधति, वधतु; जक्षति, जक्षतु; जापति, जापतु ॥ This अत् is replaced by जुत, as अवदु, अवधु: ॥ Here also the accent will be on the firstsyllable of the substitute. Thus ईदति, अत, ईदति, ईदतु, ईदताम् in the subsequent sutras. The accent of the reduplicates, however, is governed by VI. 1. 189, (अभ्यस्तानामादिः) ॥

आत्मनेपदेष्वनतः ॥ ५ ॥ पदानि ॥ आत्मनेपदेषु, अ नतः, (अत्) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ आत्मनेपदेषु यो हाकारस्तस्यानकारान्तादङ्गादुत्तरस्यावित्ययमादिशो भवति ॥

5. अत् is always substituted for the श in the Atmanepada, when it is not preceded by a verbal stem ending in अ ॥

Thus चिन्वते, चिन्वताम्, अचिन्वतः, लुनते, लुनताम्, अलुनत ॥ Why in the Atmanepada? Observe चिन्वन्ति, लुनन्ति ॥ Why “when not preceded by an अ”? Observe च्यवन्ते, प्लवन्ते, in which, though the roots are च्यु and प्लु, they assume the form च्यव and प्लव when the Vikarana शप् is added; the vikaraṇa is added first, because it is nitya; and then the substitution of अन्त or अत for श, as the case may be. The word अनतः qualifies श, the श should be immediately preceded by a stem ending in a non-अ; if some other letter intervenes, the rule will not apply. Thus from शी—शयान्ते, here between शी and श, intervenes the augment आ, therefore श is not preceded by a stem ending in non अ, but by आ ॥

[ Bk. VII. Ch. I § 8

शीङो रुद् ॥ ६ ॥ पदानि ॥ शीङः, रुद् ॥
वृत्तिः ॥ शीङोद्वादुत्तरस्य द्वादशस्यालो रुद्रागमो भवति ॥

6. The अत substitute of झ, gets the augment रुद्, after the root शी ॥

Thus शेरते, शेरताम्, अशेरत ॥ The augment र् is added at the beginning of the affix, making अत=रुद् ॥ Had this र् been an augment of झ, then like the आह augment in शयान्ते, it would have intervened between the शी and झ, and झ not immediately following a non-अ stem, अह् would not have been substituted for झ at all. Therefore रुद् is made the augment of the substitute अत, and not of झ ॥ The root शी is read in the sutra with its anubandha इ in order to indicate, that there is no रुद् augment when there is elision of the Intensive affix यह, nor any Guṇa. As व्यति शेरयते ॥

It is a general rule that an operation applying to a root which is exhibited with an anubandha, will not apply to the same root in its Intensive-yañ-luk form. The following verse shows when operations applying to simple roots will not apply to their Intensive forms:—

दितपा शपादुवन्धेन निर्दिष्टं ग्रहणेन च ।
यथैकाज् ग्रहणं चैव पंचैतानि न ग्रहणुकि ॥

"These five sorts of operations will not apply to Intensive-yañ-luk forms: 1. When the simple root is exhibited in the sutra with दितप् as भू in VII. 4. 73 is shown as भयति ॥ In Intensive, the perfect will be बोभवाम्बकार and not बभवाम्बकार ॥ 2. Where the root is exhibited with शप्, as the root भू in VII. 2. 49 is shown as भर ॥ There is इद after the Desiderative of simple root but not in Intensive. 3. When a simple root is exhibited with an anubhandha, as शीङ् here. 4. Where a gaṇa is mentioned in a rule, as इयन् is taught after Divādi-roots (III. 1. 69). It will apply to simple roots of Divādi gaṇa, and not to their Intensive. 5. Lastly, where the word एकाच् is used in a sutra. As VII. 2. 10. That rule will apply to एकाच् simple roots and not to their Intensives."

वेत्तेविभाषा ॥ ७ ॥ पदानि ॥ वेत्तेः, विभाषा ॥
वृत्तिः ॥ वेत्तेरद्वादुत्तरस्य द्वादशस्यालो विभाषा रुद्रागमो भवति ॥

7. The अत substitute of झ optionally gets the augment रुद् after the verbal stem विद् (वेत्ति) ॥

As संविदते or संविद्वते; संविदताम् or संविद्वताम्; समविद्वत or समविद्वत ॥ The विद् is the Adādi root here, and does not apply to विन्दे, विन्विते, विन्विते, which belongs to the Rudhādi class (विद् विचारणे) ॥

There is no augment in ग्रहणुक् here also, as व्यतिवेविदे ॥

बहुलं छन्दसि ॥ ८ ॥ पदानि ॥ बहुलम्, छन्दसि, (रुद्) ॥
वृत्तिः ॥ छन्दसि विषये बहुलं रुद्रागमो भवति ॥

8. The augment रुद्र is diversely applied in the Veda.

Thus देवा अदुद्र; गन्धर्वा अप्सरसो अदुद्र ॥ Here अदुद्र is the Imperfect (लङ्) plural of दुङ् ॥ Thus दुङ्+झ=दुह्+रत्=अदुद्र, the त् being elided by VII. I. 41. Sometimes, the augment does not take place, as अदुद्र ॥ Owing to the word बहुल, 'diversely', the augment र् is added to other affixes also, than झ ॥ As अदुद्र in अदुद्रस्य केतवः ॥ This is the aorist in अङ् of the root इश by III. I. 57, the guna ordained by VII. 4. 16, does not 'diversely' take place.

अतो मिस् पेस् ॥ ६ ॥ पदानि ॥ अतः, मिस्, पेस् ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अकारान्तादङ्गादुत्तरस्य मिस् ऐसित्यय मावेशो भवति ॥

Kārikā ॥ एष्वं भिसि परत्याचेवत ऐस्स्व भविष्यति । कृतेष्वेवे भौतपूर्वादैस्तु नित्यस्तथा सति ॥

9. After a nominal stem ending in अ, पेस् is substituted for the case-ending मिस् ॥

As वृक्षैः, प्रक्षैः, अतिजरसैः ॥ Why do we say ending in अ? Observe अग्निभिः, वायुभिः ॥ Why 'short अ'? Observe खड्गभिः, मालाभिः ॥ The adhikāra of 'अतः' ('after a short अ'), extends up to VII. I. 17.

The form अतिजरसैः illustrates some important principles of grammar. अति + जरा = (जगमतिकान्नः) अतिजर (अ being shortened by I. 2. 48). The word अतिजर ends in अ, and therefore forms its Ins. pl. by पेस् ॥ Thus अतिजर + पेस् ॥ Now we apply VII. 2. 101, which says for जरा is substituted जरा before vowel-beginning case-endings. It should not be objected, that the substitution is ordained for जरा and not जर; for the maxim एकदेशाविकृतमनन्यवद् भवति (a tail-less dog is still a dog) applies here. Having made this substitution, we get अतिजरसैः ॥ Nor should you object that it was the अ of जर which had given occasion to the existence of पेस्, and that अ should not be destroyed, on the maxim संनिपातलक्षणो विधिरनिमित्तं तद् विधातस्य, for this maxim is not universal, as Pāṇini himself shows in employing the form कहाय (III. I. 14), in which ए of the Dative is changed into य by VII. I. 13, and then this very य causes the destruction of अ and makes it आ (See VII. I. 13 also).

Kārikā :—If there be substitution of ए for the final अ before the affix मिस् by the subsequent sūtra VII. 3. 103, where will then the present sūtra, causing the substitution of पेस् for मिस् after stems ending in अ, find its scope, (because there will be no stem left ending in अ)? If even after changing अ into ए, you change the मिस् into पेस्, because the ए was once अ (भौतपूर्वाद्); then the rule of changing मिस् into पेस् becomes a nitya rule, because it takes effect even after the application of rule VII. 3. 103, and being nitya it debars that rule. Thus वृक्ष + मिस् ॥ Here the subsequent rule VII. 3. 103, requires the अ to be changed into ए ॥ Thus वृक्षे + भिः Now the present rule cannot apply because there is no अदन्त stem. However, if considering that वृक्षे once

[ Bk. VI. Ch. II. 12.

was अयन्त, we change भिः to ऐस् then the rule becomes a *nitya* rule. In fact, it is a *nitya* rule and debars the application of VII. 3. 103, within its jurisdiction, VII. 3. 103, finds its scope in वृक्ष + सु = वृक्षेषु ॥

बहुलं छन्दसि ॥ १० ॥ पदानि ॥ बहुलम्, छन्दसि, (ऐस्) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ छन्दसि विषये बहुलमेसावेशो भवति ॥

10. In the Veda the substitution takes place diversely.

That is ऐस् is substituted for भिस् even after stems which do not end in short अ; as नषः; and some times the substitution does not take place even after stems ending in short अ, as, देवोभिः सर्वेभिः प्रोक्तम् ॥ देवोदेवोभिरामगत् (Rig Veda I. 1. 4).

नेदमदसोरकोः ॥ ११ ॥ पदानि ॥ न, इदम्, अदसोः, अ, कोः, (भिस् ऐस्) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ इदम् अदस इलेतयोरककारयोभिस् ऐस् भवति ॥

11. This substitution of ऐस् does not take place after इदम् and अदस, except when they end in क ॥

As एभिः, अमीभिः, but इमकैः, अयुकैः ॥ By VII. 2. 102, अ is substituted for the final of इदम्, as इद + अ = इद (VI. 1. 97). By VII. 2. 113, the इद is elided before भिस्, and the only portion left is अ, which becomes ए according to VII. 3. 103. For the final of अदस is similarly by VII. 2. 102, अ substituted, and अद + अ = अद (VI. 1. 97), and according to our present *sūtra*, the form in Ins.pl. would be अदेभिः, but इ is changed to म by VIII. 2. 80, and ए to ई by VIII. 2. 81.

The exception made with regard to these forms ending in क, shows the existence of the following maxim : तदमध्यपतितस्तदमहणेन गुह्यते “Any term that may be employed in Grammar denotes not merely what is actually denoted by it, but it denotes also whatever word-form may result when something is inserted in that which is actually denoted by it.”

The *sūtra* has not been made as इदमवसोः कात्, for had it been so constructed the rule would have applied to the क ending इदम् and अदस and to no other क ending pronoun, and we could not get the forms सर्वकैः, विश्वकैः ॥ Moreover such a construction would have made ऐस् applicable to इदम् and अदस also in their simple states : i. e. we could not have got the forms एभिः or अमीभिः ॥ Therefore the negative construction न अकोः is used in *sutra* in order to prevent the rule of contrariety.

टाडसिडसामिनात्स्याः ॥ १२ ॥ पदानि ॥ टा, डसि, डसाम, इन, आत्, स्याः, ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अकारान्तावह्लादुत्तरेषां टाडसिडसाम इन आत् स्य इलेते आवेशा भवन्ति यथासंख्यम् ॥

12. After a stem ending in अ, are substituted इन for the Instrumental ending ; आ आत् for the Ablative ending अस्, and स्य for the Genitive ending अस् ॥

Thus वृक्षेण and प्रक्षणः; वृक्षात् and प्रक्षात्; and वृक्षस्य and प्रक्षस्य ॥ After stems not ending in अ we have the original ending, as पत्या, सख्या ॥ Some

BK. VII. CH. I. §. 15 ]

SOME SUBSTITUTIONS.

1321

would have the forms अतिजरस्तिन and अतिजरसात् from अतिजर ॥ This is on the analogy of अतिजरसः [See Sūtra 9 ante]. Thus अति+जरा=अतिजर (I. 2. 48). Then by VII. 2. 101, जस् is substituted for ज् before the vowel-affixes. These forms are not supported however by Patanjali. According to him the forms will be either अतिजर, अतिजरात्, or अतिजरसा and अतिजरसः but never अतिजरसिन and अतिजरसात् ॥

ऊर्यः ॥ १३ ॥ पदानि ॥ ऊः, यः, ( अतः अङ्गस्य ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ ऊरिति चतुर्थैकवचनस्य प्रहणम् अकारान्तादङ्गादुत्तरस्य ऊ इत्येतस्य च इत्ययमादिशो भवति ॥

13. After a stem ending in अ, there is substituted य for the Dative ending प ॥

Thus वृक्षाय, वृक्षाय, the अ is lengthened by VII. 3. 102, in spite of the maxim संनिपातलक्षणो विधि रानिमित्तम् तदविधातस्य ॥ “That which is taught in a rule the application of which is occasioned by the combination of two things, does not become the cause of the destruction of that combination”. Thus य is substituted here, because the preceding word ends in a short अ, thus this short अ occasioned the existence of य, therefore this य cannot occasion the destruction of अ ॥ But that however it does, for it is on account of this य, that the preceding अ is replaced by आ ॥

The ऊः is the anomalous genitive case of the Dative ending ऊः; this affix is exhibited without any vibhakti in VII. 1. 28. The ऊः should not be taken as the Genitive singular of ऊः the affix of the Locative singular.

सर्वनाशः स्मै ॥ १४ ॥ पदानि ॥ सर्वनाशः, स्मै, ( अतः ऊः ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अकारान्तात्सर्वनाश उत्तरस्य ऊः स्मै इत्ययमादिशो भवति ॥

14. After a Pronominal stem ending in अ, स्मै is substituted for the प of the Dative.

As सर्वस्मै, विश्वस्मै, यस्मै, कस्मै, तस्मै ॥ But भवते where the Pronoun does not end in अ ॥ When अश is substituted for इदम् (II. 4. 32) in anvādeśa sentences, then we have the form अस्मै ॥ But in अच इदम्+ऊ=अच अ+ए=अचा+ए, here the preceding word ends in आ and we could not have ए replaced by स्मै ॥ Therefore we infer that स्मै being an antaranga operation should be substituted first, and the sandhi afterward and we get अचास्मै ॥ (See VII. 2. 102 for the change of यद्, तद् &c into य, त &c). The change of ए into स्मै is antaranga as it depends upon one word, while the एकादिश long आ is bahiranga because it is an operation depending upon two words.

ऊसिञ्च्योः स्मादस्मिनौ ॥ १५ ॥ पदानि ॥ ऊसि, ऊयोः, स्माद, स्मिनौ, ( अतः सर्वनाशः ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ ऊसि ऊ इत्येत्योरकारान्तात्सर्वनाश उत्तरयोः स्माद स्मिन् इत्येतावादिशो भवतः ॥

15. After a Pronominal stem ending in अ, स्माद

1322

SOME SUBSTITUTES.

[ Bk. VII. Ch. I. §. 18.

is substituted for the Ablative ending अस् and स्मिन् for the Locative ending इ ॥

Thus सर्वस्मात्, विश्वस्मात्, यस्मात्, तस्मात् and कस्मात् ॥ सर्वस्मिन्, विश्वस्मिन् यस्मिन्, तस्मिन् and अन्यस्मिन् ॥ But भवतः and भवति from भवत् ending in a non-अ, and वृक्षात् and वृक्षे in non-pronouns. See VII. 2. 102 for यह लह &c.

पूर्वादिभ्यो नवभ्यो वा ॥ १६ ॥ पदानि ॥ पूर्व-आदिभ्यः, नवभ्यः, वा, ( सर्व-नाशः ऊसिङ्गोः स्मात् स्मिनौ ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ पूर्वादिभ्यो नवभ्यः सर्वनाम उत्तरयोऽसिङ्गोः स्मात् स्मिन् इत्येतावदिशो वा भवतः ॥

16. स्मात् and स्मिन् are optionally substituted for the Ablative and Locative endings, after पूर्व and the eight that follow it (I. 1. 34).

Thus पूर्वस्मात् or पूर्वात्, पूर्वस्मिन् or पूर्वे, परस्मात् or परात्, परस्मिन् or परे, अवरस्मात्, or अवरात्, अवरस्मिन् or अवरे, दक्षिणस्मात् or दक्षिणात्, दक्षिणस्मिन् or दक्षिणे, उत्तरस्मात्, or उत्तरात्, उत्तरस्मिन्, or उत्तरे, अपरस्मात्, or अपरात्, अपरस्मिन्, or अपरे, अपरस्मात्, or अधरस्मिन्, or अधरे, स्वस्मात्, or स्वात्, स्वस्मिन् or स्वे, अन्तरस्मात् or अन्तरात्, अन्तरस्मिन् or अन्तरे ॥ नवभ्य इति किम्, तस्मात्, तस्मिन् ॥

Why do we say 'nine only'? Observe तस्मात् and तस्मिन्, no option is allowed here.

जसः शी ॥ १७ ॥ पदानि ॥ जसः, शी, ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ आकाशान्तासर्वनाम उत्तरस्य जसः शीत्ययमादिशो भवति ॥

17. After a Pronominal stem ending in अ, ई is substituted for the nominative plural अस् ॥

Thus सर्वे (सर्व+ई), विश्वे, ये, के, ते ॥ Though सर्व+ई would have also given सर्वे, the long ई is taken for the sake of subsequent sutras, in forming बपुणी, जतुनी ॥

औङ् आपः ॥ १८ ॥ पदानि ॥ औङ्, आपः, ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ आवन्तादङ्गादुत्तरस्यौङ् शीत्ययमादिशो भवति ॥

*Kārikā*—औकारोयं शीभिधी डिङ्गुर्हीतो डिङ्गास्माकं नास्ति कोयं प्रकारः ।

सामान्यार्थस्तस्य चासंजनस्मिन्किल्कार्यं ते दया प्रसक्तं स दोषः ॥

डिङ्गे विद्याद्वर्णनिरैशमायं वर्णं यत्स्वाच्च विद्याच्छादि ।

वर्णभायं तेन डिङ्गेप्यदोषो निदेशोयं पूर्वसूत्रेण वा स्यात् ॥

18. After a stem ending in the feminine affix आ, ई is substituted for the dual endings औ of the Nominative and Accusative.

Thus खट्टे तिष्ठतः, खट्टे पदय, बहुराजे (IV. 1. 13), कारीषगन्ध्ये ॥ The इ in औङ् is for the purposes of included औङ् also. There is, in fact, no such affix as औङ् taught by Pāṇini any where. The following Karika raises this question and certain doubts in the first verse and then answers them in the second.

BK. VII. CH. I §. 20. ] शि SUBSTITUTION.

1323

*Kārikā* :—In this rule about शी, the letter ओ has been enunciated with an indicatory ह्; but we have no ओ with a ह्, taught any where. What sort of sūtra construction is this? If you say, the use of ह् is to form a common term for the two affixes ओ and ओह्, then by so doing, हिन् operations must be performed with regard to this शी of yours, and this is an error. [शी replacing हिन् ओह् will be considered as हिन्, and being हिन्, it will take the augment याद by VII. 3. 113 : and the form will be खद्गि and not खद्गि ] ॥

*Ans* :—The ह् should be considered here as merely indicating the letter ओ, and as not an ह्, so that whatever will apply to the letter ओ will apply to any form beginning with it, by the maxim बसिम् विधि तवावान् भङ्गे ॥ Or ओह् may be considered as merely the letter ओ and not any particular *affix*, and ह् is added only for the sake of facility of pronunciation, like ह् in कूरोरम् ओ being merely a letter, will include all affixes having the letter ओ as their significant part : and thus the ओह् not being a हिन् affix the rule VII. 3. 113, will not apply : and so there is no anomaly. Or the form ओह् may be considered as the affix of the dual, for Nominative and Accusative in the terminology of Ancient Grammarians, and will not produce हिन् effects, because the anubandhas of the Ancients do not produce their effects in this Grammar of Pāṇini : i.e. the rules regarding anubandhas made by Pāṇini refer to the anubandhas made by him and not by older authors.

नपुंसकाच्च ॥ १६ ॥ पदानि ॥ नपुंसकात्, च ( ओङ्: शी ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ नपुंसकावङ्गादुत्तरस्य ओङ्: शी इत्ययमादिशो भवति ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ इषां प्रतिषेधो वक्तव्यः ॥

19. After a neutral stem, ई is substituted for the nom. and acc. dual ओ ॥

Thus कुण्डे: तिष्ठतः, कुण्डे पञ्च ॥ कुण्ड+ई=कुण्डे, the अ of कुण्ड required to be elided by VI. 4. 148. This is, however, not done by the following

*Vārt* :—Prohibition should be stated in the case of the affix शी ॥ Therefore the अ is not elided.

Similarly इधिनी, मधुनी, चपुनी, जतुनी ॥ The augment म् is added by VII. 1. 73.

जदशसो: शि: ॥ २० ॥ पदानि ॥ जस्, शसो:, शि:, ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ नपुंसकावङ्गादुत्तरयोर्जदशसो: शि इत्ययमादिशो भवति ॥

20. After a neutral stem, इ is substituted for the endings of the Nominative and Accusative Plural (जस् and शस्) ॥

Thus कुण्डानि तिष्ठन्ति, कुण्डानि पञ्च, इधीनि, मधुनि, चपुनि, जतुनि ॥ The augment म् is by VII. 1. 72, The word शस् in the sūtra being read along with जस्

2

1324

ELISION OF सु AND अम् ॥

[ Bk. VII. Ch. I. §. 23.

denotes the Accusative Plural ending शस् and not the Taddhita affix शस् (V. 4. 43); as कुण्डशो वृक्षति, वनशः प्रविशति ॥

अष्टाभ्य औश् ॥ २१ ॥ पदानि ॥ अष्टाभ्यः, औश्, ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अष्टाभ्य इति कृताकारोऽष्टशशो गृह्यते तस्मादुत्तरयोर्जैश्वर्यशोभिरित्ययमावेशो भवति ॥

21. After the stem अष्टा (the form assumed by अष्टम् VII. 2. 84), औश् is substituted for the endings of the Nominative and Accusative Plural.

As अष्टौ तिष्ठन्ति, अष्टौ पद्य ॥ Why have we taken the form अष्टा and not अष्ट? Observe अष्ट तिष्ठन्ति, अष्ट पद्य ॥ This peculiar construction of the present sūtra (अष्टाभ्यः instead of अष्टम्) indicates, that the अष्ट substitution for the नृ of अष्टम् is optional. This sūtra is, moreover, an exception by anticipation, to the following sūtra, by which the plural Nom. and Acc. endings are elided after the numerals called पद्य ॥ The elision of case-endings taught by II. 4. 71, is not, however, barred by this rule; the elision taught therein will take place, whether this rule applies or not. Thus अष्टपुत्रः, अष्टमार्यः ॥

The present rule applies even when अष्ट is at the end of a compound, as परमाष्टौ, उत्तमाष्टौ ॥ But in प्रियाष्टानः, औ does not come, as अष्टम् has not assumed the form अष्टा here i. e. it has not lost its नृ ॥

षड्भ्यो लुक् ॥ २२ ॥ षड्भ्यः, लुक्, ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ षड्भ्योऽष्टा उत्तरयोर्जैश्वर्यशोभिर्यति ॥

22. The Nom. and Acc. Plural endings are elided after the Numerals called षष् (I. 1. 24).

As षष् तिष्ठन्ति, षष् पञ्च, पञ्च, सप्त, नव, वश ॥ The rule applies even to compounds ending with 'shash' words: as परमषष्, उत्तमषष्, but the 'shash' should be the principal; if it is only a secondary member of the compound, the rule will not apply: as प्रियषष्, प्रियपञ्चानः ॥ For the elision of नृ see VIII. 2. 7.

स्वमोनैपुंसकात् ॥ २३ ॥ पदानि ॥ सु, अमोः, नपुंसकात्, ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ सु अम् इषेतयोर्नपुंसकादुत्तरयोर्जैश्वर्यशोभिर्यति ॥

23. The nom. and acc. singular case-endings सु and अम् are elided after a Neutral stem.

As वधि तिष्ठति, वधि पद्य, मधु तिष्ठति, मधु पद्य ॥ So also मधु and अतु ॥ In सद् ब्राह्मणकुलम् the word सद् has lost its nom. sing. ending by this rule, which has thus superseded the subsequent rule VII. 2. 102, by anticipation, by which अम् replaces the final नृ of सद् ॥ Or this *luk* rule of the present sūtra is a Nitya rule compared with VII. 2. 102. How can this be a nitya rule when it is set aside by the next rule अमोऽम् ॥ We still call this rule nitya, on the maxim

BK. VII. CH. I. §. 25 ]

अदृढ़ SUBSTITUTE.

1325

यस्य च लक्षणान्तरेण निमित्तं विहन्यते न तदनित्यम् "(an operation) the cause of which would, (after the taking effect of another operation that applies simultaneously), be removed by another (third rule), is not, (on that account regarded as) not nitya". For here the cause which is luk-elision, is removed by the following aphorism अतोऽम् which ordains an अम् instead of luk, and not by VII. 2. 102. For the application of rule VII. 2. 102, the necessary condition is that a case-affix should follow तद् &c. But when the case-affix itself is luk-elided, the substitution taught in that sūtra cannot take place.

अतोऽम् ॥ २५ ॥ पदानि ॥ अतः, अम्, ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अकारान्तानुप्रसक्तानुत्तरयोः स्वमोरमित्ययमादेशो भवति ॥

24. After a Neutral stem in अ, अम् is substituted for सु and अम् the endings of the nom. and acc. sing.

As कुण्डं तिष्ठति, कुण्डं पद्य ॥ So also वनम्, पीठम् ॥ Why do we not say "म् is substituted"? कुण्ड+म्=कुण्डाम्, thus there would be lengthening if only म् was taught (VII. 3. 101), while कुण्ड+अम्=कुण्डम् (the single substitution of the form of the antecedent by VI. 1. 107).

अदृढ़ं इतरादिभ्यः पञ्चभ्यः ॥ २५ ॥ पदानि ॥ अदृढ़ं, इतरा दिभ्यः, पञ्चभ्यः ॥
वृत्तिः ॥ इतरादिभ्यः परयोः स्वमोरदृढ़ं इत्ययमादेशो भवति ॥

Kārikā अपुक्ष्वभेदो दोपो निवृत्ते इतरादिषु । अदृढित्वा इतरादीनां न लोपो मापि दीर्घता ॥

25. अदृढ़ is substituted for the Nom. and Acc. singular endings सु and अम् after the five Pronouns इतर &c. (i. e. the stems formed with the affixes 1. इतर, and 2. इतम्, and the stems 3. इतर, 4. अन्य and 5. अन्यतर).

These are the five pronouns, which in the list of Sarvanāmans are read together (See I. 1. 27):—इतर, इतम्, इतर, अन्य and अन्यतर ॥ Thus कतर+अदृढ़=कतरत् (the अ of katara elided by इ): as कतरत् तिष्ठन्ति, कतरत् पद्य ॥ So also कतमत्, इतरत्, अन्यतरत् and अन्यत् ॥ Why after these five only? Observe नेत्रं तिष्ठन्ति, नेत्रं पद्य ॥ Why do we make the affix have an indicatory इ? In order to prevent the lengthening of the vowel in the nominative singular: as कतर+अत्=कतरात् by VI. 1. 102. In the case of the accusative, अत् being the substitute of अम् will be sthānivat, and give us कतरत् by VI. 1. 107 even without इ ॥ Why not make the affix merely त् and not अदृढ़; it would give कतरत् &c without the application of any rule of Sandhi? The simple त् would not give us the Vocative हे कतरत्, The final would have been elided in the Vocative, as being an aprikta. See however VI. 1. 69.

Kārikā:—If in the sūtra VI. 1. 69, there is the anuvṛtti of the word 'apṛkta', then there is fault with regard to अम् (i. e. the vocative of members in अम् will not be elided, हे कुण्डम् will be the form required and not हे कुण्ड); if

1326

SOME SUBSTITUTIONS.

[ Bk. VII. Ch. I §. 28.

however, the anuvritti of aprkta ceases, there will be anomaly with regard to pronouns कतरत् &c (i. e. we shall not have the form हे कतरत् but हे कतरत्) Therefore, by reading the affix अत् with an indicatory इ i. e reading it as अदृढ, we get out of this dilemma, and so there is not the elision of अत् in कतरत् &c in the vocative; nor is there lengthening of the vowel (कतरत्, which would have been the form had there been no इ).

नेतराच्छन्दसि ॥ २६ ॥ पदानि ॥ न, इतरात, छन्दसि, ॥
वृत्तिः ॥ इतरशब्दात्तरयोः स्वमोऽछन्दसि विषये अदृढादेशो न भवति ॥

26. In the Veda, अत् (or अदृ) is not the substitute of सु and अम् Nom. and Acc. Sg. endings, after इतर ॥

As इतरमितरमण्डमजायत; वार्धमितरम् ॥ Why in the Vedas? See इतरत् काष्ठम्, इतरत् कुडचम् ॥ Had this sutra been placed immediately after अतोऽम् (VII. 1. 24), we could have made it simpler by saying इतराच्छन्दसि; the present position of the sutra indicates that we should divide it into two, to include other cases. In the case of एकतर, the अदृढ substitution does not take place, either in the Veda or in the Common Language. As एकतरं तिष्ठति, एकतरं पदम् ॥

युष्मदस्मद्भ्यां ङसो ऽश् ॥ २७ ॥ पदानि ॥ युष्मदस्मद्भ्याम्, ङसः, अश् ॥
वृत्तिः ॥ युष्मदस्मद्भ्याम् युष्मदस्मद्भ्याम् ङसो ऽशित्ययमादेशो भवति ॥

27. अश् (I. 1. 55), is substituted for the Genitive ending अस्, after युष्मद् and अस्मद् ॥

Thus तव and मम ॥ The indicatory श् of अश् shows that by I. 1. 55, the whole of the affix अस् is to be replaced: otherwise it would have replaced only the first letter of the affix; and the affix not being a substitute-affix, rule VII. 2. 89, would not be applicable to it. The तव is substituted for युष्मद्, and मम for अस्मद् by VII. 2. 96; and तव+अ (अश्), and मम+अ=तव and मम by VI. 1. 97.

डे प्रथमयोरम् ॥ २८ ॥ पदानि ॥ डे, प्रथमयोः, अम्, ॥
वृत्तिः ॥ डे इत्यविभक्तिको निर्देशः डे इत्येतस्य प्रथमयोश्च विभक्तोः प्रथमाद्वितीययोः युष्मदस्मद्भ्याम् युष्मदस्मद्भ्याम् युष्मदस्मद्भ्याम् युष्मदस्मद्भ्याम् भवति ॥

28. अम् is substituted for the Dative ending ए and for the endings of the nom. and acc. in all numbers, after the stems युष्मद् and अस्मद् ॥

The डे the ending of the Dative is exhibited anomalously in the sutra without any case ending (compare VII. 1. 13, डे:) प्रथमयोः means 'of the first and second cases.' Thus युष्मद्+डे=तुभ्यद्+डे (VII. 2. 95)=तुभ्य+डे (VII. 1. 102) =तुभ्य+अम् (VII. 1. 28)=तुभ्यम् (VI. 1. 107 or 97); similarly महाम् ॥ So also युष्मद्+सु=त्वद्+सु (VII. 2. 94)=त्व+सु (VII. 2. 94)=त्व+सु (VII. 2. 102)=त्व+अम्

BK. VII. CH. I. §. 30 ]

SUBSTITUTION OF CASE-AFFIXES.

1327

(VII. 1. 28) = लम् (VI. 1. 97 or 107). Similarly अहम् ॥ So also युवाम् and आवाम् by VII. 2. 92 and VI. 2. 88; युयम् and वयम् by VII. 2. 93 and VI. 1. 97 or 107, लाम् and नाम् by VII. 2. 97 and VII. 2. 87; and युवाम् and आवाम् as before.

शसो न ॥ २६ ॥ पदानि ॥ शसः, न, ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ युष्मदस्मजपावृत्तस्य शसो नकारादेशो भवति ॥

29. न is substituted for the स of अस् the affix of the Accusative Plural after युष्मद् and अस्मद् ॥

As युष्मान् and अस्मान् (दृ elided by VII. 2. 90, and lengthening by VII. 2. 87). युष्मान् ब्राह्मणान् । अस्मान् ब्राह्मणान् । युष्मान् ब्राह्मणीः । अस्मान् ब्राह्मणीः । युष्मान् कुलानि । अस्मान्कुलानि ॥

भ्यसो भ्यम् ॥ ३० ॥ पदानि ॥ भ्यसः, भ्यम् ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ युष्मदस्मजपावृत्तस्य भ्यसो भ्यमित्ययमादेशो भवति ॥

30. अभ्यम् is substituted for the Dative भ्यस after 'yushmad' and 'asmad.'

As युष्मभ्यम् and अस्मभ्यम् ॥ As the sūtra is constructed (भ्यसो भ्यम्) it is not easy to say whether the substitute is भ्यम् or अभ्यम् ॥ If it is भ्यम्, then we have two cases, (1) eliding the final दृ of yushmad and asmad, by VII. 2. 90, and adding भ्यम् (2) eliding अदृ of yushmad and asmad by VII. 2. 90, and adding भ्यम् ॥ It will be shown hereafter that VII. 2. 90, is capable of two explanations, one by which yushmad and asmad lose their दृ only, and by another अदृ ॥ Similarly with अभ्यम् we have also two cases: Thus we have four cases, as (1) yushma+bhyam, (2) yushm+bhyam, (3) yushma+abhyam, (4) yushm+abhyam. In the case of the first (yushma+bhyam) we can get the proper form, though it may be objected that yushma+bhyam should be equal to युष्मभ्यम् by VII. 3. 103: this ए substitution will not take place, however, by force of the maxim अङ्गवृत्त पुनर्वृत्तावविधि निर्विघ्नतस्य 'when an operation which is taught in the angādhikāra has taken place, and another operation of the angādhikāra is subsequently applicable, this latter operation is not allowed to take place.'

The second case is an impossibility, namely, yushm+bhyam can give us no form. The third case yushma+abhyam will give us the proper form युष्मभ्यम् (अ+अ=अ by VI. 1. 97). Moreover the accent also will be on the middle युष्मभ्यम् by VI. 1. 161, the udātta अ of yushma being elided by the anudātta अ of अभ्यम्, the acute will be on the anudātta अ ॥ It should not be objected that in VI. 1. 161, the word अन्त of VI. 1. 159 is understood, and the accent will be on the final. We have shown in that sūtra, that the udātta will fall on the आदि (beginning) of the anudātta term which causes the elisi n The fourth alternative yushm+abhyam is free from all objections.

1328

ओं SUBSTITUTE OF णल् ॥

[ Bk. VII. Ch. I. §. 34.

पञ्चम्या अत् ॥ ३१ ॥ पदानि ॥ पञ्चम्या, अत् ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ पञ्चम्या भ्यसौ युष्मदस्संप्रापुत्तरस्य अतित्ययमादिशो भवति ॥

31. अत् is substituted for the Ablative भ्यस, after युष्मद् and अस्मद् ॥

As युष्मद्, अस्मद् ॥ The ॠ is elided by VII. 2. 95, before the case ending भ्यस, and युष्म+अत्=युष्मद् by VI. 1. 97.

एकवचनस्य च ॥ ३२ ॥ पदानि ॥ एकवचनस्य, च ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ पञ्चम्या एकवचनस्य युष्मदस्संप्रापुत्तरस्य अतित्ययमादिशो भवति ॥

32. This substitution of अत् is made in the singular number also of the ablative, after yushmad and asmad.

As खद् and मद् ॥ For the substitution of ख and म see VII. 2. 97; and ख and म+अत्=खद् and मद् by VI. 1. 97.

साम आकम् ॥ ३३ ॥ पदानि ॥ सामः आकम् ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ साम इति पष्ठीबहुवचनमागतसुदृढं गृह्यते, तस्य युष्मदस्संप्रापुत्तरस्याकामित्ययमादिशो भवति ॥

33. आकम् is substituted for the Genitive plural affix साम (VII. 1. 52), after yushmad, and asmad.

साम is the affix आम of the Genitive plural with the augment स ॥ Thus युष्माकम् and अस्माकम् ॥ Why is it read साम and not आम, when there is no स at the time when the substitution is ordained? It is read as साम in order to indicate that आकम् will not get the augment स, for otherwise 'yushma' and 'asma' having lost their 'd' by VII. 2. 90, end in अ, and so by VII. 1. 52, would cause the genitive affix to get the augment स; the present sūtra removes that also. The substitute is exhibited with a long आ, in order to make अ+आ=आ in युष्म+आकम्, had it been short अ, then there would have been no lengthening but अ+अ=अ by VI. 1. 97. If you say 'the very fact that आकम् was taught and not कम्, would prevent para-rūpa and cause lengthening'; we reply, that the अ of आकम् would find its scope in preventing ए substitution. For without अ, we should have युष्म+कम्=युष्मेकम् (VII. 3. 103).

आत ओ णलः ॥ ३४ ॥ पदानि ॥ आतः, ओ, णलः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ आकारान्तादङ्गादुत्तरस्य णल ओकारादिशो भवति ॥

34. ओ is substituted for णल्, the affix of the first and third person singular of the perfect, after roots ending in long आ ॥

Thus पषो, तस्थो, जन्तो, मन्तो, from पा, स्था, नै (ग्ला) and नै (ब्ला) ॥ The form पषो is thus evolved, पा+णल्=पा+अ ॥ Here three operations simultaneously present themselves for application, namely; 1. Reduplication, 2. Leng-

BK. VII. CH. I. §. 35 ]

तातङ् SUBSTITUTION.

1329

thening; by the single substitution of one long vowel आ, for आ+अ; and 3. The substitution of औ for आ by the present sūtra. In what order should these operations be then performed? First the affix अ should be replaced by औ. then the single substitution of औ for आ+औ; and then treating it as sthānivat, and then reduplication. For if the single substitution of आ for आ+अ had taken place first, then there would be no scope for औ substitution, therefore the औ substitution, should take place first. Thus we have पा+औ=पौ; this vṛddhi-ekādeśa, is treated as sthānivat by I. I. 59, and it causes reduplication. The vṛddhi-ekādeśa should first take place (i. e. आ+औ=औ) and then the reduplication, because the former rule is subsequent to the latter.

तुह्योस्तातङ्शिष्यन्यतरस्याम् ॥ ३५ ॥ पदानि ॥ तु, ह्योः, तातङ्, आशिषि, अन्यतरस्याम् ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ तु हि इत्येतयोराशिषि विषये तातङ्गवेशो भवत्यन्तरस्याम् ॥

35. तातङ् is optionally substituted for the affixes तु and हि of the Imperative, when benediction is meant.

As जीवतात् भवान्, जीवतात् त्वम्, जीवतु भवान्, जीव त्वम् ॥ The ङ prevents Guṇa and Vṛddhi, (I. I. 4), and the substitute replaces the whole affix (I. I. 53 notwithstanding). The substitute is not sthānivat पितृ, though it replaces a पितृ affix, because it has its own indicatory letter ङ, and ङित् does not become पितृ; and consequently in ज्ञातत् ई is not added to the affix, by VII. 3. 93, ई being added only to पितृ affixes after ङ् ॥ When not denoting benediction, we have not this substitution: as धानं गच्छतु भवान् or गच्छ धामम् ॥

The affix तातङ् being a substitute of हि, is like हि, and, therefore, rules propounded with regard to हि, will apply to तातङ् also. Thus VI. 4. 105 says that after stems ending in short अ, the हि is elided; therefore, after such words तातङ् should also be elided. Therefore we cannot get the form जीवतात् त्वम् for जीवत्वम् ॥ This objection, however, is futile; for, in the sūtra अतो हे (VI. 4. 105), there is the anuvritti of हि from sūtra VI. 4. 101 (इ ह्यन्यो हे ङिः) ॥ So that अतो हे should be construed as meaning “there is the elision of हि when it is of the form हि, and not when it assumes the form तातङ्” ॥

The object of ङ् in तातङ् is, as we have said above, for the sake of preventing Guṇa and Vṛddhi. It should not be said that the object of ङ् in तातङ् is for the sake of अन्याविधिः by the application of sūtra ङिच (I. I. 53), just as the substitutes अनङ् &c (VII. I. 93 and 94) apply to the finals. For by so doing, तातङ् would replace only the ङ of तु and the ङ of हि, which is not desired. And the case of तातङ् is to be distinguished from अनङ्, for in अनङ् the ङ has no other object but to prevent sarvādeśa; but in तातङ् we see that ङ has another object, namely, the prevention of Guṇa and Vṛddhi; and ङ having thus found scope, the तातङ् substitute will be governed by the general rule अनेकात् पितृ सर्वस्य (I. I. 55).

1330

स्वप् SUBSTITUTE.

[ Bk. VII. Ch. I. §. 37.

The Kārikā given below raises these points.

Kārikā:—तात्त्विक् किल्वं संक्रामकृत्यादन्त्यविधिषेत्तच्च तथा न ।

हेरधिकारे हेरधिकारो लोपविधौ तु ज्ञापकम् ॥

तात्त्विक् किल्वसामर्थ्याश्रयमन्त्यविधिः स्तुतः ।

न तद्वदनङ्गवीनां तेन ते अन्त्यविकारजाः ॥

Kārikā:—In तात्त्विक् क् is for the sake of preventing Guṇa and Vṛiddhi (संक्रम=गुणवृद्धिप्रतिबोधः) ॥ If it be said, it is for the sake of अन्त्याविधि by I. 1. 53; we say it is not so. (If you say that after roots ending in short अ, तात्त्विक् should be elided, by VI. 4. 105 read with I. 1. 56, we reply): when the anuvṛtti or adhikāra of हि was already existent in the sūtra VI. 4. 105 from sūtra VI. 4. 101, the express employment of हि in VI. 4. 105, indicates that the lopa rule does not apply to तात्त्विक् ॥ (The lopa-rule not applying to तात्त्विक्, it follows that it replaces the whole of हि and not only its final). The क् in तात्त्विक् finds its scope in preventing Guṇa and Vṛiddhi, therefore, it is not for the sake of antyavidhi (I. 1. 53). The किल्वं in अतक् &c has no other scope, therefore, these substitutes replace the final only.

विदेः शतुर्वसुः ॥ ३६ ॥ पदानि ॥ विदेः, शतुः, वसुः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ विद् ज्ञानइत्येतस्माद्धातोरुत्तरस्य शतुर्वसुरादिशो भवति ॥

36. वसु is substituted for the Present Participle affix शतु after the root विद् 'to know'.

Thus विद्वत् (n. s. विद्वान्), विद्वांसी, विद्वांसः ॥ The words formed with affixes having an indicatory उ or ऋ (उगान्) add a न् in their strong cases (VII. 1. 70), and form their feminine with unaccented ई ॥ शतु is an affix having an indicatory ऋ, therefore its substitute would also be considered as having an indicatory ऋ, the उ of वसु therefore is not absolutely necessary for the purposes of उगान् operations. वसु is so written, in order that in the sūtra वसो संप्रसारणं (VI. 4. 131.), both कुसु and वसु should be included. Nor can we object that in the above mentioned sūtra, वसु with one indicatory letter being taken, cannot include an affix like कुसु having two indicatory letters,—on the maxim एकातुबन्धकमहणे न धातुबन्धकस्य—for if that were so, there was no necessity of उ in वसु ॥ Some read the anuvṛtti of the word optionally into this: and we have विद्वत्, विदन्तो, विदन्तः formed with शतु (see V. 4. 38).

समासे अनजपूर्वे क्रो ल्यप् ॥ ३७ ॥ पदानि ॥ समासे, अनज, पूर्वे, क्रः ल्यप् ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ समासे अनजपूर्वे क्त्वा इत्येतस्य त्यवित्ययमादिशो भवति ॥

37. In a compound, the first member of which is an Indeclinable but not नज्; ल्यप् is substituted for क्ता ॥

Thus प्रकृत्य, प्रहृत्य ॥ The tvā is added by III. 4. 21, the compounding is by II. 2. 18, and तुक् by VI. 1. 71. पार्श्वतःकृत्य, The tvā is added by III. 4. 61. and compounding is by II. 2. 22. नानाकृत्य; द्विधाकृत्य The tvā is added by III. 4. 62. Why do we say 'in a compound'? Observe कृत्वा हत्वा. Here the counter exam-

BK. VII. CH. I §. 38 ]

ल्य् SUBSTITUTION.

1331

ple is हृद्या, which is preceded by an Indeclinable कृद्या, but as it is not compounded, there is no substitution. Why do we say 'not preceded by नञ्'? Observe आकृत्या, आहृत्या, परमकृत्या, उत्तमकृत्या ॥ The word अनञ् means 'other than नञ्', and means words of the same class as नञ्, i. e. Indeclinables : and does not mean words which are not Indeclinables. The compounds like स्नात्वाकालक contained in the class of मयूरव्यंसक &c (II. 1. 72.), do not take ल्यप् anomalously. Or the word समासे is in the Locative with the force of specification : and means those compounds which are specifically formed with क्ता and not any compound in general.

Now by the rule I. 1. 72, ktvā would denote a form ending with ktvā; and would include the case of a compound ending in ktvā. But this general rule is modified by the maxim प्रत्यय महणे यस्मात् स विहित स्तवदस्त्वन्तस्य महणम् 'an affix denotes, whenever it is employed in grammar, a word-form which begins with that to which that affix has been added and ends with the affix itself.' But the affix ktvā is never ordained after a compound. Therefore, the case of compounds ending in ktvā, would not be covered by the mere employment of ktvā. Then comes the maxim कृद महणे गति कारक पूर्वस्यापि महणे 'a krit affix denotes whenever it is employed in grammar, a word-form which begins with that to which that krit affix has been added and which ends with the krit affix, but moreover should a gati, or a noun such as denotes a case-relation have been prefixed to that word-form, then the krit affix must denote the same word-form together with the gati or the noun which may have been prefixed to it.' By this a compound also may end in ktvā. This maxim will cover cases like प्रकृत्या, पार्श्वतः कृत्या but not उष्ठः कृत्या &c because उष्ठः is neither a gati nor a kāraka. Hence the employment of the word समासे in the sūtra, and also of the word अनञ्पूर्वे, for नञ् is neither a Gati nor a Kāraka.

In the case of प्रधाय and प्रस्थाय this maxim applies :—अन्तरङ्गमपि विधीत् बहिरङ्गो ल्यप् बाधते 'a Bahiranga substitution of ल्यप् supersedes even antaranga rule'. What are these antaranga rules superseded by the substitute ल्यप्? (1) हिल्—the substitution of हि for धा (VII. 4. 42). Thus हिल्वा but प्रधाय and not प्रहिल्वा ॥ (2) इदं—the substitution of इद for वै (VII. 4. 46)—as इद्वा, but प्रधाय and not प्रहिल्वा ॥ (3) आर्त्त्वं as required by VI. 4. 42 : as खाद्वा, प्रधाय and प्रहिल्वा ॥ (4) इदं—as स्थित्वा but प्रस्थाय ॥ (5) इदं by VI. 4. 66, as पीत्वा but प्रधाय ॥ (6) दीर्घत्वं by VI. 4. 15, as शान्त्वा but प्रधाय ॥ (7) इदं by VI. 4. 19, as पृष्ट्वा but आपृष्ट्वा ॥ (8) कद—as शून्वा ॥ (9) इद (VII. 2. 56)—देवित्वा but प्रधीय ॥

कृापि छन्दसि ॥ ३५ ॥ पदानि ॥ कृा, अपि, छन्दसि ॥
वृत्तिः ॥ समासे उनमुपूर्वे क्त्वा इतेतस्य क्त्वा इत्यमादेशो भवति अविश्वान्त्यवपि भवति छन्दसि विधेये ॥

38. In the Veda the क्त्वा also, as well as ल्यप्, is substituted for त्क्वा, after an Indeclinable compound, other than one preceded by the Negative तञ् ॥

3

1332

VEDIC CASE-AFFIXES

[ Bk. VII. Ch. I. §. 39

Thus कृष्णं वासो यजमानं परिभाषित्वा, प्रत्यञ्चर्मकं प्रत्यर्थित्वा ॥ So also we have
स्वप्न, as उद्भूतं जुहोति ॥ The sutra could have been made shorter by saying
merely या छन्दसि; not doing so indicates that conditions and limitations are
set aside in the Vedas in applying this affix. Therefore स्वप्न is applied even
when there is no compound, as, अर्च्य तान् देवान् गतः ॥ The word छन्दसि governs
the following sutras upto VII. I. 50, inclusive.

सुपां सुलुकपूर्वसवर्णाच्छेयाडाञ्चायाजालः ॥ ३६ ॥ पदानि ॥ सुपाम्, सु, लुक,
पूर्वसवर्ण, आ, आत, रो, या, डा, इया, याच्, आलः ॥
वृत्तिः ॥ छन्दसि विषये सुपां स्थाने सु लुक पूर्वसवर्ण आ आत रो या डाञ्चा याच् आल इत्येति अधिशा
भवन्ति ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ सुपां सुपो भवन्ति इति पक्तव्यम् ॥ वार्तिकम् ॥ तिङां तिङो भवन्तीति वक्तव्यम् ॥
वार्तिकम् ॥ इयाडियाजोकाराणासुपसंख्यानम् ॥ वार्तिकम् ॥ आङ्याजयारासुपसंख्यानम् ॥

39. The following irregular endings are substituted for the various case endings in the Veda: (1) स of the Nom. Sg. for अस of the Plural, (2) the *luk*-elision of the case-endings, (3) the single substitution of the homogeneous long vowel for the end vowel of the stem, (4) आ, (5) आत, (6) ए (रो) for the ending of the Nom. Plural, (7) या, (8) आ (डा), with the elision of the last vowel and the consonant, if any, that follows it in the stem, (9) या (ड्या) with the similar shortening of the stem (10) यौ (याच्) and आ (accent of ल) ॥

Thus (1) अनुशरा ऋजवः सन्तु पन्थाः (for पन्थानः) Rig Veda X. 85. 23.

*Vårt*:—It should be stated that case-endings replace case-endings promiscuously, as, धुरि दक्षिणायाः (for दक्षिणायाम् Rig I. 164. 9).

*Vårt*:—One personal ending replaces another personal ending in the Vedas चपाले ये अभ्युपाय तक्षति (for तक्षन्ति) Rig I. 162. 6.

(2) लुक-elsion:—As आङ् चर्मन्, लोहिते चर्मन् for चर्मणि; हविर्धाने यत् सुन्वन्ति, तत् समिधेनोरन्वाह (यद् for यस्मिन् and तद् for तस्मिन्) ॥

(3) Lengthening:—धीती, मती, सुदुती for धीता, मत्वा and सुदुता ॥

(4) आ—उभा यन्तारी (for उभौ) ॥

(5) आत—न ताद् ब्राह्मणाद् निन्वामि for तान् ब्राह्मणान् ॥

(6) रो—न युष्मे (for युष्म) वाजबन्धवः, Rig VIII. 68. 19. अम्मे (for वयं) इन्द्राह-हस्पती; Rig IV. 49. 4, the युष्म and वयं substitution has not taken place as a Vedic usage.

(7) या—उरुया, धृष्णुया for उरुणा and धृष्णुणा ॥

(8) डा—नामा (for नामी) पृथिव्याः Rig I. 143. 4.

(9) ड्या—अनुष्ठ्या च्यावयतात् for अनुष्ठ्या Ait Br. II. 6. 15.

(10) याच्—साधुर्या for साधु, there was required the elision of सु ॥

BK. VII. CH. I. §. 43 ]

VEDIC SUBSTITUTIONS.

1333

(II) आल्—वसन्ता यजेत for वसन्ते ॥

Vårt:—The following substitutes should also be enumerated, (a) इया, (b) द्वियाच् with elision of the final vowel and the consonant, if any, that follows it, and (c) long ई ॥ As (a) उर्विया परिधानम्, for उरूणा, so also वार्विया for वारूणा ॥ (b) सुसेविया for सुसेविणा, and सुगाविया for सुगाविणा ॥ (c) इति न सुष्के सरसी शयानम् for सरसि ॥

Vårt:—So also (a) आह्, (b) अयाच् and (c) अयात्: as प्रवाहवा for प्रवाहना, (b) स्वमर्था सच सेवनम् for स्वमेन, (c) सिन्धुमिव नार्विया for नावा ॥

The word आच्छे in the sutra is compounded of three words आ + आत् + शे, the word आत् = आ + आत् ॥

अमो मश् ॥ ४० ॥ पदानि ॥ अमः, मश् ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अम् इति मिवादेशो गृह्यते । तस्य छन्दसि विषये मशादेशो भवति ॥

40. For the Personal ending अम of the First Person Singular (in the Aorist) म (I. 1. 55) is substituted in the Veda.

The अम here is the substitution of मिष्, and not the accusative singular affix. As वर्धा वृत्रम् (for अवधिषम्) Rig I. 165. 8: क्रमिम् वृक्षस्य शाखाम् ॥ The अद् augment is diversely elided (VI. 4. 75). The indicatory श् of मश् shows that the whole of the affix अम is to be replaced. The substitution of म् for म् is to prevent the change of म् into anusvāra as in VIII. 3. 25.

लोपस्त आत्मनेपदेषु ॥ ४१ ॥ पदानि ॥ लोपः, त, आत्मनेपदेषु ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ आत्मनेपदेषु यस्तकारस्तस्य छन्दसि विषये लोपो भवति ॥

41. In the Veda the त of the Atmanepada Personal ending is elided.

As देवा अदुह् and गन्धर्वा अप्सरसी अदुह् for अदुह् (see VII. 1. 8); दुहाम् (for दुधाम्) अभिध्यां पयो अप्स्येवम् ॥ Rig I. 164. 27. दक्षिणतः शये for शते ॥ Owing to the anuvritti of अपि from VII. 1. 38, this substitution sometimes does not take place; as: आत्मानमनुतंकुरते ॥ Why in the Atmanepada? Observe वत्सं दुहन्ति कलशं चतुर्विलम् ॥

ध्वमो ध्वात् ॥ ४२ ॥ पदानि ॥ ध्वमः, ध्वात् ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ छन्दसि विषये ध्वमो ध्वादिव्ययमादेशो भवति ॥

42. In the Veda, ध्वात् is substituted for the Personal ending ध्वम् ॥

As अन्तर्वोध्यानं वारयध्वात् for वारयध्वम् ॥ Ait Br. II. 6. 14.

यजध्वैनमिति च ॥ ४३ ॥ पदानि ॥ यजध्वैनम्, इति, च ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ यजध्वमित्येतस्य एनमित्येतस्मिन्परतो मकारलोपो निपात्यते वकारस्य च यकार+छन्दसि विषये ॥

43. यजध्वैनम् is irregularly formed in the Veda for

यजध्वमेनम् ॥

The word यजध्वम् followed by एनम् loses its final म् in the Veda. As यजध्वैनं त्रियमेधाः (Rig VIII. 2. 37). The Kasika adds “that म् is also irregularly

VEDIC SUBSTITUTES

[ Bk. VII. Ch. I. §. 48.

changed into य' : the form would then be यजध्वेनम् ॥ This is, however, a mistake as pointed out by Bhattoji Dikshit.

तस्य तात् ॥ ४४ ॥ पदानि ॥ तस्य, तात् ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ तश्चत्वं लोभ्यभ्युपरुषबहुवचनस्य स्थानं तादित्ययमादिशो भवति ॥

44. For the ending त of the 2nd Pers. Pl. Imperative is substituted तात् in the Veda.

As गानं गानमस्या नूनं कृणुतात् (for कृणुत), and ऊवध्यं गोहं पार्थिवं खनतात् (for खनत) Ait Br. II. 6. 15, 16. अस्मारत संज्ञातात् (= संज्ञात), सूर्यं चक्षुर्गमयतात् (= गमयत).

तत्पन्ननयनाश्च ॥ ४५ ॥ पदानि ॥ तप्, तनप्, तन, थनाः, च ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ तस्येति वच्यते । छन्दसि विषये तस्य स्थानं तप् तनप् तन थन इत्येति आविशा भवन्ति ॥

45. Also त् and तन (before both, on account of the indicatory प् the preceding vowel of the verbal stem is strengthened, or if weak not shortened), तन and थन are substituted for the त of the 2nd Pers. Pl. Imperative in the Veda.

This श्रुतोत प्रावाणः (for श्रुत), श्रुतोत्त (= श्रुत), संवरजा दधातन (for धत्त), श्रुत-हन (for श्रुत) the ślu vikaraṇa being added as a Vedic irregularity ; यदिष्टन for यदिष्टत ॥ The indicatory प् makes तप् and तनप् non-डित् affixes (I. 2. 4).

इदन्तो मसि ॥ ४७ ॥ पदानि ॥ इदन्तः, मसि ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ छन्दसि विषये मसि यद्यं शब्द इकारान्तो भवति । मसः सकारान्तस्य इकारागमो भवति स च तस्यान्तो भवति ॥

46. The Personal ending मस् becomes in the Veda मसि ending with an इ ॥

Thus पुनस्त्वां दीपयामसि (for दीपयामः) शलंभं भञ्जयामसि (for भञ्जयामः), त्वयि रात्रि वासयामसि for वासयामः ॥

कोयक् ॥ ४८ ॥ पदानि ॥ कः, यक् ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ त्वा इत्येतस्य यगागमो भवति छन्दसि विषये ॥

47. In the Veda, the Absolutive affix क्वा gets at the end, the augment य ॥

Thus इत्याय सविता धियः (for इत्वा). This sūtra is not read immediately after VII. 1. 38, as in that sūtra, the anuvṛtti of samāsa is understood, while there is no such anuvṛtti here.

इष्टीनमिति च ॥ ४९ ॥ पदानि ॥ इष्टीनम्, इति, च ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ इष्टीनमित्यय शब्दो निपात्यते छन्दसि विषये । यजेः क्त्वाप्रत्ययान्तस्य ईनमादिशोन्त्यस्य निपात्यते ॥ वात्तिकम् ॥ पीत्वीनमित्यपीप्यते ॥

48. In the Veda, the Absolutive इष्टीनम् is irregularly formed for इष्टा ॥

To the root यज् is added क्वा, and the final आ is replaced by ईनम् ॥ As इष्टीनम् देवान् for इष्टा देवान् ॥ The च in the sūtra indicates that there are other forms like this, as पीत्वानम् for पीत्वा ॥

VEDIC SUBSTITUTIONS.

सात्व्यदध्यश्च ॥ ५६ ॥ पदानि ॥ सात्वी-आदयः, च ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ स्नात्वी इत्येवमादयः शब्दा निपात्यन्ते छन्दसि विधये ॥

49. स्नात्वी &c. are irregularly formed in the Veda.

Thus सात्वी मतादिव, for सात्वा; पीत्वी सोमस्य बाधुं for पीत्वा ॥ The word आदि 'et cetera' means 'of the form of', namely words having form like सात्वी, as पीत्वी &c.

आज्ञसेरसुक् ॥ ५० ॥ पदानि ॥ आत्, जसे; असुक् ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अवर्णान्तादङ्गादुत्तरस्य जसेरसुगागो भवति छन्दसि विधये ॥

50. After a stem ending in अ or आ, the affix अस् of the Nom. Pl. gets, in the Veda, the augment अस् (असुक्) at the end.

Thus ब्राह्मणासः पितरः सोम्यासः for ब्राह्मणाः and सोम्याः ॥ Rig VI. 75. 10. ये पूर्वासो य उपरासः (Rig X. 15. 2) for पूर्वे and उपरे ॥ So also पुतासः (R. I. 3. 4) Why is not, after the adding of the augment असुक्, the अस् changed to शी in the last example, as required by VII. I. 17, and on the maxim पुनः प्रसङ्गः विज्ञानात्? No, the maxim that applies here is सङ्कट् गतौ विप्रतिषेधे यद्वाधितं, तद्वाधितमेव ॥

अद्वक्षीरद्वपलवणानामात्मप्रीतौ क्यचि ॥ ५१ ॥ अद्व. क्षीर, द्वप, लवणानाम्, आत्मा प्रीतौ, क्यचि ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ छन्दसीत्यतः प्रवृत्ति निवृत्तम् । अद्व क्षीर द्वप लवण इत्येतेषामङ्गानामात्मप्रीतिविधये क्यचि परतो ऽसुगागो भवति ॥

वात्तिकम् ॥ अश्वद्वपयोर्मैयुनच्छायामिति वक्तव्यम् ॥ वा० ॥ क्षीरलवणयोर्ललसायामिति वक्तव्यम् ॥

वा० ॥ सर्वप्रीतिपरिकेश्यो लालासायामसुवक्तव्यः ॥ वा० ॥ सुवक्तव्यः ॥

51. The same augment असुक् is added after the words अश्व, क्षीर, द्वप and लवण before the Denominative affix क्यच्, when the delight of the subject in these things is to be expressed.

The anuvritti of छन्दसि does not extend to this sutra or any further. Thus अश्वस्यति वदवा, क्षीरस्यति माणवकः, द्वपस्यति गौः, लवणस्यशुद्धः ॥ अश्व+अस्+य+ति= अश्वस्यति (VI. I. 97). Why 'when the delight of the subject is meant'? Observe अश्वीयति, क्षीरियति, द्वपीयति and लवणीयति ॥

*Vårt* :—After अश्व and द्वप, the force of the augment is that of desiring sexual connection. *Vårt* :—After क्षीर and लवण it has the force of ardently wishing for, i. e. an intense thirsting after the thing. The augment is not added, though the sense may be that of delight, if it has not the above meanings. Others say *Vårt* :—असुक् should be added after every nominal stem when the sense is that of intense yearning after that thing : as द्रव्यस्यति, मध्यस्यति &c. Others say *Vårt* :—That the augment सुक् should be added, as द्रव्यस्यति, मधुस्यति &c.

आमि सर्वनाश्रः सुत् ॥ ५२ ॥ पदानि ॥ आमि, सर्वनाश्रः, सुत् ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ आदिति वत्तेते अवर्णात्सर्वनाश्र उत्तरस्यामः सुत्वागो भवति ॥

दूर AUGMENT.

[ Bk. VII. Ch. I. §. 55

52. After a Pronominal stem ending in अ or आ, the affix आम of the Genitive Plural gets the augment स at the beginning.

The word आम of the last sūtra is understood here. Thus सर्वेषाम्, विश्वेषाम्, येषाम्, तेषाम्, सर्वेषाम्, यासाम्, तासाम् ॥ But भवताम् of भवत् ॥ The आम of the sūtra is the Genitive Plural ending आम, and not the आम of the Locative Singular ordained by VII. 3. 116; for that आम takes the augments याद, आद or स्याद (VII. 3. 112-114), while the present आम takes सुद or सुद ॥ Nor the आम of the Perfect Tense (III. I. 35 &c), because that refers to verb and Sarva-nāma nor the आम of V. 4. 11, for the same reason. The word आमि is exhibited in the sūtra in the locative case, for the sake of the subsequent sūtra VII. 1. 53. For the purposes of the present sūtra, it should be construed, as if it was in the Genitive case (आमः सर्वेषाम् सुद), because सर्वेषाम् being in the Ablative case, the augment सुद will be added at the beginning of the affix following it, on the maxim तस्मादित्युत्तरस्य ॥

त्रैषयः ॥ ५३ ॥ पदानि ॥ त्रैः, त्रयः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ त्रिद्वैतस्य आमि परे चय इत्ययमादिशो भवति ॥

53. त्रय is substituted for त्रि before the Genitive Pl. affix.

As त्रयाणाम् ॥ त्रीणाम् however appears in the Veda: as त्रीणामपि समुद्राणाम् ॥

56. In the Veda after the words श्री and ग्रामणी, the Gen. Pl. आम gets the augment न् ॥

As श्रीणामुदारो धरणो रथीणाम्, अन्यत्र सुतग्रामणीनाम् ॥ This sūtra could be well dispensed with: by I. 4. 5. श्री is optionally a Nadi in the Genitive plural. We make the option of that sūtra a vyavasthita-vibhāshā, by saying श्री is *always* Nadi in the Veda, and *optionally* every where else. As regards सुतग्रामणीनाम्, we have सुतग्रामणीनाम् = सुतग्रामणि, the Genitive Pl. of which by VII. I. 54 will be सुतग्रामणीनाम् ॥

The necessity of this sūtra will, however, arise if the compound be सुतग्रामणीनाम् ते ग्रामण्यम् सुतग्रामण्यः ॥

58. न् is added after the vowel of the root, in a root which has an indicatory इ in the Dhātupātha.

Thus from कुडि—कुण्डितु, कुण्डितुम्, कुण्डितव्यम्; from हुडि—हुण्डितु, हुण्डितुम्, हुण्डितव्यम् &c. But पचति, पठति where इ is not इत् ॥ The न् is added to the root from its very inception, and they must be considered to have got a न्, for the purposes of the application of the grammatical rules. Thus III. 3. 103 says that आ is added in the feminine to a root which ends in a consonant and has a prosodially long vowel. The root कुडि must be considered to be such a root and कुण्डा, हुण्डा are thus formed. Similarly though the roots in the Dhātupātha are धिवि and कृवि, in applying affixes we must consider them as धिन्व् and कृन्, as the author himself has indicated in III. 1. 80. In short, in adding affixes, these roots should be considered as having a न् ॥ Moreover the *root* (*dhātu*) should have इ, and not the *stem* (*aṅga*). The affixes तासि (Future) and सिन्व् (Aorist) when added to roots, will not make those roots

इदिन्; for the इ in नासि and सिच् is merely for the sake of pronunciation, and is not to be considered as इन् in the strict sense of the word: in fact it should be considered as non-nasalised. If you say that “the इ in सिच् should be considered as इन्, for because of its being इन्, the न् of मन् is not elided by VI. 4. 24 in अमस्सा”, we reply, “not so, the न् is not elided, because sutra इन्: सिच् I. 2. 14 makes सिच् a किन् after इन् only, the result of which is that इन् only loses its न् by VI. 4. 37, and no other root”. In मन्सा = मन् + नासि + डा = मन् + न् + आ (the आस् is elided VI. 4. 143). For the purposes of the elision of न्, the elided आस् would be considered as asiddha (VI. 4. 22), for both VI. 4. 143, and VI. 4. 37, requiring the elision of न् are abhiya sutras. In मन्सा, छेन्सा from भिदिर् and छिदिर् the whole combination इन् is इन्, and not इ and न् separately, and hence न् is not added. But even if these roots be considered as इदिन्, the syllable इन् having an इ, yet they will not get the न् augment, because the word अन्त of पादान्ते (VII. 1. 57) is understood here in this sutra also, so that the roots must have a final इ as इन् for the application of this rule.

59. In मुच् &c, before the characteristic श of the Tudādi class, the न् is placed after the vowel of the root.

Thus मुच्—मुच्यति, तुम्पति, बिन्दति, लिप्पति, सिञ्चति, कृन्ताति, खिन्दति, पियाति ॥
Why “before श”? Observe मोक्ता, मोक्तुम्, मोक्तव्यम् ॥ Why “of मुच् &c”? Observe तुरति, तुरति ॥

Vārt:—The तुम्फ &c should be also enumerated. These are the following roots of Tudādi class: 24. तप (तुफ), 25. तुम्फ नमो, 26. तप तुम्प, 27. तुफ तुम्फ, हिंसायाम्, 28. इफ (इप), 29. इम्फ उन्क्लेशे, 30. क्फ (रिफ), क्फ (रिम्फ), हिंसायाम्, 31. युफ, युम्फ मन्थे, 32. उम उन्क पूरणे, 33. युम्, युम्म शोभाये ॥ Of these, those which have a nasal, lose it by VI. 4. 24, and then get the न् augment by the present rule, which being specifically ordained, cannot be again dropped. Thus तुम्फति, तुम्पति, तुम्पति, इम्फति &c. Those which have no nasal, are conjugated as तुफति, तुफति, इफति, युफति, उमति and युमति ॥

62. The augment तुम is not added to रध्, before an affix beginning with the augment इद्, except in the Perfect.

As रधिता, रधितुम्, रधितव्यम्, but रन्धनम्, रन्धकः before Anit affixes, and रन्धिव, रन्धिन in the Perfect. When तुम् is added रन्ध becomes a root ending in a conjunct consonant, and therefore the लिट् affixes after it are not किन् (असंयोगात् लिट् किन् I. 2. 5), and therefore the न् is not elided by VI. 4. 24. But when the affix क्त्वम् of the Perfect is added, we have रधिवम् Nom. Sg. रधिवान् ॥ Here the affix being expressly taught with an indicatory क् the न् is elided. The reduplicate is elided, the अ changed into ए, then इद् is added, then तुम्, and then the तुम् is elided by the expressly taught किन् ॥

Why was not the sūtra made as इदि लिटि रधेः when by so doing, the augment तुम् would have been added only in the Perfect when it had इद् and no where else? This form of sūtra would have also meant that तुम् would be added in that Perfect which took इद् and in no other Perfect, while cases other than Perfect might take it. That being so, there would be no तुम् in रन्ध, while रधिता would require तुम् ॥ See, however, the Mahabhāṣya for the contra.

65. The augment तुम् is added to लम् preceded by आ, before an affix beginning with य ॥

As आलम्, गौः ॥ The तुम् is added before the addition of the affix, and by so doing लम् becomes लम् and thus loses its character of having a penultimate आ, and therefore by III. 1. 124, we shall have ण्यत् affix, and not यत् affix by III. 1. 98. Had the तुम् been added after the addition of the affix, then यत् would be added by III. 1. 98. Though in both cases the form will be आलम्, the difference will be in the accent: यत् would throw the acute on the first syllable (यतोऽनावः) while the word has svarita on the final; thus instead of आलम् (by VI. 1. 213 and VI. 2. 139), which यत् gives, we have आलम् (तित् svar).

Why do we say 'when preceded by आ'? Observe लम् ॥ How do you explain अभिदोन आलम्? All rules are optionally applied in the Vedas. Or आलम् may be explained by saying that the तुम् having been added, is again dropped.

68. The augment तुम् is not added to लम् before खल् and घम् when सु or दुः alone (without another Preposition along with them) precede the root.

Thus सुलम्भम्, दुर्लम्भम्, सुलामो, दुर्लम्भः ॥ But सुपलम्भः, दुधलम्भः ॥ The word केवल is used in the sūtra because सुदुर्ध्यां is in the Instrumental case and not in the Ablative. Had it been in the Ablative, there would have been no necessity of using the word केवल, for the rule would not have applied, when a preposition intervened between these and the root. In अतिसुलम्भम्, the word अति is not an Upasarga but a Karmapravachaniya; when अति is used as an Upasarga, we have अतिसुलम्भः ॥ If the words सुदुर्ध्यां be construed as Ablative, then also the use of केवल is for a purpose similar to that as above.

Thus अलाभि or अलम्भि, लम्बलाभम् or लम्बलम्भम् ॥ This is a Vyavasthitavibhāshā, the option is allowed where there is no Preposition along with the root; and no option is allowed but तुम् must be added, when a Preposition precedes: as प्रालम्भि, प्रलम्भम् ॥

उगिद्वां सर्वनामस्थाने ध्यातोः ॥ ७० ॥ पदानि ॥ उगित्, अ चाम्, सर्वनामस्थाने, अ धातोः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ उगितामङ्गानां धातुवर्जितानामञ्चतेभ सर्वनामस्थाने परतो तुमागमो भवति ॥

70. Whatever has an indicatory उ, ऋ and ऋ, (with the exception of a root), and the stem अच्, (अञ्चति) get the augment तुम् in the strong cases.

Thus भवतु has an indicatory उ, formed by the Uṇādi affix उवतु, and it is declined as भवान्, भवन्ती, भवन्तः ॥ Similarly ईषतु—प्रेयान्, प्रेयांसी, प्रेयांसः; शतु—पञ्चन्, पञ्चन्ती, पञ्चन्तः ॥ अञ्च—प्राङ्, प्राञ्ची, प्राञ्चः ॥

Why do we say 'having an indicatory उक् vowel or the stem अच्'? Observe दृषन्, दृषदी, दृषदः ॥

1342

तुम् AUGMENT.

[ Bk. VII. Ch. I §. 73.

Why do we say in strong cases? Observe भवतः पञ्च, श्रेयः पञ्च ॥ अञ्च् root is mentioned for the sake of niyama, i. e. of the roots, only अञ्च् gets तुम् and no other root. Therefore दखासत्, पर्णप्यन् formed from the roots संहु and प्वहु having indicatory द ॥ (See III. 2. 76, IV. 1. 6, VIII. 2. 72). For the lengthening in भवात् &c, see VI. 4. 10, 14: the च् is elided in प्राह् by VIII. 2. 23, and न् becomes ह् by VIII. 2. 62: and न् in सत् by VIII. 2. 72.

Why do we say 'with the exception of a root' when by the mere fact of including *one* root अच् all other roots would have been excluded from the scope of this sūtra? The specific mention of अधातोः shows that the prohibition applies to *original* roots, and not to those roots which are *derived* from nouns. Thus गोमन्तमिच्छति = गोमत्यति formed by क्वच् ॥ Here गोमत्य is a derivative root, in its primitive state it was a noun. The prohibition of अधातोः will not apply to this root and तुम् will be added. Thus गोमत्य + क्रिप् = गोमत्य + ० (the अ is dropped by VI. 4. 48) = गोमत् + ० (the स् is elided by VI. 4. 50). Now is added तुम् and we have गोमात् ॥

युजेरसमासे ॥ ७१ ॥ पदानि ॥ युजेः, अ समासे ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ युजेरसमासे सर्वनामस्थाने परतो तुमागमो भवति ॥

71. The nominal stem युज् gets before the strong cases the augment न्, when it does not stand in a compound.

Thus युज् (VIII. 2. 23, 62) युज्जी, युज्जः; but अश्वयुक्, अश्वयुज्जी, अश्वयुजः in a compound. The root युज समाधौ (Divādi 68) is not to be taken here; therefore not here युजमापन्ना कषयः ॥ But युजिर् योगे (Rudhādi 7) is to be taken.

नपुंसकस्य झलचः ॥ ७२ ॥ पदानि ॥ नपुंसकस्य, झल, अचः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ नपुंसकस्य झलन्तस्याजन्तस्य च सर्वनामस्थाने परतो तुमागमो भवति ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ बहुजि प्रतिषेधो वक्तव्यः ॥ वा० ॥ अन्त्यार्पुर्व तुममेकइच्छन्ति ॥

72. The augment तुम् is added in the strong cases to a Neuter stem ending in a consonant (other than a nasal or a semivowel), or ending in a vowel.

Thus दवश्चिन्ति, शकुन्ति (VI. 4. 10) यथांसि, पर्यांसि; कुण्डानि, वनानि (VI. 4. 8), चपूर्णि, ज्वलनि ॥ Why 'of a Neuter'? Observe अग्निचिद् ब्राह्मणः ॥ Why do we say 'not ending in a semivowel or a nasal'? Observe बहुपुरि, बहुपुरि, विमलविधि, चत्वारि, अज्ञानि (VII. 1. 98). A neuter having an indicatory एक vowel gets तुम् by this sūtra and not by VII. 1. 70, as that is superseded by this, this being the subsequent. As श्रेयांसि, भूयांसि कुर्वन्ति कृपन्ति ब्राह्मणकुलानि ॥

*Vārt* :—Prohibition should be stated with regard to बहुजि; as बहुजि ब्राह्मणकुलानि ॥ Some would have न् added between र् and ज् of this word, as बहुजि ब्राह्मणकुलानि ॥ See I. 4. 13.

इको अचि विमक्तौ ॥ ७३ ॥ पदानि ॥ इक्ः, अचि, विमक्तौ ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ इगन्तस्य नपुंसकस्याज्ञस्याज्ञादि विमक्तौ तुमागमो भवति ॥

BK. VII. CH. I. §. 73 ]

तुम् AUGMENT.

1343

Kārikā—इकोचि व्यञ्जने मा भुइस्तु लोपः स्वरः कथम् ।
स्वरो वै भूयमाणो पि लुप्ते किं न भविष्यति ॥
रायालं तिसुभावश्च व्यवधानानुमा आपि ।
तुङ् वाच्य उत्तरार्धे तु इह किं चित्रपो इति ॥

73. The augment तुम् is added to a Neuter-stem ending in a simple vowel, except अ, before a case-affix beginning with a vowel.

Thus बपुणी, जतुनी, तुम्बुरुणी, बपुणे, जतुने, तुम्बुरुणे ॥ Why “with the exception of अ”? Observe कुण्डे, पीठे ॥ The phrase “before an affix beginning with a vowel” is employed here for the sake of the subsequent sūtras like VII. 1. 75. Here we could have dispensed with it: for before affixes beginning with a consonant, तुम् would be elided by VIII. 2. 7. The only object that it serves here is that we can form हे बपो! or हे बपु! in the Vocative singular. For had we बपु+स in the vocative, the form would have been हे बपु+ like हे राजन्, for न् would not be elided here, see VIII. 2. 8.

If it be objected that by the sūtra न लुमताङ्गस्य (I. 1. 63) when the affix स् is elided in the Vocative, it will leave no trace behind, and there being no affix at all, तुम् will not be added in the Vocative. We reply: that this very employment of the word अच् in this sūtra indicates (jñāpaka) that the rule prohibiting the effect of an affix (I. 1. 63) does not apply here. Therefore, though the affix is elided, it produces its effect in spite of I. 1. 63, and we have the gūṇa of the vowel in the Vocative, as हे बपो by VII. 3. 108.

Why have we used the word विमलौ ‘when a case-affix follows’? Observe तुम्बुरं चूर्णम्, where the taddhita affix अच् is added to तुम्बुरु by IV. 3. 139.

Kārikā :—The employment of the words इक्: आचि in the sūtra shows that तुम् will not come when the affix begins with a consonant, as बपुभ्यां, बपुनि: ॥ An objector says, the employment of आचि in the sūtra is useless for तुम् may be added even before an affix beginning with a consonant, for having added it, it will be elided by न लोपःप्रतिपदिकान्तस्य (VIII. 2. 7). We reply, yes it can be so done, but how will you then manage the accent? For in पँञ्चबपुभ्यां, पँञ्चबपुनिः, the accent is regulated by the rule VI. 2. 29 which says that in a Dvigu compound, the first member preserves its original accent if the second member ends in an इक् vowel. But if there was a तुम्, then the second member would not end in इक् but in न्: and the elision of this न् by VII. 2. 7. is asiddha for the purposes of accent. To this the objector answers, that even where न् is not elided the accent is governed by VI. 2. 29, namely the accent of पँञ्चबपुणे or पञ्चबपुणः is by VI. 2. 29, why should it not be so when न् is elided. So the objection about accent has no strength.

1344

बुद्ध AUGMENT.

[ Bk. VII. Ch. I. §. 74.

Well if बुद्ध be added even before consonant-affix, then there will arise this anomaly: अतिरि+भ्यां=अतिरिन्+भ्यां (by adding बुद्ध). Here rule VII. 2. 85 cannot apply: because न् intervenes between रि and भ्यां, therefore इ of रि is not changed to आ, and therefore we cannot get the proper from अतिराभ्यां ॥ Moreover in प्रियात्रि+भ्यां, the त्रि cannot be changed to तिस् if there be बुद्ध, and so we cannot get the form प्रियतिसुभ्यां ब्राह्मणकुलानि ॥

To this it is answered, the change of इ into आ in the case of रि, and the substitution of तिस् for त्रि will take place even when the बुद्ध intervenes, on the maxim विभक्तिविधानवशायां यदनन्तये तत् तत्राश्रीयते न त्वविधविधानवशायाम् ॥ And this is done in this way: अतिरि+भ्यां, and प्रियात्रि+भ्यां, here बुद्ध is superseded by the subsequent rule requiring आ and तिस् respectively.

If this be so, then the employment of अच् in the sūtra is for the sake of the supersession of बुद्ध by बुद्ध (VII. 1. 54). Thus बुद्ध has unrestricted scope in अग्नीनां, वायूनां, and बुद्ध has unrestricted scope in चपुणे and जतुने ॥ But in चपूर्णाम् and जतूनाम्, both बुद्ध and बुद्ध present themselves. Here however बुद्ध is superseded by बुद्ध by purva-vipratishedha and so there is lengthening of the vowel by VI. 4. 3. This supersession is indicated by the employment of अच्, for बुद्ध and बुद्ध being both *anitya* and of equal force, had there been no अच्, बुद्ध would have come and not बुद्ध ॥

But this is also not valid, for बुद्ध would have to be added, even if there had been no अच् in the sūtra.

The employment of अच् is for the sake of the subsequent sūtra VII. 1. 75. The only object that अच् serves in this sūtra, is in forming the vocative हे चपो as shown above.

तृतीयादिषु आपितपुंस्कं पुंववृगालवस्य ॥ ७४ ॥ पदानि ॥ तृतीयादिषु, आपितपुंस्कम्, पुंववृगालवस्य ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ तृतीयादिषु विभक्तिविश्वाविषु आपितपुंस्कं पुंस्कं पुंववृगालवस्याचार्यस्य मतेन पुंववृगालवस्याचार्यस्य मतेन पुंववृगालवस्याचार्यस्य मतेन पुंववृगालवस्याचार्यस्य मतेन पुंववृगालवस्याचार्यस्य मतेन पुंववृगालवस्याचार्यस्य मतेन पुंववृगालवस्याचार्यस्य मतेन पुंववृगालवस्याचार्यस्य

74. A neuter stem ending in a vowel, except अ, of which there exists an equivalent, uniform masculine, is treated like the masculine, in the opinion of Gálava, before the vowel beginning affixes of the Instrumental and the cases that follow it.

As in the Masculine there is no shortening, nor the addition of बुद्ध, so here also. As आमणी is the equivalent, uniform masculine of the neuter form आमणि, we have either Ins. आमणिना or आमण्या ब्राह्मणकुलेन, the Ins. Sg. of आमणि n. Similarly Dat. आमणिने or आमण्ये ब्राह्मणकुलाय; Abl. आमणिनो or आमण्यो ब्राह्मणकुलात्, Gen. Sg. आमणिनो or आमण्यो ब्राह्मणकुलस्य, Gen. Du. आमणिनो ब्राह्मणकुलयोः or आमण्योः; Gen. Pl. आमणीनां or आमण्यां ब्राह्मणकुलानां ॥ Loc. आमणिनि or आमण्यां ब्राह्मणकुले ॥ Similarly: Ins. शुचिना (same form in mas. and neu.), Dat. शुचये or शुचिनि; Abl. and Gen. शुचेः or शुचिनः Gen. Du. शुचयोः or शुचिनोः Loc. शुचो or शुचिनि ॥

BK. VII. CH. I. §. 76 ] अनड् SUBSTITUTION.

1345

Why do we say after the 3rd case and the rest? Observe मानिणी ब्राह्मणकुले, and शुचिनी Nom. dual. Why do we say having an appropriate masculine of the same form and meaning? Observe बपुणे, जतुने ॥ Why have we only one form पीलुने फलाय, when पीलुवृक्षः and पीलुकुलं show that पीलु has a masculine form also. The word पीलु is masculine when it applies to 'trees', and पीलु is neuter when it refers to 'fruits'; so this word पीलु cannot be said to be भापितपुंसकः, the masculine पीलु not having the same meaning as the neuter पीलु ॥ See VI. 3. 34.

Why do we say 'ending in a vowel except अ'? Observe कीलालपा ब्राह्मणः and कीलालपं ब्राह्मणकुले; the Ins. &c of कीलालपा will not be the Ins. &c of कीलालपं ॥ The latter will have only one form कीलालपेन ब्राह्मणकुलेन ॥ &c.

Before case affixes beginning with a consonant we have one form only, as मानिणी ब्राह्मणकुलाभ्याम् ॥

अस्थिदधिसकृप्यशणामनडुदात्तः ॥ ७५ ॥ पदानि ॥ अस्थि, दधि, सकथि, अ-शणाम्, अनड्, उदात्तः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अस्थि दधि सकथि असि इयेतेषां नपुंसकानां तृतीयारिध्वजारिपु विभक्तिपु परतो ऽनडित्ययमा-देशो भवति, स चोवाचो भवति ॥

75. The acutely accented अन (अनड्) is substituted for the finals of asthi, dadhi, sakthi and akshi, before the affixes of the Instrumental and the cases that follow it, which begin with a vowel.

Thus अस्थ्याँ, अस्थे, इथ्याँ, इथ्याँ, सकथ्याँ, सकथ्याँ, अङ्गो, अङ्गो ॥ The words अस्थि &c have acute on the first syllable, the substitute अनड would have been also anudatta, but for this sutra. The stem getting the designation अ, we elide the अ (VI. 4. 134), the udatta अ being thus elided, the case-ending, which was anudatta before, now becomes udatta (VI. 1. 161). The stems ending with 'asthi &c' and though not neuter, are governed by this rule. As मिथ्याशा ब्राह्मणेन, मिथ्याशा ॥ Why 'before the affixes of the Instrumental and the rest?' Observe अस्थिनी, इथिनी ॥ Before affixes beginning with a consonant, we have अस्थिभ्याम्, इथिभ्याम् ॥

छन्दस्यपि हृदयते ॥ ७६ ॥ पदानि ॥ छन्दसि, अपि, हृदयते ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अस्थिदधिसकृप्यशणामनड् छन्दस्यपि हृदयते । यत्र विहितस्ततोऽन्यत्रापि हृदयते ॥

76. In the Veda also, the stems 'asthi', 'dadhi', 'sakthi' and 'akshi', are found to take the substitute अनड्, before endings other than those mentioned above.

Thus the substitute is ordained before endings beginning with a vowel. In the Veda it comes before affixes beginning with a consonant. As इन्द्रो इथीयो अस्थ्यभिः, भङ्गं पश्येमाश्विभिः ॥ The substitute is ordained to come after the Instrumental &c. In the Vedic literature it is found in the Acc. &c. As अस्थ्यनि in अस्थान्युच्छल जुहोति ॥ The substitute comes before case-endings (vi-

1346

तुभ् AUGMENT.

[ Bk. VII. Ch. I. § 80.

bhakti), in the Vedic literature it comes before affixes which are not case-endings, as अश्वत्पूर्वता लाङ्गलम्, अस्यन्तं यदनस्या विभन्ति ॥ See VI. I. 176.

ई च द्विवचने ॥ ७७ ॥ पदानि ॥ ई, च, द्विवचने ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ द्विवचने परसङ्घनसि विषये उस्थादीनामीकारवेशो भवति, सच्चोवाचः ॥

77. The acutely accented ई is substituted for the final of asthi, dadhi, sakthi and akshi, in the Veda, when the case-affixes of the dual follow.

As अर्शी ते इन्द्रापङ्क्ते कपेतिव ॥ अर्शीभ्याम् ते नासिकाभ्याम् ॥ In अर्शी the augment तुभ् is not added to the stem before the vowel-beginning ending, because VII. I. 73, which ordained तुभ्, is superseded by the present sutra, and being once superseded, it is superseded for good. (सङ्कट गतो विप्रतिषेधे यद्वाधितं तद्वाधितमेव) ॥

नाभ्यस्ताच्छतुः ॥ ७८ ॥ पदानि ॥ न, अभ्यस्तात्, शतुः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अभ्यस्तादङ्गादुत्तरस्य शतुर्भुजं भवति ॥

78. The Participial-affix शतु (अत्-अन्त), does not take the augment तुभ् after a reduplicate stem.

Thus इदत्, इदतो, इदतः, जशत्, जशतो, जशतः, जामत्, जामतो, जामतः ॥ This is an exception to VII. I. 70, and applies of course to sarvanāmasthāna or strong cases. The तुभ् is to be read into this sutra from VII. I. 70; for the negation of this sutra cannot apply to ई taught in the preceding sutra, for ई is never ordained after śatri: therefore, though several other operations intervene, yet तुभ् is to be read here.

वा नपुंसकस्य ॥ ७९ ॥ पदानि ॥ वा, नपुंसकस्य ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अभ्यस्तादङ्गादुत्तरो यः शतुमय्यस्तदन्तस्य नपुंसकस्य वा तुमागमो भवति ॥

79. The Participial-affix शतु optionally takes the augment तुभ् after a reduplicate stem, in Neuter nouns.

Thus इदति or इदन्ति, कुलानि, इदति or इदन्ति कुलानि, जशति or जशन्ति कुलानि, जामति or जामन्ति कुलानि ॥ This of course applies to sarvanāmasthāna or strong cases.

आच्छीनद्योतुभ् ॥ ८० ॥ पदानि ॥ आत्, शी, नद्योः, तुभ् ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अवर्णान्तादङ्गादुत्तरस्य शतुर्भुजं तुमागमो भवति शीनद्योः परतः ॥

80. When the affix शतु comes after a verbal stem ending in अ or आ, it may optionally take the augment तुभ्, before the neutral case-ending शी and before the feminine affix ई ॥

Thus तुवती कुले or तुवन्ती कुले, तुवन्ती ब्राह्मणी, तुवती ब्राह्मणी, याती कुले, यान्ती कुले याती ब्राह्मणी, यान्ती ब्राह्मणी, करिष्यती कुले, करिष्यन्ती कुले, करिष्यती ब्राह्मणी, करिष्यन्ती ब्राह्मणी ॥ अवान्तरङ्गत्वादिकादिशे कुले व्यपवर्गाभावाववर्णान्तादङ्गादुत्तरस्य शतुर्भुजं न युज्यते ववतु, उभयत आभये नान्ताविविद्वान्ताविवज्ञावोपि नास्ति भूतपूर्वगत्याभवर्णो वा उरतो प्रतीयेवमादिव्यतिप्रसङ्ग इति, अत्र समाधि

BK. VII. CH. I § 81 ]

तुल् AUGMENT

1347

के चित्ताहुः, शत्रुवयवे शत्रुशब्दो वर्तते, अवर्णान्तादङ्गादुत्तरो यः शत्रुवयव इति ॥ अपरे पुनराहुः, आदित्येवेन शीनद्यावेव विशेष्यते, अवर्णान्तादङ्गादुत्तरे ये शीनद्या तयोः परतः शत्रुत्सत्यं तुभ्यवतीति, तत्र येन नाध्यवधानं तेन व्यवहितेपि वचनप्रमाण्यादिति तकारेणैव व्यवधानमाश्रयिष्यते ॥ आदिरिति किम्, कुर्वती, छुन्वती ॥ शीनद्योरिति किम्, तुवताम्, तुवताम् ॥

The form तुवती is thus evolved. तुव्+श+शतु+ङीप् ॥ The vikaraṇa श is added by III. I. 77, & ङीप् by IV. I. 6. This is equal to तुव्+अ+अत्+ई= तुवती the अ+अ becoming अ by the rule of पररूप ekādeśa (VI. I. 97). This ekādeśa operation being antaranga, now there is no शतु affix coming after a stem ending in अ, and therefore this sūtra will not apply. If you say the ekādeśa will be considered as the final of तुव् by VI. I. 85, we reply, that the antāchvadbhāva of that sūtra will not apply when simultaneous operations are to be performed, for अ cannot be said at one and the same time as the final of तुव् and the beginning of अत् (शतु). If you say the maxim सांप्रतिकाभावे मृतपूर्वं गतिः (when a word cannot denote something which actually is what is expressed by the word, it must be understood to denote something which formerly was what is expressed by it), will apply here, and that तुव् will be considered to end in अ because it formerly did end in the affix अ of श; we reply that then the present rule should apply to forms like अवती प्रती &c. For here also we have अत्+शप् लोप+शतु+ङीप्; and अत् should be considered to end in अ, because it had the affix शप् after it, though it was afterwards elided. The maxim quoted, therefore, proves too much.

To solve these objections, some say, that the word शतु in this sūtra means 'a portion of the affix शतु, such as त्' and the sūtra means 'after a stem ending in अ, to the portion त् of the affix शतु there is added तुव्.' Others say, the word आन् in the sūtra qualifies शी and नदी and not शतु; and the sūtra means 'तुम् is added to a stem ending in शतु, when शी or नदी affixes follow after a stem ending in अ.' Therefore in तुवती the affix ई is considered to come after the अ of तुव्, the intervening त् not debarring it.

Why do we say 'after अ'? Observe कुर्वती and छुन्वती, no optional तुम् is added here. Why do we say 'शी and नदी following'? Observe तुवताम् and तुवताम्.

शप्इयनोर्नित्यम् ॥ ५१ ॥ पदानि ॥ शप्, इयनोः, नित्यम् ॥
वृत्तिः ॥ शप् ञ्यन् इत्येतयोः शतुः शीनद्योः परतो नित्यं तुगागनो भवति ॥

81. When the affix शतु comes after a verbal stem ending in the vikaraṇas शप् and इयन्, it invariably takes the augment तुम् before the neutral case-ending शी (ई), and the feminine ending ई (Nadi).

Thus पचन्ती कुले, पचन्ती ब्राह्मणी, वीव्यन्ती कुले, वीव्यन्ती ब्राह्मणी, सीव्यन्ती कुले, सीव्यन्ती ब्राह्मणी ॥ The word नित्य stops the anuvṛtti of वा (VII. I. 79).
