तुम् AUGMENT.

[ Bk. VII. Ch. I. §. 85

सावनदुहः ॥ ५२ ॥ पदानि ॥ सौ, अनदुहः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ सौ परतो उनदुहो नृमागमो भवति ॥

82. अनदुह gets the augment तुम् before the ending
सु of the Nom. Sg. (and Vocative).

By VII. 1. 98 अनदुह gets the augment आ after उ in the strong cases,
and अ in Vocative Singular (VII. 1. 99). It thus becomes अनदुह and अनदुह ॥
By the present sutra नृ is added after this आ and अ ॥ The case-ending is
elided by VI. 1. 68, and the final ह by VIII. 2. 23. Thus we have अनदुह
Nominative Singular; and अनदुह in the Vocative Singular. The augments
आम् and अम् (VII. 1. 98, 99), do not supersede तुम्, nor are they superseded
by तुम् ॥

In this sutra, some read the annvritti of आम् from VII. 1. 80; and by
so doing they add तुम् to that form of अनदुह where there is an आ or अ,
namely, after the word has taken the augment आम् in the nominative singular
by VII. 1. 98, and अम् in the Vocative by VII. 1. 99. Therefore, the तुम् does
not debar आम् or अम्, nor is it debarred by आम् or अम् ॥ Others hold that
though one is a general rule and the other is a particular rule, yet in this instance,
आम् (or अम्) and तुम् are applied simultaneously, one not debarring the
other, there is no relationship of बाध्य and बाधक among them, just as in
विचारयति the rule of lengthening (VI. 4. 16) and reduplication are applied
simultaneously, one not debarring the other. In बहुनदुहि ब्राह्मणकुलानि, we add
first आम् because it is subsequent, and them we add तुम् by VII. 1. 72 on the
maxim of पुनः प्रसङ्गविज्ञान &c ॥

हकस्ववस्वतवसां छन्दसि ॥ ५३ ॥ पदानि ॥ हक, स्ववस्, स्वतवसाम्,
छन्दसि ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ हक स्ववस् स्वतवसुह्येतेषां सौ परतो तुमागमो भवति छन्दसिविषये ॥

83. हश, स्ववस् and स्वतवस् take the augment तुम्
before the affix सु (Nominative and Vocative Singular) in
the Veda.

Thus ईहक, ताहक, याहक, सहक, स्ववान्, स्वतवान् ॥ The श of ईहश (formed by
III. 2. 60), is elided by VIII. 2. 23; and क substituted for नृ by VIII. 2. 62.
The lengthening in स्ववान् and स्वतवान् is through VI. 4. 14.

दिव औत् ॥ ५४ ॥ पदानि ॥ दिवः, औत् ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ दिवित्येतस्य सौ परतो औदित्ययमादेशो भवति ॥

84. औ is substituted for the final of दिव् before सु
(Nom. Sg. and Voc. Sg).

As सौः ॥ There is a nominal-stem दिव् which is taken here. It has no
indicatory letters annexed to it. The root दिव् is not to be taken here, as it

has the indicatory letter इ and is exhibited in the Dhātupāṭha as दिहु ॥ The nominal-stem derived from दिहु, does not take ओ, but ऊ, the Nom. Sg. of which is शु: as असुसु: (See VI. 4. 19, and VI. 1. 131).

पथिमध्युमुक्षामात् ॥ ८५ ॥ पदानि ॥ पथि, मथि, क्कुमुक्षाम्, आत् ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ पथिन् मथिन् क्कुमुक्षिन् इत्येतेपामङ्गानां सौ परत आकार आदिशो भवति ॥

85. आत् (आ) is substituted for the final of 'pathin' 'mathin' and 'ṛbhukshin', before the ending सु (of the Nom. Sg).

As पन्थाः, मन्थाः, क्कुमुक्षाः ॥ Though the sthānin here is a nasal (i. e. न), yet the substitute आ is not to be nasalised, but to be pronounced purely. For न् see VII. 1. 87. The nasal आ is not to be taken on the maxim माध्यमानेन सवर्णानां महन् न भवति ॥ 'A letter which is taught in a rule does not denote the letters homogeneous with it.'

इतोत्सवैनामस्थाने ॥ ८६ ॥ पदानि ॥ इतः, अत्, सर्वनामस्थाने ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ पथ्यादीनामिकारस्य स्थाने आकारादिशो भवति ॥

86. अ is substituted for the इ of 'pathin, mathin and ṛbhukshin,' in the strong cases.

Thus पन्थाः, पन्थानो, पन्थानः, पन्थानम्, पन्थानो, मन्थाः, मन्थानो, मन्थानः, मन्थानम्, मन्थानो, क्कुमुक्षाः, क्कुमुक्षाणो, क्कुमुक्षाणः, क्कुमुक्षाणम्, क्कुमुक्षाणो ॥ आदिति वर्त्तमाने पुनरुद्धचनं पपूर्वायम्, क्कुमुक्षाणमित्यत्र वा पपूर्वस्य निगमहति दीर्घविकल्पः ॥

Though the anuvṛtti of आत् was here, the separate mention of अत् is for the sake of VI. 4. 9: by which in the case of क्कुमुक्षिन् we have two forms, क्कुमुक्षाणम् and क्कुमुक्षाणम् ॥

थोन्थः ॥ ८७ ॥ पदानि ॥ थः, अन्थः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ पथिमयोस्यकारस्य स्थाने न् इत्यवमादेशो भवति सर्वनामस्थाने परतः ॥

87. न् is substituted for the थ of pathin and mathin in the strong cases.

As पन्थाः, पन्थानो, पन्थानः, मन्थाः, मन्थानो मन्थानः ॥

अस्य टेलोपः ॥ ८८ ॥ पदानि ॥ अस्य, टेः, लोपः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ पथ्यादीनां असङ्गकानां टेलोपो भवति ॥

88. The last vowel, with the consonant that follows it, is dropped in pathin, mathin and ṛbhukshin, before a weak case-ending beginning with a vowel (before which the stem is called Bha I. 4. 18).

As पथः, पथा, पथे, मथः, मथा, मथे, क्कुमुक्षः, क्कुमुक्षः, क्कुमुक्षे ॥ The anuvṛtti of sarvanāmasthāna, of course, is inappropriate here: though its anuvṛtti is current as will be seen in the next sūtra.

पुं सो ञ्सुङ् ॥ ८९ ॥ पदानि ॥ पुंसः, असुङ् ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ पुंस इत्येतस्य सर्वनामस्थाने परतो ञ्सुङ्गित्यवमादेशो भवति ॥

1350

गिरि OPERATIONS.

[ Bk. VII. Ch. I. §. 91.

89. असुइ (अस) is substituted for the final of पुंस in the strong cases.

The word पुंस is derived from पा (to protect) + इम्सुन (Un IV. 178), the न् being changed to anusvāra. So when स् of पुंस is replaced by अस् we get the form पुमस, the उ of असुइ indicates that न् should be added in the strong cases after अ (VII. 1. 70), so we have पुमान्, पुमांसी, पुमांसः ॥

This substitution must take place in its incipient stage before the affixes are added, (उपदेशविद्भावः): otherwise the accent will be wrong. The compounds have acute on the final, (VI. 1. 223), therefore, परमपुंस् has acute on पु. and in the Nominative Singular परमपुमान् the acute will remain on पु, but it is intended that it should be on मा, thus परमपुमान् ॥ The simple word पुमान् of course, has accent on पु ॥

गोतो णित् ॥ ६० ॥ पदानि ॥ गोतो, णित् ॥
वृत्तिः ॥ गोशब्दात्परं सर्वनामस्थानं णिद्धवति ॥

90. The endings of the strong cases are णित् after गो ॥

That is, these affixes produce all the णित् operations: such as Vriddhi &c. As गोः, गावो, गावः ॥ Why have we added a न् after गो? The rule applies to the form गो, and not when it assumes the form सु, as in चिचसुः, शबलसुः ॥

How do you explain the forms हे चिचगो, हे शबलगवः? This is done on the maxim अङ्गुत्ते पुनर्ज्ञाताविधि निहितस्य, (when an operation which is taught in the Angādhikāra VI. 4.—VII. 4. has taken place, and another operation of the Angādhikāra is subsequently applicable, this latter operation is not allowed to take place). For when Guṇa once takes place before the Vocative and the Nominative Plural affix by VII. 3. 108-109, the णित् operation of this rule will not again take place. Or गोतः in the sūtra may be construed as Sambandha-lakshāṇa Sasthī (a Genitive denoting a general relation): and the meaning will be “that sarvanāmasthāna affix, denoting singular, dual, plural, which refers to the meaning of गो or ‘cow.’ While in चिचसुः, the sarvanāmasthāna affix does not refer to ‘cow’ but to another object, namely to a ‘person’ who possesses brindled cows. न् in गोत् in this view is for specification only.

Some read the sūtra as ओतः णित्, so that the rule will apply to बोः also: as, बोः, यावो, यावः ॥ If the reading be taken गोतः, then we extend this rule to बोः also, by taking गो as merely illustrative of all words ending in ओः; and this is done by the letter न् in गोतः, for the सपर rule applies to letters, and not to words, so that गोतः means and includes गो and words ending in ओ ॥

णलुत्तमो वा ॥ ९१ ॥ पदानि ॥ णल्, उत्तमः, वा ॥
वृत्तिः ॥ उत्तमो णल्वा णित् भवति णित्कायं सन्न वा भवतीत्यर्थः ॥

91. The ending of the First Pers. Sg. in the Perfect optionally acts as णित् ॥

The Vriddhi is optional, as अहं नकार् or नकर, अहं पपाच् or पपच् ॥

सख्युरसम्बुद्धौ ॥ ६२ ॥ पदानि ॥ सख्युः, अ सम्बुद्धौ ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ असंबुद्धौ यः सखिशब्दः तस्मात्परं सर्वनामस्थानं गिद्धवति ॥

92. After सखि, the endings of the strong cases, with the exception of the Vocative singular, are णित् ॥

That is, they cause Vriddhi. As सखायो, सखायः, but हे सखे ॥

अनङ् सौ ॥ ६३ ॥ पदानि ॥ अनङ्, सौ ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ सखिशब्दस्य सौ परतो ऽनङ्मयमादेशो भवति स चेखुशब्दः संबुद्धिर्न भवति ॥

93. अनङ् (अन्) is substituted for the इ of सखि before सु of the Nominative Singular, (but not in the Vocative Singular).

As सखा, but हे सखे ॥

ऋतुशनसुरुदंशोनेहसां च ॥ ६४ ॥ पदानि ॥ ऋत, उशनस्, पुरुदंशः अनेहसाम् च ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ ऋकारान्तानामङ्गानादशनस पुरुदंशम् इत्येतेषां चासंबुद्धौ सौ परतो ऽनङ्मदेशो भवति ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ उशनसः सम्बुद्धावपिपलेऽनङ् इष्यते । न ङ्मसंबुद्धोरिति नलोपप्रतिषेधोपि पक्षइष्यते ॥

*Kārikā* :—संवेधने तुषनसस्त्रिरूपं सान्तं तथा नान्तमथाप्यदन्तम् ॥

माध्यं विनिर्विष्टं गुणं विगते नपुंसके व्याघ्रपदा वरिष्ठः ॥

94. Anan (अन्) is substituted for the final of the stems ending in ऋ, as well as for the final of uṣanas, purudanṣas, and anēhas, in the Nominative Singular (but not in the Vocative Singular).

As कर्ता, हर्ता, माता, पिता, भ्राता, उशना, पुरुदंशा, अनेहा ॥ In the Voc. Sg. we have हे कर्तः, हे मातः, पितः पुरुदंशः, अनेहः and उशनः ॥

*Vārt* :—अनङ् is substituted for the final of उशनस् in the Voc. Sg. also, as हे उशनन्, the final न् not being elided (See VIII. 2. 8). Otherwise we have हे उशन ! Thus it has three forms in the Vocative Singular : as हे उशनस्, हे उशनन्, and हे उशन ! ॥

*Kārikā* :—In the vocative, the word उशनस् has three forms, (1) ending in स् when अनङ् is not added, (2) ending in न्, when न् is not elided, (3) ending in अ when न् is elided. This is the opinion of the Achārya Mādhyandini. So also according to the Achārya Vaiyāghrapadya, (the best of the Vyāghrapadas), there is Guṇa in the Neuter of the stems ending in इक् vowels; as हे बपो ॥

The न् in ऋन् is for the sake of distinctness.

तृज्वत्कोषुः ॥ ६५ ॥ पदानि ॥ तृज्वत, कोषुः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ कोषुदुशब्दस्तुन्यव्ययान्तः संज्ञाशब्दः सर्वनामस्थाने ऽसंबुद्धौ परत तृज्वद्वति ॥

दृष्टि AUGMENT.

[ Bk. VII. Ch. I. §. 97

95. The word क्रोष्टु 'a jackal' is treated in the strong cases (with the exception of Vocative Singular) as if it ended in तृच् (तृ) ॥

The word क्रोष्टु is declined like क्रोष्टु in the strong cases. As क्रोष्टो, क्रोष्टोरो, क्रोष्टोः, क्रोष्टोः, क्रोष्टोरो ॥ But क्रोष्टु in weak cases, and हे क्रोष्टो in the Vocative Singular. The accent in the strong cases is also that of the तृच् affix, i.e. acute on the final. The word क्रोष्टु is formed by the affix तृच् (Un सितनिगनि &c, I. 69).

स्त्रियां च ॥ ६२ ॥ पदानि ॥ स्त्रियां, च ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ असर्वनामस्थानार्थनारम्भः । स्त्रियां च क्रोष्टुशब्दस्य तृच्यव्रतति ॥

96. The word क्रोष्टु is treated as if it ended in तृच्, in the feminine, before all case-endings.

This sutra is commenced for the sake of cases other than strong ones. In strong cases, whether of masculine or feminine, the former sutra applies; but in the feminine, in other cases also there is trich-treatment. Thus क्रोष्टो, क्रोष्टोः, क्रोष्टोः ॥ Some read the word क्रोष्टु in the Gaurādi class (IV. I. 41), and they treat it as a तृच् ending word before the feminine affix ङीप्, as क्रोष्टो ॥ According to them, in forming the Taddhitārtha compounds like पञ्चभिः क्रोष्टोःः क्रोष्टोःः = पञ्चक्रोष्टुनी रयेः, we could not get the form पञ्चक्रोष्टुभिः, because when the affix ङक is elided by V. I. 28, the feminine is also elided by I. 2. 49, and the ङीप् being thus luk-elided, there would be no तृच्ङाप्, because the affix leaves no trace behind I. I. 63. To get out of the difficulty, we can only say, that the form is so, in spite of the apparent inconsistency.

Those who do not read क्रोष्टु in the Gaurādi class, they explain this sutra by saying that the word स्त्रियां indicates the sense, namely, क्रोष्टु is treated like a तृच् word, when it denotes a female, wherever it may occur.

And because क्रोष्टु is treated as if it was क्रोष्टु, the feminine will be formed by the affix ङीप् by IV. I. 5, and the form क्रोष्टोः will be end-acute by VI. I. 174. So that whether क्रोष्टो be formed by ङीप् under Gaurādi class, or by ङीप् under IV. I. 5, the accent remains the same: while under this second view, we have not to face any such difficulty as in the first.

विभाषा तृतीयादिष्वचि ॥ ६७ ॥ पदानि ॥ विभाषा, तृतीयादिषु, अचि ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ तृतीयादिषु विभक्तिम्पन्नादिषु क्रोष्टुविभाषा तृच्यव्रतति ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ तृच्यव्रतात् पूर्वव्रततिवेधेन तृच्यव्रतति भवतः ॥

97. क्रोष्टु may optionally be treated as Kroshtr, before the endings beginning with a vowel, in the Instrumental and the cases that follow it.

As क्रोष्टोः or क्रोष्टुना, क्रोष्टोः or क्रोष्टवे, क्रोष्टोः or क्रोष्टोः, क्रोष्टोः or क्रोष्टोः, क्रोष्टोः or क्रोष्टोः ॥ But क्रोष्टु in the Accusative Plural, and क्रोष्टु-यां before consonant-beginning affixes.

102. उर् is substituted for the final long ऋ of a root, when it is preceded by a labial consonant belonging to the root.

As पूर्ति and पूवर्पति from पू, so also पूवर्पति ॥ The lengthening is by VIII. 2. 77. The rule applies when the dento-labial व precedes: as पूवर्पति कश्चिजम् from पू; so also प्राप्युप्पति कञ्चलम् ॥ The labial consonant must be the consonant of the root. Therefore when ऋ 'to go' is preceded by सत्, the rule will not apply, for न् is not part of the root: as समीर्णम् by VII. I. 100.

*Vārt*:—The Guṇa and Vṛiddhi do take place in supersession of इर् and उर् substitution. Thus आस्तरणम् and आस्तारकः (from रुह् with लुह् and लुह्), निपरणम्, निपारकः from पू, निगरणम्, निगारकः from गु ॥

बहुलं छन्दसि ॥ १०३ ॥ पदानि ॥ बहुलम्, छन्दसि ॥
वृत्तिः ॥ छन्दसि विधेये कृकारान्तस्य धातोरङ्गस्य बहुलङ्कारवेशो भवति ॥

103. In the Veda, the उर् substitution for ऋ of a root-stem is diverse.

That is, it takes place even when the preceding letter is not labial, and does not take place even when the letter is labial. Thus मित्रा वरुणो ततुरिः, इरे ह्यध्वा जयुरिः, पपितमम् (no change), and पपुरिः, from तू, गु and पू ॥ All these words ततुरि, जयुरि and पपि are formed by the affix किन् (III. I. 171).

### BOOK SEVENTH.

सिचि वृद्धि: परस्मैपदेषु ॥ १ ॥ पदानि ॥ सिचि, वृद्धि:, परस्मैपदेषु ॥
वृत्तिः ॥ परस्मैपदे परे सिचि परत इगन्तस्याङ्गस्य वृद्धिभेवति ॥

1. Before the Aorist-characteristic स (सिच), Vriddhi is substituted in the Parasmaipada, for the final of a stem ending in इ, उ, ऋ (long or short, I. 1. 3).

The word इङ् is to be read into this sutra by virtue of I. 1. 3. As अचैषीत्, अनैषीत्, अलावीत्, अपावीत्, अकार्पीत्, अहार्पीत् (VII. 3. 96 and VIII. 2. 28) The antaranga guna substitution is superseded by the express mention of Vriddhi. If the antaranga guna is superseded by this vriddhi, why is not the antaranga उबङ् also superseded in न्यदुवीत्, न्यदुवीत्? The Vriddhi does not take place, as these roots belong to कुटादि class, after which this affix is ङित् (I. 2. 1). The Vriddhi being thus superseded, we have उबङ् substitution. Why do we say in the Parasmaipada? Observe अच्योङ्, अहोङ् ॥

अतो ज्ञान्तस्य ॥ २ ॥ पदानि ॥ अतः, ज्ञान्तस्य ॥
वृत्तिः ॥ रैकलकारी यावतः समीपो तदन्तस्याङ्गस्य अत एव स्थाने वृद्धिभेवति ॥

2. Vriddhi is substituted for the short अ, when it is immediately followed by the final र् or ल् of a root, before the Parasmaipada s-Aorist.

As क्षर्-अक्षारीत्, स्वर्-अस्सारीत्, ज्वल्-अज्वालीत्, ह्वल्-अह्वालीत् ॥ This debars the option of VII. 2. 7. Why 'short अ'? Observe न्यस्सारीत् न्यसीलीत् ॥ Why do we say 'ending in र or ल'? Observe मा भवानसीत्, मा भवानदीत् ॥ The word अन्त means here 'proximity', as in the sentence उबङ् कान्तं गतः = उबङ् कसमीपं गतः ॥ The अ must be in the proximity of the र and ल् ॥ Therefore the rule does not apply to अवशीत्, अश्वलीत्, for though र and ल are here final of the stem, yet are not in the proximity of अ ॥

वदवजहलन्तस्याचः ॥ ३ ॥ पदानि ॥ वद, प्रज, हलन्तस्य, अचः ॥
वृत्तिः ॥ वदवजोहलन्तानां चाङ्गानामचः स्थाने वृद्धिभेवति सिचि परस्मैपदे परतः ॥

3. In the Parasmaipada s-Aorist there is Vriddhi of the अ of बबू, अज़, and of any vowel, without distinction, of the stems ending in a consonant.

As अयादीत्, अज़ाजीत् ॥ This debars the option in the case of these two roots, which would have otherwise obtained by VII. 2. 7. So also of stems ending in consonants: as अपाशीत्, अमैशीत्, अच्छैशीत्, अरोशीत् ॥ By the splitting up of the sūtra (yoga-vibhaga) these forms could be evolved without using the word इलन्त in the sūtra. Thus (1) बब्बुज्यो: “In the room of the अ of बबू and अज़ there is Vriddhi”. (2) अच्: “In the room of the vowel of the stem there is Vriddhi”. The word “stem” is understood throughout these chapters. If the vowel be at the end of the stem, there would be Vriddhi by VII. 2. 1, and if in the middle of the stem, then the verb ends with a consonant, and still there will be Vriddhi by our rule. The use of the word इलन्त in the sūtra indicates that the rule applies when more than one consonant even is at the end: as अराङ्शीत्, अनाङ्शीत् ॥

Had the word इलन्तस्य not been used in the sūtra, then the following maxim would have applied “येन नान्यवधानं तेन व्यवहितेऽपि वचनप्रामाण्यात्” ॥ The rule would have applied where only one consonant intervened between the vowel and the affix, but not when more than one consonant intervened. But it is intended that the rule should apply to such cases also.

The form उद्वेगाम् is thus evolved. To the root बह् we add सिच् in the second Person singular. Thus बह्+स्ताम् ॥ Now there appears the Vriddhi rule on the one side; and the rule requiring the change of इ to ड (VIII. 2. 31) the rule requiring the elision of स् (VIII. 2. 26), the rule requiring the change of त into ध (VIII. 2. 40), then the rule requiring the change of ध into ड, and then the elision of one ड (VIII. 3. 13) on the other. What rule is to be applied first—the Vriddhi or the other rules? The Vriddhi rule is to be applied first, because the other rules are considered as asiddha (VIII. 2. 1): and after that we apply the other rules: and afterwards on account of the elision of ड, we change the Vriddhi आ into ओ (VI. 3. 112). The equation will be something like this:—बह्+स्ताम्=वाह्+स्ताम् (VII. 2. 3)=वाह्+स्ताम् (VIII. 2. 31)=वाह्+ताम् (VIII. 2. 26)=वाह्+धाम् (VIII. 2. 80)=वाह्+दाम् (VIII. 4. 41)=वा+दाम् (VIII. 3. 13)=वोदाम् (VI. 3. 112). This with the upasarga उत् and the augment अ becomes उद्वेगाम् ॥ Similar is the evolution of उद्वेगाम् with स्तम् ॥ Once the अ has been Vriddhied into आ, there is no Vriddhi of ओ ॥ Had we not first Vriddhied the बह् into वाह्, but applied the vriddhi rule last, then there would have been vriddhi of ओ, as वोदाम् which is wrong. In fact where there has not taken place vriddhi first, there ओ is vriddhied, as=वोदामिनस्यापत्यं =वोदामिनः ॥

In the case of roots ऊन and ईद in the above examples, the चङ् is prohibited by III. 1. 51. This is an exception to VII. 2. 7: so far as stems in ह, य and म are concerned. There is no option allowed here. In the case of जागु, णि, roots, and दिव, the Vriddhi would have taken place by VII. 1. 1; and VII. 1. 4, could not have debarred Vriddhi, hence the special mention of these roots.

Nor can it be said, in the case of these roots, that 'they will take first guṇa, on account of its being an Antaranga operation', because, then the rule of Vriddhi ordained by VII. 1. 1 will find no scope. Moreover, if the guṇa

1358

AORIST VRIDDHI.

[ Bk. VII. Ch. II. §. 6.

took place first and then Vriddhi, the mention of णि-roots and णि in the sūtra would be redundant. For in ऊनयीत् and अश्वयीत्, having guṇated the roots ऊनि and णि to ऊन and णि, and then substituting अश् (which is also antaranga) for ण् before ईत्, we have ऊनय+ईत्, and अश्+ईत् ॥ Now these are roots which end in य् and would be covered by the first portion of the present sūtra, viz, "h-m-y-anta", so the especial mention of णि-roots and णि would be superfluous, if guṇa was to take place first. The very mention of णि-roots and णि in this sūtra, is a jñāpaka (indicator) of the following maxim न सिचि अन्तरङ्गमस्ति ॥

Why have we used the root जाग् in the sūtra, when the special sūtra VII. 3. 85 will cause guṇa by superseding Vriddhi in the case of जाग्? This supersession will take place on the analogy of अचोऽमृणाति (VII. 2. 115); for as this vriddhi rule VII. 2. 115 is superseded by VII. 3. 85, so will the present Vriddhi rule VII. 2. 1. Ans. No, this is not so. No doubt VII. 3. 85 does supersede the vriddhi rule VII. 2. 1 and we have guṇa, as जागर+ईत् ॥ Then comes in VII. 2. 2, which would cause vriddhi, because now it is a root ending in र्; this second vriddhi is prohibited by the present sūtra. You can say, that by the very fact that the guṇa rule VII. 3. 85 takes effect, will prevent every future Vriddhi, as in जागर+ति there is no penultimate vriddhi by VII. 2. 116 [ जाग्+णि=जागर+णि (VII. 3. 85)=जागरि the rule VII. 2. 116 does not apply after guṇa ] You can, of course, say so, and there is no answer to this but by saying that the mention of जाग् is only for the sake of distinctness.

In case the reading of जाग् in the sūtra be held necessary, then the operations which it undergoes, are shown below:

जाग्+इस्+ईत् ॥ Now appears (1) the rule VI. 1. 77, requiring the change of क् into र् ॥ (2) This अणादेश is however, debarred by the rule VII. 3. 84 which causes guṇa of the finals of verbal stems before all sārvadhātuka and ārdhadhātuka affixes, because this guṇa rule is an apavāda to अणादेश ॥ (3) But this guṇa in its turn is debarred by the rule VII. 2. 1 requiring the vriddhi. (4) But this vriddhi is, however, superseded by VII. 3. 85, which causes the guṇa of the final of जाग् ॥ Now having guṇated it, we get this form:—

जागर+इस्+ईत् ॥ Now appears VII. 2. 3 which requires vriddhi, because it is a root ending in a consonant. (2) But that vriddhi is superseded by VII. 2. 4 because the affix सिच् has taken the इद् augment. (3) Then appears the rule VII. 2. 7 requiring optional vriddhi, (4) But that optional vriddhi is superseded by the compulsory vriddhi required by VII. 2. 2, because it is a root ending in र् ॥ (5) And this last vriddhi is prohibited by the present sūtra VII. 2. 5. These nine stages through which the form अजागरीत् is evolved, is abbreviated in the following mnemonic verse:—युणो वृद्धि युणो वृद्धि: प्रतिषेधो विकल्पनम् ॥ पुन वृद्धि निषेधोऽतो अणपूर्वो: प्रापयो नव ॥

ऊर्णोतेर्विभाषा ॥ ६ ॥ पदानि ॥ ऊर्णोतिः, विभाषा ॥
वृत्तिः ॥ ऊर्णोतेरिहारी सिचि परलेपपरे परतो विभाषा वृद्धिर्नभवति ।

BK. VII. CH. II. §. 7 ]

AORIST VRIDDHI.

1359

6. Before an इद-beginning s-Aorist of the Paras-maipada, there is optional Vriddhi of the vowel of ऊर्णु ॥

As प्रीर्णवीत् or प्रीर्णवीत् ॥ This option applies when the सिच् is not treated as डित् ॥ But after ऊर्णु, सिच् is optionally डित्, (I. 2. 6): when it is डित्, there being neither guna nor vriddhi; we have उवहू substitution, as प्रीर्णवीत् (VI. 4. 77).

अतो हलादेलेघोः ॥ ७ ॥ पदानि ॥ अतः, हल् आदेः, लघोः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ हलादेलेघोः लघोरकारस्य इदादो सिच् परलेपपपरे परतो विभाषा वृद्धिम् भवति ।

7. Before an इद-beginning s-Aorist of the Paras-maipada, the short अ of the root gets optionally Vriddhi, when the stem begins with a consonant, and the अ is prosodially short by being followed by a simple consonant.

Thus अकणीत् or अकाणीत्, अरणीत् or अराणीत् ॥ Why do we say 'of अ'? Observe अवेवीत्, असेवीत् ॥ Besides this patent objection, there is another, not so manifest. If we had not taken अतः, the sutra would have ordained Vriddhi of every vowel (अचः VII. 2. 3), the Vriddhi so ordained would be an अच् pertaining Vriddhi, and not an इक्-pertaining Vriddhi. Therefore डित् affixes will not debar such Vriddhi, for the बिडति च (I. 1. 5), debars only इल्लक्षण Vriddhi. Therefore कुदादि roots after which सिच् is डित् (I. 2. 1), will get Vriddhi, which is not desired. Therefore we have only one form of त्यकुटीत्, त्यपुटीत् ॥

Why do we say 'beginning with a consonant'? Observe मा भवानधीत्, मा भवानधीत् from अश् and अद् ॥ Why do we say 'prosodially short'? Observe अतक्षीत्, अरक्षीत् ॥

But why does not vriddhi take place in अचकासीत् from the root चकास् (Ad. 65)? The vriddhi does not take place on the maxim वेन ना व्यवधानं तेन व्यवहितेऽपि वचन प्रामाण्यात्; for the rule applies to short अ only when a consonant intervenes between it and the affix, and not when both consonants and vowels intervene. In चकास् not only the consonants क् and स् intervene but also the vowel आ ॥ Hence there is no vriddhi. Moreover, the व्यवधान can be by one letter and not by more than one letter. Therefore, applying this maxim, the word लघोः might have been omitted from the sutra without any detriment. In that case, the form अतक्षीत् from the root लक्ष (Bhu 685) will be explained by saying that rule VII. 2. 7 does not apply to it, because two consonants intervene between अ and the affix. In this view of the case, the employment of the word लघोः in the sutra is for the sake of distinctness only.

The word इद is understood in this sutra, so that the rule applies to सेद् aorist. The rule therefore, does not apply to Anit aorist, as अपाक्षीत् ॥

The form अपिपलिपीत् the aorist of the Desiderative root, is explained by saying that the long आ of vriddhi is elided by VI. 4. 64.

इद AUGMENT.

[ Bk. VII. Ch. II. §. 9 ]

नेडुशि कृति ॥ ८ ॥ पदानि ॥ न, इद, वशि, कृति ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ वशादि कृति प्रत्यये परत इडागमो न भवति ।

8. The augment इद is not added to a krit-affix beginning with a sonant consonant (वश pratyāhāra).

The वश pratyāhāra is rather vague. The rule really applies to Krit-affixes beginning with व, र (ल) म and न, and no कृत affix begins with any other letter of वश class. Thus ईशिता, ईशितुम् non-vaś letters get the augment, but not ईश्वरः, (III. 2. 175) so also दीपिता, दीपितुम् but not दीपम् (III. 2. 167) मस्तिता, मस्तितुम् but not मस्तः, (III. 2. 75. मानम्) यतिता, यतितुम् but not यतः (III. 3. 90 नः)

The Vārtika नेडु वरमनादि कृति gives the rule in a more definite form. Of course, in the Uṇādi Krit-affixes, there is diversity. There we get the affix ङ, for example, which of course does not take the augment, as इम्+ङ=इण्डः (Un I. 113). Why do we say कृत affixes? Observe इदिय, इदिय ॥

Here by VII. 2. 76 the Sārvadhātuka affixes beginning with a वश consonant take इद augment after the roots इद &c; but this इद will also be prohibited by the present sūtra, if the word कृति be not read in the sūtra. So that rule VII. 2. 76 would find scope before those वशादि affixes only which do not begin with a वश letter; as इदियः ॥ In some texts of Kāsika the counter-example is इदियम् in the Perfect. This is wrong, according to Padamjari (कादिनि-यमादि इदः सिद्धत्वात्) because इद always comes in the Perfect except after the root क &c. (VII. 2. 13): so the counter-example from the Perfect Tense is not valid. This sūtra is an exception to VII. 2. 35. The Krit-affixes beginning with वश letters as given by Pāṇini are the following: वन (वनिष, कुनिष, ऊवनिष), वर (वरच and कुरप), वस (कुसु), र (कु), लुक (कलुकन), मन (मनिन), मर (कमरच्) न (नह, नम्), नङ् (नजिह्), तु (कतु) ॥ This list will show the truth of the above vārtika.

तितुत्रतयसिसुसरकसेषु च ॥ ९ ॥ पदानि ॥ ति, तु, त्र, त, य, सि, सु, सर, क, सेषु, ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ ति तु त्र त य सि सु सर क स इय्येतेषु कुसु इडागमो न भवति ।

वार्तिकम् ॥ तितुवेषु अथशदीनाम् इति वक्तव्यम् ॥

9. The इद augment is not taken by the following Krit-affixes:—ति, तु, त्र, त, य, सि, सु, सर, क and स ॥

Thus (1) किंच्—तन्ति: but तनिता, तनितुम्, किंच्—दीपिः but दीपिता, दीपितुम् ॥ (2) तुन् (Un I. 70)—सक्तुः but साचिता, साचितुम् ॥ (3) तुन् (III. 2. 182)—पञ्च but पतिता, पतितुम्, so also Uṇādi तुन् (Un IV. 158), as तन्त्रम् from तन् ॥ (4) तन् (Un III. 86)—हस्तः but हसिता, हसितुम्; so also लीतः, पीतः, धूर्चः from तु, पु, धूर्च forming सेद् लबिता, पविता, धूर्चिता ॥ The त affix mentioned in the sūtra refers to this Uṇādi त (Un III. 86), and not to the त (क) of Nishthā, for the Nishthā त takes the augment, as हसितुम् ॥ (5) कथम् (Un II. 2)—कुछम् but कोपिता, कोचितुम्, काष्ठम् but काषिता, काषितुम् ॥ (6) कृति (Un III. 155), as कुक्षिः but कोपिता, कोचितुम् ॥ (7) कछु (Un III. 157)—इक्षुः but एपिता, एपितुम्; (8) सरन् (Un III. 70)—अक्षरम्,

BK. VII. CH. II. §. 10 ]

इद AUGMENT.

1361

but अशिता, अशितुम् ॥ (9) कन् (Un III. 43)—शल्कः but शलिता, शलितुम् ॥ (10) स (Un III. 62)—वस्तः but वविता, ववितुम् ॥

*Vārt*:—The affix ति, तु and बि take इद augment after मह and words of similar formations:—as विशुद्धीतिः, उपसिद्धीतिः, निक्षुचित् निपादितिः ॥

Before non-krit ति &c, we have इद, as रोवितिः, स्वपितिः ॥

एकाच उपदेशो अनुदातात् ॥ १० ॥ पदानि ॥ एकाचः, उपदेशो, अनुदातात्, ॥
वृत्तिः ॥ उपदेशो य एकाच धातुरनुदात्तश्च तस्मादिद्वागमो न भवति ।

10. The augment इद is not added to that affix which is joined to a root, which in the Grammatical system of Instruction (i. e. in the Dhātupāṭha) is of one syllable, and is without accent (anudātta).

A list of such roots has been collected by the *Anit—Kārikā*. They are given below.

*Kārikā*:—अनिद्रस्वरान्तो भवतीति दृढयतामिमांस्तु सेटः प्रवृत्ति तद्विः ।

अवन्तभुवन्तमृतां च वृक्ष्युनी भिडीकिवर्णेष्वय शीङ्भिन्नाभिपि ॥

गणस्थमुवन्तमृतां च रस्तुवो श्रुवन्तयोर्णातिमयो गुणुक्षणः ।

इति स्वरान्ता निपुणैः समुचितास्ततो हलन्तानपि सन्निबोधतः ॥

As a general rule all monosyllabic roots ending in a *vowel* except अ, long क and long क् are anudātta, and do not take इद augment: as दातृ, नेतृ, चेतृ, स्तोतृ, कर्तृ, हर्तृ ॥ The following are the exceptions:—

(1) All roots ending in short अ are Udātta and take इद; as अवधिष्ट ॥

(2) All roots ending in long क् are सेद, as नृ—तरिता or तरीता ॥

(3) All roots ending in short क् are अनिद् except वृङ् (IX. 38 the references are to the class and number in the Dhātupāṭha) and वृञ् (V. 8, X. 271): as निर्वरिता or निर्वरीतां, प्रवरिता or प्रवरीता ॥

(4) All roots in short इ are Anit, except भि (I. 1059), 'to grow' and भिम् 'to attend' (I. 945), as भ्ययिता, भ्ययिता ॥

(5) All roots in long ई are Anit, except शीङ् 'to rest' (II. 22), and शीङ् 'to fly' (I. 1017. IV. 27), as शयिता, उड्डयिता ॥

(6) All roots in long क् are सेद, as लविता, पविता from लु and पु ॥

(7) All monosyllabic roots in short उ are Anit, except, रुङ् 'to sound' (II. 24, I. 1008), स्तु 'to flow' (II. 29), श्रु 'to sound' (II. 27), पु 'to mix' (II. 23) तु 'to praise' (II. 26), क्षणु 'to sharpen', (II. 28); and कर्णुम् 'to cover' (II. 30, though consisting of more than one syllable, is treated like तु for the purposes of यङ्) ॥ Thus रविता, प्रसविता, शयिता, यविता, नविता, क्षणविता and प्रोणविता ॥

Of the roots ending in consonants, all are सेद except the following:—

*Kārikā*:—इति स्वरान्ता निपुणैः समुचितास्ततो हलन्तानपि सन्निबोधतः ।

शक्तिस्तु कान्तेष्वनिडेक इष्यते पसिञ्च सान्तेषु वासः प्रसारणी ॥

रमिस्तु मान्तेष्वय मैथुने यभिस्ततस्तुमीयोलभिरेवनेते ॥

यमिर्मन्तेप्यनिदेक इष्यते रमिष यत्र दयनि पश्यते मनिः ।
ननिषतुर्यो हनिरेव पञ्चमो गमिष षष्ठः प्रतिषेधवाचिनाम् ॥
विहिर्दुर्हिर्महतिरोहती वहिर्महिस्तु षष्ठो दहतिरस्थया लिङ् ।
इमे उनिर्दाद्याविह मुक्तसंशया गणेषु हान्ताः प्रविभज्य कीर्तिताः ॥
विधि दुधि वशिमयो दुधि स्वधि विधि वधि क्रोधतिमहने विधिम् ।
लिङ् च शान्ताननिदः पुराणगाः पठनिं पादेषु वशेव नेतराम् ॥
रुधिः सराधिर्दुधिबन्धिसाधयः कुधिषुधी युष्यतियुष्यतो व्यधिः ।
इमे तु धान्ता दश येऽनिदो मतास्ततः परं सिद्धातिरेव नेतरे ॥
विधि विधि युष्यतियुष्यती विधि विधि निलधि युष्यतियुष्यती विधिम् ।
इमान्देवोपविशन्त्यनिद्विधो गणेषु धान्तान्कुधिषुधी तथा ॥
तपि तिथि चापिमयो वापि स्वपि तिथि युषि युष्यति युष्यती युषिम् ।
स्वरेण नीचेन वापि युषि विधि प्रतीहि पान्तान्पठितांख्योपश ॥
आदि हदि स्कन्धिभिर्विच्छिद्विधुवीन् वापि सादि स्वियातिपथाती खिदिम् ।
तुवि युषि विधातिविन्त इष्यपि प्रतीहि शान्तान्दश पञ्च चानिदः ॥
पथि वधि विचिरिचिरिञ्जितयुष्यतीन् निधि विधि युषिभजिमिञ्जितयुष्यतीन् ।
व्यजि यजि युजिरिजिसिञ्जितयुष्यतीन् युजि स्वजिसिञ्जितयुषी विद्वधनिरस्वराम् ॥

(1.) क—शक् 'to be able' (IV. 78, V. 15). शक्ता, शक्ष्यति

(2.) स—पस् 'to eat' (I. 747, and also substitute of अद्), as, पस्ता; वस् 'to dwell' (I. 1054), as वस्ता ॥ The वस् which takes Samprasāraṇa by VI. 1. 15, is meant here, and not वस् 'to cover' (II. 13), which does not vocalise, as वसिता वस्त्राणाम्, but वधितः from वस् 'to dwell' (VII. 2. 52).

(3.) म्—Three roots: रम् 'to desire' (I. 1023), as, आराध्या, यम् 'coire' (I. 1029), याध्या, लम् 'to take' (I. 1024), लाध्या ॥

(4.) म्—Four roots, यम् 'to cease' (I. 1033), यन्ता; रम् 'to play' (I. 906) रन्ता, नम् 'to bow' (I. 867, 1030) नन्ता, गन्त 'to go' (I. 1031) गन्ता ॥

5. म्—Two roots नम् 'to think' (IV. 67), मन्ता, हम् 'to kill' (II. 2), हन्ता ॥ The Divādi नम् should be taken, otherwise मनिता from मन्—मनुते (VIII. 9).

(6.) ह्—Eight roots:—विह् 'to smear' (II. 5), देह्या; दुह् 'to milk' (II. 4), दोह्या; निह् 'to sprinkle' (I. 1041) मीहा, रुह् 'to grow' (I. 912) रोहा; वह् 'to carry' (I. 1053) वोहा, नम् 'to bind' (IV. 57) नद्धा; इह् 'to burn' (I. 1041) इध्या, लिङ् 'to lick' (II. 6) लेइहा ॥ In other collections सह् (I. 905, IV. 20), मुह् (IV. 89), रिह् (VI. 23), लुह् (?), are also enumerated; of these सह् takes इह् optionally before affixes beginning with त, so also मुह् because it belongs to the class of बधादि (VII. 2. 45) the other two are not found (?) in root-collections, hence the Kārika uses the words मुक्तसंशयः ॥

(7.) श्—Ten roots:—विश्व 'to show' (VI. 3), दृश 'to see' (I. 1037), दश 'to bite' (I. 1038), दृश 'to rub' (VI. 131), स्वश 'to touch' (VI. 128), रिश्व (VI. 126), रुश्व (VI. 126) both meaning 'to hurt', विश्व 'to enter' (VI. 130), लिश्व 'to be small' (IV. 70, VI. 127). As देहा, ब्रह्मा, देहा, आभ्रहा or आभ्रहा, स्वहा or स्वहा, The roots with a penultimate क् short, which are anudatta in the dhātupāṭha, with the exception of भृज् and दृश, take optionally the augment रम् (VI. 1. 59), ॥ रेहा, रोहा, क्रोहा, प्रेहा, लेहा ॥

(8.) पू—Ten roots:—इपू with अनु, 'to love', इपू 'to obstruct' (IV. 65) रोजा, राप 'to accomplish' (IV. 71, V. 16) राजा; युप 'to fight' (IV. 64) योद्धा; बन्ध 'to bind' (I. 1022), बन्धा; साध 'to accomplish' (V. 17) साधा; कुपू 'to be angry' (IV. 80) कोद्धा, युप 'to be hungry' (IV. 81) शोद्धा; युप 'to be pure' (IV. 82) शोद्धा, युप 'to be aware' (IV. 63) बोद्धा; व्यप 'to pierce' (IV. 72) व्यप; सिप 'to be accomplished' (IV. 83) सेपा ॥ The roots युप and सिप are exhibited in the above Kārikā with यप, vikarana (बुद्धति, सिद्धति); therefore युप and सिप take इद in other ganas than the Fourth; as बोधिता and सेधिता ॥ There being want of prohibition with regard to निष्ठा, we have बुधिते and सिधिते ॥

(9.) पू—roots. 11. The augment इद is not added to an affix having an indicatory क्, when it comes after the root श्रि, or after a monosyllabic root ending in उ, ऊ, ऋ or ऋ in the Dhātupāṭha.

As श्रित्वा, श्रितः, श्रितवान् ॥ So also with roots ending in उक् vowels: as युत्वा, युतः, युतवान्; युत्वा, युतः, युतवान्; युत्वा, युतः, युतवान्; तीर्त्वा, तीर्गः, तीर्गवान् ॥

Why 'श्रि and उक् ending roots only'? Observe श्रित्वा ॥ Why having an indicatory क्? Observe श्रित्वा, श्रितुम्, श्रितव्यम् ॥ Some read two क्'s in the sūtra and would apply it to the indicatory ग् also, as भृश् (III. 2. 139).

This rule applies to those roots, which have not been enumerated above. In the case of यु the Nishṭhā will not take इद even by VII. 2. 49 read with VII. 2. 15.

When two क् are read in the sūtra, one standing for ग्; there arises a little difficulty of combination. Thus ग् coming after the visarga of उक् would require that the visarga be changed to उ by VI. 1. 114. If ग् be changed to ऋ (VIII. 4. 55) then also, the visarga required to be changed into upadhmaniya by VIII. 3. 37. If the change of ग् into ऋ (VIII. 4. 55) be considered asiddha

(VIII. 2. 1.), then also the visarga must be changed to उ (VI. 1. 114), and the sūtra should be अपकोकिति ॥ This, however, is not done as an anomaly allowable in sūtra construction. According to Kāsikā, this difficulty would not at all arise, if in the sūtra ग्लाजिस्यबकस्तु (III. 2. 139), the स्था+भा be taken as compounded into स्था; so that that rule would apply to that स्था which ends in भा, and not to that स्था whose final is changed to ई; so that the form स्थास्तु: is evolved without anomaly : and the affix will be किंतु (कस्तु) and not गित् (गस्तु). The affix being किंतु, the above sandhi difficulty will not arise at all.

The word उपदेश is understood here also, so that the rule will apply to roots which end in उक् vowel, in their original states and not to the transformed base before the affix. Thus तु is a उक्-ending root, which is transformed to सीर before the Nishtha त ॥ The rule will apply to it, as तीर्थः ॥ If you object saying, that तु ends in long भ् and its Desiderative optionally takes इद by VII. 2. 41, and therefore, its Nishtha will always take no इद by VII. 2. 15. we reply, that the option taught in VII. 2. 41 applies to roots ending in long भ्; but when the root vowel is changed to ई, it is no longer a भ्-ending root. If you say, the rule of sthānivad bhāva will apply : we say, that that rule is not applicable to अल् विधि, and this is an अल्विधि ॥ Therefore, the word उपदेश should be read into this sūtra. If this be so, the rule ought to apply to आप्, and we could not get the forms जागरितः and जागरितवान् ॥ To explain this we should also read the anuvritti of एकान् into this sūtra. The root ऊर्ध्व, however is an exception and is governed by this rule, in spite of its consisting of more than one vowel. Thus प्रार्थितः and प्रार्थितवान् ॥

Kārikā :—ऊर्ध्व is treated as if it was तु, when the affix यह is to be applied, आप् is to be prohibited, or इद is to be debarred.

As जिपृशति, जुपृशति, रुरुपति, लुप्पति ॥ The anuvritti of भि is not drawn into this sūtra, as option is allowed regarding it by VII. 2. 49. यह would always get इद, गुह (I. 944) being ऊदित् (in the Dhātupāṭha), would have optionally taken इद (VII. 2. 44)

The forms जिपृशति and जुपृशति are thus evolved :—यह+सन् (the affix is किंतु by I. 2. 8) = गुह+सन् (VI. 1. 16) = गुह+सन् (VIII. 2. 31) = गुह+सन् (VIII. 2. 41) = जिपृशति (VIII. 2. 37). So also with गुह संवरणे, the सन् is किंतु here by I. 2. 10.

13. The Personal endings of the Perfect do not get the augment इद, after क्, सु, भु, वु, स्तु, हु, सु, भु ॥

Thus क्—चक्रव, चक्रव; सु, ससुव, ससुन; भु, बभव, बभन; वृभ, ववुव, ववुन; वृह, ववुवहे, ववुनहे; स्तु, तुदुव, तुदुन; हु, तुदुव, तुदुन; भु; सुभुव, सुभुन; भु; शुभुव, शुभुन ॥ सिजे सत्वारम्भो नियमार्थः, क्रावय एव लिखानिरस्ततोऽये सेद इति ॥

These roots with the exception of वृ are Aniṭ by rule VII. 2. 10; their special mention here is for the sake of niyama, namely, these roots alone are Aniṭ in the Perfect, other roots are all Set in the Perfect. Thus बिभिबि, बिभिबिम, लुलुबिम, लुलुबिम ॥ All anudatta roots of the Dhātupāṭha are to be understood, by this rule, to get इद ॥ The affix य of the Perfect gets इद after वृभ, as the irregular form ववर्थ in VII. 2. 64, indicates that in the Veda, य does not get इद after वृभ, but in the secular literature it does. By VII. 2. 63, the य would have got इद after स्तु, हु, सु and भु; that इद is also prohibited by the present sūtra. As तुदोय, तुदोय, सुभोय, सुभोय ॥

Vārt:—इद is added when क् takes the सुद् augment: as संचस्करिव, संचस्करिम ॥ The rule VII. 2. 63, applies here also, as संचस्करिय ॥

14. The Participial affixes त and तवत् (kta and ktavatu), do not get the इद augment after भि, and after the root which has an indicatory ई ॥

As शूनः, शूनवान; ओलेजी (VI. 10),—लम, लमवान्; ओविजी (VI. 9), उद्भिः, उद्भिमवान् ॥ The त is changed to न because of the indicatory ओ (VIII. 2. 45). So also वीवी (IV. 42), वीवः, वीववान् ॥ In the Dhātupāṭha, वीव (IV. 27), is classed among ओवित् roots, and it indicates that the Nishthā is anit after it: and ओ is for न-change (VIII. 2. 45) as, उद्भीनः उद्भीनवान् ॥ The word निष्ठायाम् governs the following sūtras upto VII. 2. 35.

15. The Participial-affixes do not take इद, after those roots, to which another suffix can optionally be added, with or without this augment इ ॥

That is, a root which is optionally Set before other affixes, is invariably anit before Nishthā. Thus by VII. 2. 44, वल consonant beginning affixes are optionally सेद after the roots भू &c. The Nishthā after भू &c, will be invariably anit. Thus विभूतः, विभूनवान्; गृहः, गृहवान् ॥ By VII. 2. 56, the roots having an indicatory उ, optionally are followed by Sst क्त ॥ The Nishthā after उदित् roots will invariably be anit: as वृक्षः, वृक्षवान् ॥

By the *vārtika* तानि पति शशिताणामुपसख्यानम् the roots तन्, पत and शशिता take optional ईद in the Desiderative (VII. 2. 49). Though पत् is a root which thus *optionally* takes ईद in the Desiderative, yet its Nishthā is always सेद, for Pāṇini himself has employed the word पतित in Sūtra II. 1. 24, 38. According to Padamanjari this rule of यस्य विभाषा is anitya and not of universal application. Because had this rule been of universal application then the root कृत which is *optionally* anit by VII. 2. 57, would be *universally* anit by the present sūtra: and there would be no necessity of reading it with a long ई in the Dhātupāṭha, as कृती छेदने (VI. 141) to make its nishthā anit under VII. 2. 14.

16. The Participial-affixes do not get ईद augment after a root which has an indicatory आ ॥

As भिमिदा—मित्रः, मित्रवान्; भिमिदा—क्षिपणः, क्षिपणवान्; भिमिदा—स्वित्रः, स्वित्रवान् ॥ The च implies that other roots not enumerated are to be also included, as आश्चरतः, वान्तः ॥

This and the sūtra following it could have been made into one, as आदितश्च विभाषा भावादिकर्मणोः ॥ The separate making of two sūtras indicates that the rule of यस्य विभाषा (VII. 2. 15), applies with the restrictions and limitations of the rule ordaining 'option', i.e., the prohibition of ईद augment, with regard to the participial-affixes is limited by the same conditions, which apply to the optional employment of ईद before other affixes in the विभाषा rules (यदुपाधेर्विभाषा, तदुपाधेः प्रतिषेधः) ॥ Thus VII. 2. 68 ordains ईद optionally to the affix वसु after the roots गम्, हम्, विद् and विश् ॥ The root विद् there is the Tudādi root meaning 'to acquire'. The rule यस्य विभाषा will apply to this विद् with this meaning: and not to विद् meaning 'to know', the Past Participles of which are विदितः, विदितवान् ॥

विभाषा भावादिकर्मणोः ॥ १७ ॥ पदानि ॥ विभाषा, भाव, आदिकर्मणोः ॥

17. The participial affixes after roots having an indicatory आ, may optionally take the augment ईद, when the affixes have an Impersonal sense, or denote the beginning of an action.

Thus मित्रमनेन or मेदितमनेन, प्रमित्रः, प्रमेदितः ॥ The Saunāgas optionally make the Nishthā set after the root शक्, when the affix has a Passive significance even, as शकितो घटः कर्तुम् or शक्तोः घटः कर्तुम् ॥ Not so, when the affix has Impersonal force, as शकमनन ॥ The root अस् 'to throw' (अस्यति), is followed by सेद् Nishthā, when the sense is Impersonal: as असितमनन; but not when the beginning of action is meant, as असतः काण्डः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ ध्रुवः स्वान्तः ध्वान्तः लग्नः मिष्ठः विरिच्छः फाण्डः वादः इलेते निपातन्ते यथासम्बन्धे मन्थः मनस्तमः सक्ताविस्पष्टः स्वानायासभूश इलेते व्ययेषु ॥

18. The following words are made without इद augment in the senses given against them :—

1. ध्रुवः 'a churning stick', 2. स्वान्तः 'the mind', 3. ध्वान्तः 'darkness', 4. लग्नः 'attached', 5. मिष्ठः 'indistinct or unintelligible', 6. विरिच्छः 'a note or tone', 7. फाण्डः 'made without an effort or by an easy process', and 8. वादः 'excessive'.

When the words have not the above sense, we have 1. ध्रुवितं 'disturbed or agitated'. The phrase ध्रुवो गिरिः or नदी is a metaphorical use of the word. 2. स्वनितः as स्वनितो ध्रुवः, स्वनितं मनसा ॥ 3. ध्वनितो ध्रुवः or ध्वनितं मनसा ॥ 4. लगितं, 5. लेलेच्छतं, (= अपभायितं) 6. विरभितं from रेश 'to sound', or विरभितं from रिभि ॥ 7. फाणितं ॥ फाण्डः is a decoction, prepared without much trouble, by simply slightly heating the substance with some water, without powdering or pasting it. (यदधृतमपिष्टं च कषायधृक् संपर्कमाचाह् विभक्तसमीपदुष्पां) a medicine for any disease may be administered in five forms :—रसः or essence, कल्कः paste or powder, वृत्तः decoction or extract, शीतः cold extract prepared by throwing pounded drugs into cold water, and keeping that all night to soak. This watery extract, to be drunk in the morning, is so called. फाण्डः is a similar hot preparation, but for immediate use, when the drugs are put in boiling water and the decoction after purification is ready for use as a drink. 8. वाहितं from बाह् 'to strive'.

ध्रुविशसी वैयाल्ये ॥ १९ ॥ पदानि ॥ ध्रुवः, शसी, वैयाल्ये, ॥
वृत्तिः ॥ विधातस्य भावो वैयाल्यम्, प्रागल्भ्यभविनीतता ॥ तत्र ध्रुवः शस इलेते योनिष्ठायामिजागमो न भवति ॥

19. The Participial affix does not get इद augment, after the roots ध्रुव and शस, when meaning 'bold, impudent and arrogant'.

As ध्रुवः, विशस्तः ॥ The root ध्रुव is exhibited in the Dhātupāṭha as भिक्षुषा 'to be impudent' (V. 2. 2), and as it has an indicatory आ, its past participle would be अनिद्र by VII. 2. 16. शस is शषु in the Dhātupāṭha (I. 763), and as it has an indicatory इ by VII. 2. 56. read with VII. 2. 15, its Nishthā is also Anit. The special mention of these roots here, is for the sake of making a niyama rule: namely, अनिद्र only then when meaning 'impudent', and सद् in other senses : as पार्थितः, विशस्तितः 'ध्रुव never forms past participle with the force of भाव (Impersonal action) or भाविकर्म (beginning of action), and therefore VII. 2. 17 cannot apply to it'—This is Kāśikā. According to Bhattoji Dikshit who

BK. VII. CH. II. §. 21 ] IRREGULAR PARTICIPLES.

1369

quotes Haradatta and Mādhava, ध्रुव forms participles in those senses, when option is allowed, as, ध्रुव or भर्तित, मधुरः or प्रपर्तितः not meaning 'impudent'.

दृढः स्थूलबलयोः ॥ २० ॥ पदानि ॥ दृढः, स्थूल, बलयोः, ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ दृढ इति निपात्यते स्थूल बलवति चाये ॥

20. The irregularly formed Past Participle दृढ means 'stout' and 'strong'.

It is derived from दृढ with न affix. In other senses, the forms are दृढितम् or दृढितम् ॥ There are two roots one दृढ (I. 769) without nasal, and the other दृढ (I. 770) with the nasal. दृढ can be derived from any one of these by eliding दृ, and the nasal, and changing न to द, and not adding the augment दृढ ॥

The difference between स्थूल and बल is that a man may be stout or स्थूल without being strong (बलवान्) and vice versa. The word बल in the sūtra is equal to बलवान्; in fact, the word बल is formed by अच् affix. The irregularity in the formation of दृढ consists in the absence of दृढ and the elision of ह (and of न, if the root दृढ be taken) : and the change of न into द ॥ This irregular elision of ह is for the sake of preventing the application of the rule पूर्ववर्तिम् (VIII. 2. 1). The form could have been obtained in the regular way by the elision of द, thus: दृढ+न=दृढ+न (VIII. 2. 31) = दृढ+ध=दृढ+द=द+द (VIII. 3. 13) = दृढ ॥ But then when द is elided, the rule पूर्ववर्तिम् will apply, and the forms दृढिना, दृढीयान्, दृढयति could not be obtained. For क् is changed to र by VI. 4. 161 only when it is laghu or light, but द-lopa being considered asiddha, the क् would be heavy as standing before a conjunct consonant. So also the form परिदृढव्याऽगतः could not be obtained : for the णि would not be changed to अच् before ल्यप when the क् is not light or laghu (VI. 4. 56). So also, परिदृढव्यापत्यं=परिदृढी (the daughter of Paridṛḍha) could not be formed. For क् being considered guru or heavy, the affix प्यङ् would have come in the feminine (IV. 1. 78).

प्रभौ परिवृढः ॥ २१ ॥ पदानि ॥ प्रभौ, परिवृढः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ परिवृढ इति निपात्यते प्रभुञ्जवति ॥

21. The irregularly formed परिवृढ means 'Lord'.

This is formed, like दृढ, from दृढ or दृढ ॥ When not having the sense of 'Lord', we have परिवृद्धितम् and परिवृद्धितम् ॥

The ह is elided first as an anomaly. By so doing we can get the forms like परिवृद्धयति, परिवृद्धव्यागतः; परिवृद्धीकन्या ॥ The form परिवृद्धव्यागतः is formed by ल्यप् instead of ktvā ॥ Though the full noun is परिवृढ and णिच् is added to such a noun, yet for the purposes of ktvā it is considered as a compound verb, having परि as upasarga. In fact, णिच् is added to दृढ, and the root becomes द्रढि, and then ktvā is added to this root, and then there is compounding of परि with this word ending in ktvā, and then by the regular process the ktvā is replaced by ल्यप् ॥ The general rule is that Derivative roots formed from nouns, like परिवृढ, उद्गनस, घुमनस &c which have an upasarga as one of their formative elements,

1370

ई. AUGMENT.

[ Bk. VII. Ch. II. §. 23

are treated as if they were compound verbs having those upasargas. The result of this is, that though the full noun is **धुमनम्**, yet in the derivative verb, **धु** will be treated as an upasarga, as in ordinary compound verbs. Thus the augment **ध** in the Imperfect is added after **धु** and not before it, as **स्वमनायत**, **वद-मनायत** ॥ The rule is **उपसर्गसमानाकारं पूर्वपदं धातुसंज्ञाप्रयोजके प्रत्ययं चिकीर्षिते पृथक् क्रियते** ॥ The Participial form of these words is therefore with **स्वप्** and not **स्वा**, as **धुमनाध्य** and **उन्मनाध्य** ॥ The only exception to this rule is the noun **संभाम**, in which the upasarga **सम्** is not considered as a separate member in the Derivative verb. This being the general rule, in **परिव्रतयति** the portion **परि** is treated as an upasarga, and **व्रतयति** as the verb and its accent is governed by **तिङ् तिङ्** (VIII. I. 28) i. e. it becomes altogether unaccented and **परि** retains its accent. So also **परिव्रतय**, where is **परि** is compounded with the Participial form **व्रतिवा**, and then **स्वा** is changed to **स्वप्** by VII. I. 37.

कुञ्जगहनयोः कषः ॥ २२ ॥ पदानि ॥ कुञ्ज, गहनयोः, कषः, ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ कुञ्ज गहन इत्येतयोर्यथोः कषेऽर्जातोनिष्ठायामिडागमो न भवति ॥

22. The Participial affix does not take the augment **इद्** after the root **कष**, when the participle means 'difficult' and 'impenetrable'.

As **कष्टोऽभिः**, कष्ट व्याकरणं, ततोऽपि कष्टतरणिसामानि ॥ 'Difficult is Fire-sacrifice i. e. it is difficult to completely master the ritual connected with the worship of fire; and difficult enough is Grammar, but the Sāmāns are worst of all'. **कष्टानि वनानि** 'impervious forests.' **कष्टाः पर्वताः** ॥ When not having these senses, we have **कषितं सुवर्णम्** ॥

धुषिरविश्वद्वने ॥ २३ ॥ पदानि ॥ धुषिः, अविश्वद्वने ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ धुषेऽर्जातोरविश्वद्वने यं निष्ठायामिडागमो न भवति ॥

23. The Participial affix does not take the augment **इद्**, after the root **धुष** in any sense other than that of 'proclaimed'.

As **धुष्टा रञ्जुः**, **धुष्टो पादौ** but **अवधुषितं वाक्यमाह** ॥ **विश्वद्वन** = **प्रतिज्ञानम्** 'assertion, affirmation, agreement'. **धुषिर अविश्वद्वने** is Bhvādi (I. 683), and **धुषिर विश्वद्वने** is Churādi (X. 187), both of these are referred to in the sūtra. The prohibition of **विश्वद्वन** in the sūtra, indicates by jñāpaka that the **णिच्** added to the root in the Churādi class in the sense of **विश्वद्वन** is anitya. So the following construction becomes valid:—as **महीपालवचः शून्वा जुधुषुः पुष्पमाणवाः** 'expressed their opinions in words'.

In short the **णिच्** is optionally added to the **धुषिर** of the Churādi class.

Some say the Churādi **णिच्** is anitya generally and not only after **धुषिर** (अभित्य व्यन्ताऽचुरादयः) ॥ This is inferred from the mention of the root **चिति स्मृखाम्** (X. 2) in this class. The indicatory **इ** in **चिति** shows that the augment

BK. VII. CH. II. §. 27 ]

इद AUGMENT.

1371

वृत्त will be added to the root, which will thus become चिन्त and this न will be retained throughout and never dropped. ( VII. 1. 48 ). Now had the चिन्त been nitya, then the root ought to have been taught as चिन्त स्युत्थान, because no rule would have caused the elision of the न of चिन्त when चिन्त was added. The enunciation of the root as चिन्ति, therefore, indicates that the churādi चिन्त is anitya, and thus we get the forms like चिन्तिनः, चिन्त्यान्, चिन्त्यते, चिन्तति, चिन्तेन &c.

As अभ्यर्णा सेना, अभ्यर्णा शत्रु ॥ Why 'when meaning near' ? See अभ्यर्थिनो
वृषतः शीतेन meaning पीडितः ॥ विदुरे means 'remote,' that which is not remote is आवि-
हुरे 'non-remote,' the state of being non-remote is आविदुर्ये 'non-remote-ness.' The

णेरध्ययने वृत्तम् ॥ २६ ॥ पदानि ॥ णेः, अभ्ययने, वृत्तम्, ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ ण्यन्तस्य वृत्तेर्निद्यायामध्ययनार्थे वृत्तमिनीडमादो णिलुक् च निपातते ॥

26. The word वृत्त is formed from the causative of वृत्त, in the sense of 'studied through or read.'

There is absence of इद and luk-clusion of the causative sign. As वृत्तो
युणो देववृत्तेन 'Devadatta has read or gone through Gupta.' (युणः पाठः पश्यन्तवृत्तिना
रूपोऽध्ययनविशेषः) ॥ वृत्तं पारायणं देववृत्तेन ॥ When the sense is not that of 'read', we
have वृत्तिनम् ॥ The root वृत्त is intransitive, and becomes Transitive when
employed in the Causative. The participle is formed from this Transitive
causative verb, otherwise it could not have governed an object as shown above.
"The affix ऋ is added with a Passive force to वृत्त, as we find the author himself
using this form in निर्दुत्तम in sūtras IV. 2. 68, and V. 1. 79; on the analogy of
निर्दुत्त the word वृत्त: could also have been formed without this sūtra."

27. The following irregularly formed Participles, from the causative roots, may optionally take इद, namely, दान्त, शान्त, पूर्ण, दन्त, स्पष्ट, छन्न, छन्न ॥

These words are formed either from the causative base or from the primary roots इद &c. The other forms are इमितः, शमितः, पूरितः, शासितः, शाश्वितः, छावितः and झपितः ॥ The words दान्त &c. are formed by the luk-elision of णि (Causative), and not taking the इद Augment. By VII. 2. 49 इद optionally is सेद and, therefore, by VII. 2. 15, its Participle would have been *always* अनिद्, hence, this sutra makes an option.

रुष्यमत्वरसंघुपास्वनाम ॥ २८ ॥ पदानि ॥ रुषि, अम, त्वर, संधुप, आस्वनाम ॥
वृत्तिः ॥ वेति वचते । रुषि अम त्वर संधुप आस्वन इत्येतेषां निष्ठायां वा इडागमो न भवति ॥

28. The Participial affix may optionally get इद augment, after रुष, अम, त्वर, संधुप, and आस्वन ॥

As रुषः or रुषितः ॥ By VII. 2. 48, the affixes after रुष are *optionally* सेद, and therefore by VII. 2. 15, the Nishtha after this verb would have been *always* anit; hence this optional rule. अभ्यान्तः or अभ्यनितः, पूर्णः or त्वरितः ॥ The त्वर is exhibited in the Dhātupātha as भिखरा (I. 812) i. e. with an indicatory long आ, and hence by VII. 2. 16. would have been anit always, this rule makes it optionally anit. So also, संधुटो पावो, or संधुधितो पावो, संधुटे or संधुधितं वाक्यमाह, संधुटो or संधुधितो वच्यो ॥ धुव preceded by सम् will be optionally anit, even when having any sense other than that of 'proclaimed', as this *subsequent* sutra supersedes VII. 2. 23 so far. So also आस्वान्तः or आस्वनितो देववत्तः, आस्वान्तम् or आस्वनितं मनः ॥ त्वम् when preceded by आ, though denoting 'mind,' is *optionally* anit, in spite of VII. 2. 18, that rule being superseded so far by this *subsequent* rule.

वृत्तिः ॥ लोमसु वचैमानस्य हृषेनिष्ठायां वा इडागमो न भवति ॥
वार्तिकम् ॥ विस्मितमतिघातयोश्चेति वक्तव्यम् ॥

29. The Participial affix optionally takes इद, after इप when the word लोमन or its synonym is in construction with it.

As हृतानि लोमानि or हृषितानि लोमानि; हृताः केशाः or हृषिताः केशाः; हृतं or हृषितं लोमभिः or केशैः ॥ हृषु 'to lie' (I. 741) is exhibited with an indicatory उ in the Dhātupātha, and would have been consequently *always* anit, in the Nishtha (VII. 2. 15) because it was optionally anit before ktvā (VII. 2. 56) hence this rule. हृषु 'to be delighted' (IV. 119) is also included here, this verb is सेद ॥ The option appertains to both these verbs. The word लोम means the hair of the body as well as of the head: as in the sentence लोमनस्य सृष्ट्वा शौचं कर्तव्यम् ॥ The sense of हृष in connection with लोम will be that of bristling up, horipillation. Why do

अपचितश्च ॥ ३० ॥ पदानि ॥ अपचितः, च, ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ किनि नित्यमिति वक्तव्यम् ॥

30. And अपचित has also a second form with the augment इ ॥

The word अपचित is formed with the preposition अप added to the root चाय (I. 929) ‘to honor, to fear, to see’ and चाय changed irregularly to चि before क् ॥ The other form is अपचायितः, as अपचितो or अपचायितो ऽनेनगुरुः ‘the teacher is feared by him’. This example is given when the sense is that of ‘fear’; when the word means ‘honor’, then the participle must govern the genitive case, as required by III. 2. 188.

Vārt:—Before किन्तु affix, चाय is always changed to चि, as अपचितिः ‘Loss, destruction, showing reverence’. The affix किन्तु is added to चाय, by considering it as belonging to the class of आप् &c. See III. 3. 94 Vārt. Otherwise it would take the affix अ by III. 3. 103.

हु हरेऽछन्दसि ॥ ३१ ॥ पदानि ॥ हु हरेः, छन्दसि ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ हरेतर्ज्ञातोर्निष्ठायां छन्दसि हु इत्ययमादेशो भवति ।

31. हु is substituted for हर (I. 978) in the Veda, before the Participial-affix.

As हुतस्य चाहुतस्य च, आहुतमसि हविर्धानम् (Vaj San. I. 9). But हुतम् in secular literature.

अपरिहृदुताश्च ॥ ३२ ॥ पदानि ॥ अपरिहृदुताः, च ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अपरिहृदुता इति निपात्यते छन्दसि विषये । हु इत्येतस्यादेशस्याभावो निपात्यते ।

32. The word ‘aparihvṛtā’ is irregularly formed in the Veda.

The हु substitution required by the last sūtra, does not take place here. As अपरिहृदुताः सतुयाम वाजम् (Rig I. 100. 19).

सोमे हरितः ॥ ३३ ॥ पदानि ॥ सोमे, हरितः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ हरित इति हरतेर्निष्ठायामिडागमो गुणश्च निपात्यते छन्दसि विषये, सोमश्चेञ्चति ।

33. हरित is irregularly formed from हु in the Veda, by guna substitution and इद augment, when it refers to Soma.

As मा नः सोमो हरितो, विहरितस्त्वम् ॥

34. In the Veda, the following irregular forms are found, some with, and some without the augment इट—1 grasita, 2 skabhita, 3 stabhita, 4 uttabhita, 5 chatta, 6 vikasta, 7 viśastri, 8 śanstri, 9 śāstri, 10 tarutri, 11 tarūtri, 12 varutri, 13 varūtri, 14 varūtrih, 15 ujjvaliti, 16 kshariti, 17 kshamiti, 18 vamiti and 19 amiti.

Of the above nineteen words, 1, 2, 3, and 4 are from roots यमु, 'to swallow' (I. 661) स्कम्सु 'to stop' (I. 414) and स्तम्सु (I. 413) all having an indicatory उ, and therefore by VII. 2. 56 read with VII. 2. 15, their Nishthā would not have taken इट ॥ Thus असित (ver. अस्त) वा एतत् सोमस्य ॥ विक्रमिते अजरे (=विक्रम्य); येन स्वस्तमितम् (=स्तम्य), सत्येनोत्तमिता भूमिः (=उत्तम्य:) ॥ The irregularity is only with the preposition उत्, with other prepositions, the form स्तमित is not employed. Similarly (5) चत्ता (=चत्तिता) वर्षेण विश्रुत् from चते याचने ॥ (6) उत्तानाया हुव्यं यद् विकस्तम् (=विकसितम्) The forms, 7, 8, and 9 are from the roots यमु हिंसायाम् and यमु स्तुतो, and यमु अनुशिती with the affix तृच् and no augment; as एकस्वदुरभस्याविशस्ता (=विशसिता), उत् शस्ता सुविप्रः (=शसिता), प्रशास्ता (=प्रशासितम्) ॥ The forms 10, 11, 12, 13 and 14 are from the roots तु and वु (वृह् and वृह्), with the affix तृच्, and the augment उद् and उद् ॥ As तरुतारं or तरुतारं रथानाम् (=तरितारम् or तरितारम्), वरुतारम् or वरुतारम् रथानाम् (=वरितारम् or वरीतारम्); वरुचीद्वा वैवीविश्ववैष्यावती ॥ वरुचीः is exhibited in this form of Nom. pl. of the feminine वरुची merely for the sake of showing one form in which it is found: another form is अहोशावार्णं वेवरुचयः ॥ Here the plural is formed irregularly, by taking the word as वरुचि ॥ The feminine form could have been easily obtained from वरुतु, by adding क्रीष्, the special mention is explanatory. The rest 15, 16, 17, 18 and 19 are from उत्-उत्पल, शर, क्षम, वम्, and अम, formed with the vikaraṇa शप् and the affix of the 3rd Per Sing तिष्, इ being substituted for क्ष् of शप्, or शप् is elided and the augment इट is added ॥ As अग्निरुज्ज्वलितं (=उ-ज्ज्वलितं), स्तामं क्षमितं (=क्षमति), स्ताकं क्षमितं (=क्षमति), यः सोनं वमितं (=वमति), अभ्यमितं वरुणः (=अभ्यमति) ॥ Sometimes we have अभ्यमात, as राघमभ्यमितं ॥

आर्जेधातुकस्येद्वलादेः ॥ ३५ ॥ पदादि ॥ आर्जेधातुकस्य, इट, वलादेः ॥
वृत्तिः ॥ छन्दसीति निवृत्तम् । आर्जेधातुकस्य वलादिरिडागमो भवति ।

35. An *ārdhadhātuka* affix (III. 4. 114 &c) beginning with a consonant (except य), gets the augment इद (in these rules).

Thus लबिता, लबितुम्, लबितव्यम्, पविता, पवितुम्, पवितव्यम् ॥ Why 'ārdhadhā-tuka'? Observe आस्ते, वस्ते ॥ The niyama rule of VII. 2. 76 ordaining इद augment to *sārvadhātuka* affixes of Rudādi verbs, would prevent इद augment before *sārvadhātuka* affixes when coming after other roots. The employment of *ārdhadhātuka* here can be dispensed with. Why before affixes beginning with a वल-consonant? Observe लव्यम्, पव्यम्, लवनीयम्, पवनीयम् ॥ Though the anuvritti of इद was understood here, its repetition is for the sake of preventing the prohibition of the foregoing *sūtras* like VII. 2. 8.

स्तुकमोरनात्मनेपदनिमित्ते ॥ ३६ ॥ पदानि ॥ स्तु, क्रमोः, अनात्मनेपदनिमित्ते ॥
वृत्तिः ॥ नियमाधिमिवम् । स्तुकमोराद्वैधातुकस्य वलादिरिदागमो भवति, न चेत्स्तुकमो आरम्भनेपदस्य निमित्ते भवतः ।

वार्तिकम् ॥ क्रमस्तु कर्तव्यात्मनेपदविव्यावस्थात्मनेपदे कृति प्रतिषेधो वक्तव्यः ॥

36. The augment इद is added to *ārdhadhātuka* valādi affixes after स्तु and क्रम, only then when they do not occasion the taking of the Personal endings of the Atmanepada.

The roots स्तु and क्रम are udātta, and will get इद augment naturally, the *sūtra* makes a restriction or *niyama*. The restriction is that when the roots themselves occasion atmanepada affixes, then they do not take इद, otherwise they will.

When do roots give occasion to Atmanepada affixes? The roots occasion atmanepada affixes when employed in the Impersonal, Passive, and Intensive senses. Sutras I. 3. 38-43, teach us when क्रम takes Atmanepada affixes. Thus प्रस्नाविता, प्रस्नावितुम्, प्रस्नावितव्यम्, प्रक्रमिता, प्रक्रमितुम्, प्रक्रमितव्यम् ॥ Why do we say 'when not the occasion of getting the Atmanepada affixes'? Observe, प्रस्नोषीष्ट, प्रक्रमीष्ट, प्रस्नोष्यते, प्रक्रम्यते, प्रस्नुषिष्यते, प्रक्षक्रमिष्यते ॥ In all these examples स्तु and क्रम have become the causes of taking the Atmanepada affixes. The Desiderative is also Atmanepadi because of I. 3. 62.

Why have we used the word निमित्त in the *sūtra*? Would it not have been simpler to say स्तुकमोरनात्मनेपदे? This form of *sūtra* would have indicated that whenever an atmanepada affix followed, then there would be no इद augment. Now the rule is that all words exhibited in the Locative case in this Grammar, have the force of परसन्नी, i. e. when that word *follows*. Therefore आरम्भनेपदे would mean when an atmanepada affix followed. If then this 'atmanepada' be taken as qualifying स्तु and क्रम, then it must follow *immediately* after those roots, as in प्रस्नोषीष्ट and प्रक्रमीष्ट; but we would not get the forms प्रस्नोष्यते and प्रक्रम्यते, because स intervenes between the atmanepada and the

1376

ई. AUGMENT.

[ Bk. VII. Ch. II. §. 38.

affix. On the other hand if “atmanepada” be taken to qualify the word “ardhadhātuka affix” understood, viz, if the sūtra ment स्तुकमिष्यां परस्यार्धधातुकस्यात्मनपे-उन्नत then the forms प्रस्वोध्यते and प्रकस्यते would be valid, but we should not get the forms प्रस्वोधीह and प्रकसीह, because the augment सीयुद् is a portion of the atmanepada affix, and there is no ardhdhātuka affix here. If the sūtra be taken to have both the above senses, then we could not get the form प्रचिकसिष्यते in the Desiderative, because here the atmanepada does not follow immediately after the sārvadhātuka affix that follows क्रम् ॥ Therefore, the word निमित्त should be taken. For by so doing, there takes place prohibition with regard to सायुद् &c, and also with regard to that after which comes the atmanepada, as the स्व in प्राचकसिष्यते, and also with regard to that which precedes the latter, as the सत् affix in the above. In प्रसन्नविधीयते (प्रसन्नविधीयतारात्), the root स्तु has not occasioned the atmanepada affix, but the affix क्यह्, hence the prohibition of this sūtra does not apply.

*Vārti* :—Prohibition of इद् augment should be stated with regard to क्रम् when an Krit-affix, with active force, follows not in the atmanepada, though in the Active voice such क्रम् was subject of Atmanepada. When क्रम् takes no upasargas, we have according to one view two forms क्रन्ता and क्रमिता (I. 3. 43) because the atmanepada here is optional. According to the other view there will be only one form, as क्रमता ॥ But with प्र and उप we have प्रकन्ता and उपक्रन्ता ॥ Why do we say ‘the Krit-affix should have an active force’? Observe प्रकमितव्यम्, उपक्रमितव्यम् ॥ Why do we say “when it was subject of Atmanepada”? Observe निष्क्रमिता ॥ Here there is इद् augment; for by I. 3. 42, क्रम् is subject of atmanepada, when the upasargas प्र and उप precede, but not otherwise.

With regard to स्तु, it will take no इद् in the Desiderative, and before a किल् affix, by virtue of VII. 2. 11 and 12. Therefore, we have the forms प्रहस्तुपति, प्रस्तुतः, प्रस्तुतवान् ॥

अहो अलिटि दीर्घः ॥ ३७ ॥ पदानि ॥ प्रहः, अ लिटि, दीर्घः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ प्रह उत्तरस्य इदः अलिटि दीर्घो भवति ।

As महीता, महीतुष्, महीतव्यम् ॥ Why not in the Perfect? Observe जगृहिष् जगृहिष् ॥ The lengthening takes place of the इद् taught in VII. 2. 35, and does not refer to the चिण्वद् इद् of VI. 4. 62 : as माहिता, महिष्यते ॥

वृत्तो वा ॥ ३८ ॥ पदानि ॥ वृत्तः वा ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ वृ इति वृङ् वृभोः सामान्येन महन् तस्मादुत्तरस्य कूकारान्तेभ्येदो वा दीर्घो भवति ।

41. The Desiderative स may optionally take इद (which is optionally lengthened also) after the said इ and कू ending roots.

As वुवर्षति । विवरिषते । विवरीषते । प्रावुवर्षति । प्राविवरिषति । प्राविवरीषति । कूकारान्तेभ्यः । तितीर्षति । तितरिषति । तितरीषति । आतिस्तीर्षति । This Parasmipada form is not valid, according to Padamanjari. आतिस्तरिषति । आतिस्तरीषति । सनि महमुद्रेषेति इदप्रतिषे प्राते पसे इडागनो विधीयते । इदश्च वृतो वेति पसेरीषैः । चिकीर्षति जिहीर्षति इत्वयोपदेशाधिकाराङ्गश्विकत्वाच इडागनो न भवति ॥

The इद was prohibited by VII. 2. 12, in case of the Desideratives, hence this sūtra: when इद is added, it may be lengthened by VII. 2. 38. The augment इद however is not added in चिकीर्षति and जिहीर्षति, as they are formed from कू 'to do' and इ 'to lose', which do not take इद at all. Because here, though the short कू is lengthened before स, by VI. 4. 16, yet such lengthening will not make the roots long कू ending roots. Because the anuvritti of the word upadeśa is understood here from VII. 2. 10, so that the rule applies to those roots only which in 'upadeśa' or Dhātupāṭha end in long कू and not those whose कू is lengthened by some Grammatical rule. Moreover, the long कू in कू and इ is temporary only, as it is replaced by long ई ॥ (See VI. 4. 16, for lengthening). The Desiderative of कू—चिकरिषति, however, does not lengthen its vowel (VII. 2. 75).

As यूपीट or यवरिपीट; यूपीट, or सारिपीट; अयूपाताम्, or अय्यरिपाताम्; अयूपाताम्, or असारिपाताम् ॥ ऋत इति किम् । यूपीट, यूपीट; अय्योट, अय्योट ॥ संयोगादिति किम् । यूपीट, यूपीट; अय्योट, अय्योट ॥ आत्मनेपदेष्वित्येव । अय्यापीत्, असापीत् ॥ संयूपीट समयतत्वोपदेशाधिकारावभक्त-स्वाध् युद् इडागमो न भवति ॥

Why ending in short ऋ? Observe यूपीट, अय्योट, यूपीट and अय्योट ॥
Why 'beginning with a conjunct consonant'? Observe यूपीट, यूपीट, अय्योट and अय्योट ॥
Why 'in the Atmanepada'? Observe अय्यापीत्, असापीत् ॥
In संयूपीट and समयतत्व there is not इद, first because यूपीट (the form assumed by यूपीट with युद् augment) is not so enunciated in the Dhātupāṭha; the word upadeśa VII. 2. 10, is understood here; so that the rule applies to those roots only which in the Dhātupāṭha are यूपीट ending and preceded by conjunct consonant; and secondly युद् augment is considered as not attached to the root (VI. 1. 135), and therefore यूपीट is not considered a root beginning with a conjunct consonant.

स्वरतिसूतिसूयतिधूयुदितो वा ॥ ४४ ॥ पदानि ॥ स्वरति, सूति, सूयति, धूज, उदितः, वा ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ स्वरति सूति सूयति धूज इत्येत्येव उदित-यौचरस्य बलविराज्यधातुकस्य वा इडागमो भवति ।

44. A Valādi-ārdhadhātuka affix optionally takes इद, after svri, after the two roots सू (sūti and sūyati), after धूज, and after a root which has an indicatory long ऊ ॥

As स्वरिता or स्वर्त्ता ॥ प्रसीता, प्रसीता ॥ सूयति, सीता, सविता ॥ धूज, धीता, धविता ॥
उदितश्च खल्वपि । गाहू, विगाहा, विगाहिता; यूप, गोमा, गोपिता ॥
वेति वर्त्त्ताने पुनर्वामहणं लिङ्सि-चोर्निवृत्त्यर्थम् । सूतिसूयतोर्विकरणनिर्देशः धू प्रेरणइत्यस्य निवृत्त्यर्थः । धूजिति सादृबन्धकस्य निर्देशो धू

विभूतनइत्यस्य निबुध्यर्थः । सविता धवितेयेव नित्यमेतयोर्भवति । स्वरतेरेतस्मादिकल्पाद्वद्भवोः स्वइत्येतद्व-
वति विप्रतिपधेन । स्वरिष्यति । किंति तु प्रत्यये शुभकः किंतीति नित्यः प्रतिपेधो भवति पूर्वप्रतिपेधेन ॥
स्वुत्वा, सुत्वा, भूत्वा ॥

Though the anuvṛtti of वा was current, the second employment of वा
is to stop the anuvṛtti of the Benedictive and the S-Aorist. The roots सू of
Adādi ( 21 ) and Divādi ( 24 ) are to be taken, as the special forms सूति and
सूयति indicate, and not the सू of the Tudādi ( 115 ) class. The भू is exhibited
with the anubandha ऋ, in order to exclude भू विभूतने of Tudādi ( 105 ).
In the case of these latter the इद augment is invariable, as सविता and
धविता ॥ The root स्वु takes invariably इद in the Future, by virtue of
the subsequent superseding rule VII. 2. 70, as स्वरिष्यति ॥ And before किंतु
affixes, the prior rule VII. 2. 11, invariably debars इद, as स्वुत्वा, सुत्वा, भूत्वा ॥

रथादिभ्यश्च ॥ ४५ ॥ पदानि ॥ रथ-आदिभ्यः, च ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ रथ हिंसासंनिद्वारित्येवमादिभ्यो ऽद्याञ्च उत्तरस्य बलादेरार्द्धधातुकस्य वा इडागमो भवति ॥

45. A valādi-ārdhadhātuka affix optionally takes
इद after रथ and the seven roots that follow it (Divādi. 84 to 91).

As रथिता or रद्धा; नष्टा, (VII. 1. 60 तुम्) नशिता; बभ्रा, (VI. 1. 59 अस्) तर्मा,
तर्पिता; ब्रह्मा, धर्मा, सर्पिता; द्रोन्धा, द्रोडा, (VIII. 2. 33) द्रोहिता; मान्धा, मोडा, मोहिता; झोडा,
झोहिता, झोन्धा, झेङ्धा, झेडा, झेहिता ॥

Some hold that the रथादि roots optionally take इद in the Perfect Tense
also, because the present sūtra being subsequent to VII. 2. 13, debars that
sūtra so far. Others hold that the रथादि roots will always take इद in the Perfect,
because the former rule VII. 2. 13 is stronger than the present, in as much as
that is a prohibitory rule. So they form रन्धिव and रन्धिम् ॥

निरः कुषः ॥ ४६ ॥ पदानि ॥ निरः, कुषः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ निर इत्येवपूर्वान् कुष उत्तरस्य बलादेरार्द्धधातुकस्य वा इडागमो भवति ।

46. A valādi-ārdhadhātuka affix gets optionally
the augment इद, after कुष when it is preceded by निर ॥

As निष्कोष्टा or निष्कोष्टिता, निष्कोष्टुम् or निष्कोषितुम्, निष्कोषञ्च्यम् or निष्कोषितव्यम् ॥
But only कोष्टिता, कोष्टितुं, कोष्टितव्यम् without निर ॥ The exhibition of निर instead
of नित्य indicates the existence of a separate and distinct preposition निर, besides
नित्य ॥ It is the र् of this निर which is changed to ल् by VIII. 2. 19, in नित्यनम्;
for the र् of नित्य being asiddha could not be changed to ल् ॥

इणिष्ठायाम् ॥ ४७ ॥ पदानि ॥ इद, निष्ठायाम् ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ निरः कुषो निष्ठायामिडागमो भवति ।

47. The augment इद is added to the Participial
affixes त and तवत, after कुष preceded by निर ॥

As निष्कुषितवान्, निष्कुषितः ॥ The special mention of इद in the sūtra is
for the sake of making its addition invariable, otherwise it would have been

तीपसहलुभरपरिषः ॥ ४८ ॥ पदानि ॥ ति, इष, सह, लुम, रूप, रिषः ॥
वृत्तिः ॥ तकारावार्यभातुके इषु सह लुम रूप रिषु इय्येतेभ्यो वा इडागमो भवति ।

48. An *ārdhadhātuka* affix beginning with a *त* may optionally take the *इद*, after the roots *इष*, *सह*, *लुम*, *रूप* and *रिष* ॥

As एडा or एषिता ॥ The *इष* 'to wish' (VI. 59) is taken here, and not the *इष* (IV. 19. IX. 53) of the *Divādi* and *Kryādi* class. Of the *Divādi* *इष* 'to send, to go' we have invariably *प्रेषिता*, *प्रेषित्*, *प्रेषितव्यं*; and the *इष* 'to repeat' of the *Kryādi* is governed also by this rule and has the same forms. Therefore some read the *anuvṛtti* of *इषित्* into this *sūtra*. सह। सोडा। सहिता। लुम। लाभिता। लोङ्घा। रूप। रोहा। रोषिता। रिषु। रेहा। रेषिता ॥ Why do we say 'beginning with a *त*'? Observe *एषिष्यति* ॥

सनीवन्तर्द्वैम्रजदम्भुश्रिस्तुयूर्णु मरजापिसनाम ॥ ४६ ॥ पदानि ॥ सनि, इवन्त, कृध, भ्रज, दम्भ, श्रि, स्तु, यु, ऊर्णु, भर, जपि, सनाम् ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ इवान्तानाम् धातुनाम्। कृधु भ्रज दम्भु श्रि स्तु यु ऊर्णु भर जपि सन् इय्येतेभ्यो च सनि वा इडागमो भवति ।

49. The desiderative *स* may optionally take *इद*, after a root ending in *इष*, and after *कृधु*, *भ्रज*, *दम्भु*, *श्रि*, *स्तु*, *यु*, *ऊर्णु*, *भू*, *जप*, and *सन्* ॥

Thus *विषेषित* or *दुष्पित*, *सिसेषित*, *सुस्पित* ॥ कृध, *अधिषित*, *ईषित* ॥ भ्रज, *विषजिषित*, (VI. 4. 47) *विषषित*, (VIII. 2. 36 and 41) *विषजिषित*, *विषषित* ॥ दम्भु, *विषषित*, *विषषित*, (VII. 4. 56) *धोषित*, *श्रि*, *उच्छिश्रयित*, *उच्छिश्रयित* ॥ स्तु, *सिस्वित*, *सुस्पित* ॥ यु, *विषषित*, (VII. 4. 80) *युष्पित*, *ऊर्णु*, *प्राणुनिषित*, *प्राणुनिषित*, *प्राणुनिषित*, ॥ The root *भूम्* of the *Bhuādi* class is to be taken, as the form *भर* with *सन्* in the *sūtra* indicates. *विषषित*, *युष्पित*, ॥ जपि, *विषषित*, *विषषित* ॥ सन्, *सिसषित*, *सिसषित* ॥ केचिद्वैम्रजापिसनितनितविद्विषणित* पषित, ॥ *तितनित*, *तितसति*, *तितसति*, *तितसति*, *तितसति*, *तितसति*, *तितसति*, *तितसति*, *तितसति*, *तितसति* ॥ सनीति *किम्*, *विषित*, *भटा* ॥

Some add *तन्*, *पन्* and *इषित* also, as *तितनित* or *तितसति* or *तितसति*, (VI. 4. 17) *पितित* or *पितसति* (VII. 4. 54, VIII. 2. 29. VII. 4. 58) *विषषित* or *विषषित* ॥ Why do we say 'Desiderative'? Observe *विषित*, *भटा* ॥ The form *अधिषित* is thus evolved. The Desiderative root is *अधिषित*, the *कृ* being *gunated* by VII. 3. 86 before *सन्* ॥ Now we reduplicate it, and the second syllable *विष* will be reduplicated by VI. 1. 2. and the *रेष* is not duplicated by VI. 1. 3: so we get *विष* to reduplicate, and *ध* is changed to *र* ॥ The form *ईषित* is thus evolved. By VII. 4. 55, the *कृ* is changed to long *ई*, which is followed by *र* by I. 1. 57. Thus we have *ईषित* as root, and *पन्* is reduplicated, and the reduplicate is elided (VII. 4. 58). The forms *विषषित* and *धोषित* are similarly formed.

किशः क्कानिष्ठयोः ॥ ५० ॥ पदानि ॥ किशः, स्का, निष्ठयोः ॥ ५० ॥

वृत्तिः । किशः स्कानिष्ठयोर्य इडागमो भवति ।

50. The affixes ktvā, क and कवतु, may optionally take इदं after किशः ॥

As किशः or किशित्वा, किशः or किशितः, किशवान् or किशितवान् ॥ किशः (IX. 50) having an indicatory क would have optionally taken इदं before ktvā by VII. 2. 44, but then the Nishthā affixes by VII. 2. 15 would never have taken the augment. किशः (Divādi 52) उपतपि, being anudātta would *always* have taken इदं before ktvā and Nishthā. Hence this rule ordains option with regard to ktvā.

पूडश्च ॥ ५१ ॥ पदानि ॥ पूडः, च ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ पूडश्च स्कानिष्ठयोर्य इडागमो भवति ।

As पूत्वा or पवित्वा, सोमोतिपूतः, सोमोतिपवितः पूतवान् or पवितवान् ॥ This allows option where by VII. 2. 11 there would have been prohibition. See I. 2. 22.

वसतिश्रुधोरिद् ॥ ५२ ॥ पदानि ॥ वसति, श्रुधोः, इदं ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ वसतेः श्रुधश्च स्कानिष्ठयोरिडागमो भवति ।

52. The affix ktvā, kta and ktavatu always receive the augment इदं after वस् (वसति) and श्रुध् ॥

As उचित्वा, उचितः and उचितवान्, श्रुधित्वा, श्रुधितः, श्रुधितवान् ॥ The वस् of the Adādi class will get इदं as it is enumerated in the list of सेद roots. The repetition of इदं shows that the rule is invariable, the 'optionally' of the preceding sūtra does not affect it.

अश्वेः पूजायाम् ॥ ५३ ॥ पदानि ॥ अश्वेः, पूजायाम् ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अश्वेः पूजायामर्थे स्कानिष्ठयोरिडागमो भवति ।

53. The affixes ktvā, kta and ktavatu take the augment इदं after the root अश्व, when meaning 'to honor or do something to show honor'.

As अश्वित्वा जातु जुहोति, अश्वित्वा अस्य गुरवः (III. 2. 188, VI. 4. 30, II. 3. 67) By VII. 2. 56 अश्व would optionally have caused इदं to come before ktvā, and hence by VII. 2. 15 never before the Nishthā. This sūtra ordains invariable addition of this augment. Why do we say when meaning 'to honor'? Observe अश्वत्पुण्यक कृपान्, 'the water is raised from the well'.

लुमो विमोहने ॥ ५४ ॥ पदानि ॥ लुमः, विमोहने ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ लुमो विमोहनेर्थे वर्तमानात् स्कानिष्ठयोरिडागमो भवति ।

54. The affixes ktvā, kta and ktavatu take इदं after the root लुम् (Tud. 22) when meaning 'entangled or confused'.

As लुमित्वा and लोभित्वा, विलुमिताः केशाः, विलुमितः सीमन्तः, विलुमितानि पदानि ॥
विमोहनः आकुलीकरणं ॥ By VII. 2. 48 लुम would have optionally caused इद to come before ktvā, and then by VII. 2. 15 the Nishthā would never have been सेद् ॥ Hence this sūtra. As लुब्धा or लोभित्वा and लुमित्वा (I. 2. 26) ॥

जुवधोः किं ॥ ५५ ॥ पदानि ॥ जू, वधोः, किं ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ जू वधि इत्येतयोः स्वायत्यये इडागमो भवति ।

As जरित्वा or जरीत्वा, (VII. 2. 38) and वधित्वा ॥ जू was prohibited by VII. 2. 11. and वध would have been optionally सेद्, as it has an indicatory long ऊ, by VII. 2. 44. Hence this rule. The special mention of ktvā, stops the anuvritti of kta and ktavatu.

उदितो वा ॥ ५६ ॥ पदानि ॥ उदितः, वा ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ उदितो धातोः स्वायत्यये परतो वा इडागमो भवति ।

56. The इद is optionally the augment of ktvā, after a root which has an indicatory short उ ॥

As शह-शमित्वा or शान्त्वा; तह-तमित्वा or तान्त्वा; दह-दमित्वा or शान्त्वा ॥

से असिचि कृतचूतच्छुदतुदनुतः ॥ ५७ ॥ पदानि ॥ से, असिचि, कृत, चूत, छुद, तुद, नुतः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ सकारावसिच्यार्जधातुके कृत चूत छुद तुद नुत इत्येतयोः धातुयोः वा इडागमो भवति ।

गमेरिद् परस्मैपदेषु ॥ ५८ ॥ पदानि ॥ गमेः, इद, परस्मैपदेषु ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ गमेऽवतोः सकारावसिच्यार्जधातुकस्य परस्मैपदेष्वडागमो भवति ।

इदिः ॥ आत्मनेपदेन समानपदस्य गमेर्यमिडागमोनेष्यते ॥

58. An ārdhadhātuka affix beginning with a स gets the इद augment, after गम् in the Parasmaipada.

As गमिष्यति, अगमिष्यत्, जिगमिष्यति ॥ Why of गम्? Observe चेष्यति ॥ The repetition of इद shows that the rule is invariable. Why 'in the Parasmaipada'? Observe संगसीट, संगसीट, संगस्यते, संगसिस्यते, संगसिसिष्यते, अभिजिगसिस्यते ॥

BK. VII. CH. II §. 59. ]
