28. Before the affix **द (पय)**, the Vriddhi is substituted for the first vowel of the second member of **प्रवाहण**, but optionally so for the first vowel of the first member (i. e. **प्र**) ॥

Thus प्रवाहणस्थापत्यं = प्रवाहणेयः or प्रवाहणेयः ॥ The affix **दक्** IV. 1. 123, is added, similarly प्रवाहणेयो भार्याऽस्य = प्रवाहणेयो भार्यः (VI. 3. 39, masculination prohibited). Or we may translate the *sūtra* as 'Before the affix **द**, the vowel of **प्र** in प्रवाहण optionally gets Vriddhi', and omit the rest. The masculination will still be prohibited by VI. 3. 41, (जाते) ॥

तत्प्रत्ययस्य च ॥ २६ ॥ पदानि ॥ तत्प्रत्ययस्य, च ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ प्रवाहणस्थेति वर्तते, तद्विति तत्प्रत्ययस्य प्रत्ययमर्थः, दक् प्रत्ययान्तस्य प्रवाहणशब्दस्य तच्चित्वे परत उत्तरपद्यस्याभाविरचो वृजिभेवति पूर्वस्य तु वा ॥

29. Even so in a new derivative from this stem ending in **द**, formed with a Taddhita affix having an indicatory **अ**, **ए** or **कृ**, there is vriddhi substitution for the first vowel of the second member, and optionally for the first vowel of the first member, in प्रवाहणेय and प्रवाहणेय ॥

As प्रवाहणेयस्थापत्यं = प्रवाहणेयिः or प्रवाहणेयिः, प्रा or प्र-वाहणेयकम् ॥

नजः शुचिभ्वरक्षेत्रकृशालनिपुणानाम् ॥ ३० ॥ पदानि ॥ नजः, शुचि, ईश्वर, क्षेत्रकृ, कुशल, निपुणानाम् ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ नज उत्तरपद्यं शुचि ईश्वर क्षेत्रकृ कुशल निपुण इत्येतेषामभामारिरचो वृजिभेवति, पूर्वपद्यस्य वा भवति तच्चित्वे भित्ति भित्ति कित्ति वा परतः ॥

30. Before a Taddhita affix having an indicatory **अ**, **ए** or **कृ**, the Vriddhi is always substituted for the first vowel of शुचि, ईश्वर, क्षेत्रकृ, कुशल and निपुण when preceded by the Negative particle, but this substitution is optional for the vowel of the Negative particle.

As अशीचम् or आशीचम्, अनैश्वर्यम् or आनैश्वर्यम्, अशैचर्यम् or आशैचर्यम्, अकीशम् or आकीशम्, अनैपुणम् or आनैपुणम् ॥ Some say the optional vriddhi of the negative particle is an *aprapta-vibhāsa*, no other rule would have caused its vriddhi had this rule not existed. They argue that by V. 1. 121, all affixes denoting भाव are prohibited after a Tatpurusha compound with the negative particle; therefore, the words शुचि &c, should be first developed by the addition of भाव-affixes, and then they should be compounded with the negative particle, which may be optionally vriddhied by this rule, which would apply to it, though it is not an *anga*, because the rule teaches vriddhi. Others controvert this opinion, and hold that other affixes causing vriddhi than भाव-affixes, also come after negative-Tatpurusha compounds, such as affixes denoting des-

BK. VII. CH. III §. 32]

VRIDDHI.

1421

cendant &c: and भाव-affixes are added to Bahuvṛthi negative compounds also, therefore, the force of the anuvṛtti of अङ्ग, which is understood up to the end of the Seventh Adhyāya (VI. I. 1), and a fortiori in this sūtra also, should not be set aside as the above interpretation would do. Moreover the full Taddhita compounds अङ्गवृत्त and अनीश्वर are read in the list of Brāhmaṇādi words (V. I. 124), and as such they take the भाव affix व्यम् which would have always caused the vriddhi of अ, but for this sūtra which makes it optional. Therefore it is a prāpta-vibhāshā.

यथातथयथापुरयोः पर्यायेण ॥३१॥ पदानि ॥ यथातथ, यथापुरयोः, पर्यायेण ॥
वृत्तिः ॥ यथातथ यथापुर इत्येतयोर्नम् उत्तरयोः पर्यायेणाभावान्नो वृद्धिभवति तद्धिते भित्ति भित्ति
किति वा परतः ॥

31. Before a Taddhita affix having an indicatory अ, ण or क्, the words अयथातथ and अयथापुर may have vriddhi of the first vowel of their first member, or that of the second member, in alternation.

That is, when the Negative particle gets the vriddhi, the words remain unchanged; and when these words are vriddhied, the negative particle remains unaltered. As आययातध्यम् or आययातध्यम्, आययापुर्यम् or आययापुर्यम् ॥ The words अययातथ and अयथापुर should be considered to belong, as negative compounds, to Brāhmaṇādi class (V. I. 124): and take व्यम् ॥ In the sūtra the compounds यथातथ and यथापुर are exhibited and are Avyayibhāvas (II. I. 7), and being neuters, the आ of तथा and पुरा are shortened. According to Patanjali this sūtra is superfluous. When the negative particle takes Vriddhi, the compound should be analysed as, न यथातथा = अययातथा, अययातथा भावः = आययातध्यम् ॥ When the second member gets the vriddhi, the compound should be analysed as, यथातथा भावः = आययातध्यम्, न आययातध्यम् = आययातध्यम् ॥

हनस्तो ऽचिण्णलोः ॥३२॥ पदानि ॥ हनः, तः, अ, चिण्ण लोः ॥
वृत्तिः ॥ तद्धितेभित्ति निवृत्तम् । तत्संबद्धे कितीत्वापि । ऽभित्तीति वच्यते । हनस्तकारविषो भवति
भित्ति प्रत्यये परतः चिण्णलो वच्येत्स्वला ॥

32. त is substituted for the न of the root हन् before an affix with an indicatory अ or ण, which causes also the vriddhi of the penultimate अ, but the augment is not added before the Aorist-sign चिण्ण, nor before the Personal ending णल् of the Perfect.

The anuvṛtti of 'Taddhita' ceases, and with it that of कित् also which causes Vriddhi in Taddhita only. The भित्त् and भित्त् do govern still. Thus घातः (with पम्), घातयति (with भित्त्), घातकः (with णुल्), साधुपातित् with इम्; घातपातम् with णुल् ॥ But जपानि and जपान with चिण् and णल् ॥ This sūtra has

[BK. VII. CH. III. §. 34]

reference to roots, and refers to those affixes only which come after roots (धातु-मध्यम्), therefore not here वार्षिकः from वृक्षम् ॥

आतो युक्तिचण्कृतोः ॥ ३३ ॥ पदानि ॥ आतः, युक्त्, चिण्, कृतोः ॥
वृत्तिः ॥ आकारान्तस्याङ्गस्य चिणि कृति चिणि युगागमो भवति ।

33. A root-stem ending in आ receives the augment युक्त् (य), before the Aorist sign चिण्, and before a krit-affix with an indicatory ञ or ण, which causes also the Vriddhi of the root-vowel.

As अवाधि, अथाधि with चिण्, वायः and दायकः, धायः, धायकः with ण and णुल् ॥
Why चिण् and krit only? Observe द्वौ, द्वौ in the Perfect, and चौडिः, बालाकिः with द्वौ a Taddhita affix (IV. 1. 96). So also ज्ञा देवता अस्य=ज्ञः ॥

नौदात्तोपदेशस्य मान्तस्यानाचमेः ॥ ३४ ॥ पदानि ॥ न, उदात्तोपदेशस्य, मान्तस्य, अनाचमे ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ उदात्तोपदेशस्य मान्तस्याङ्गस्याचमिवर्जितस्य चिणि कृति च चिणि यदुक्तं तन्न भवति ॥
वा० ॥ अनाचमिकमिवमीनामिति वक्तव्यम् ॥

34. The Vriddhi is not substituted before the Aorist चिण् or a krit-affix with indicatory ञ or ण for the vowel of that root which ends in म and is acutely accented in its original enunciation (Dhātupāṭha), but not so in चम् after आ ॥

The vriddhi of the penultimate ञ takes place before णिन् and णिन् affixes (VII. 2. 116), that vriddhi does not take place in the case of udātta roots ending in म् ॥ Thus अवाधि, अतानि, and अवधि in चिण् ॥ Compare VI. 4. 92, 93. Similarly with कृत् affixes, as शमकः, तमकः, दमकः, शमः, तमः, दमः ॥ Why do we say 'acutely accented'? Observe, यामकः, रामकः ॥ How do you explain दधम् and दपरम्? These are irregular forms exhibited by Pānini himself in the Dhātupāṭha अण्डरधमे (Bhu. 380), यम दपरमे (Bhu. 1033) Why do we use 'in the original enunciation or upadeśa'? So that the rule may apply to शमी, तमी, but not to याममः, रामकः ॥ Here to the root शम्, तम् and दम् is added the affix धिनुण् (III. 2. 141). The words शमिदे &c. get the affix-accent, namely acute ई; and thus the root-vowel becomes anudātta. Though the root now becomes anudātta, yet because in its upadeśa it was udātta, the present sūtra will apply and prevent vriddhi. The roots यम्, रम् are anudātta in upadeśa, but in यामकः, रामकः they become udātta by णिन् accent. This accent is a secondary accent and not the 'original' accent; and hence the present rule does not apply and there is vriddhi. Why do we say ending in म्? Observe चारकः पाठकः ॥ Why with the exception of आचम्? Observe आचामकः ॥

Vārt:—Prohibition must be stated in the case of the roots आ-चम्, कम् and यम्, as यामः, कामः and आचामः ॥ In the case of कम्, the affix घम् is added

BK. VII. CH. III §. 36.]

पृष्ठ AUGMENT.

1423

in that alternative, when the root does not take the affix णिह् (III. 1. 31). It thus gets vriddhi.

The word आमः is formed from the Churādi अमः, which with the affix णिह् gets Vriddhi, because णिह् is not a krit-affix, and is not therefore governed by this rule. If you say 'let there be vriddhi of णिह्, but this vriddhi will be shortened by VI. 4. 92 because it is a मित् root', we reply 'this root is not मित्' ॥ The मित् roots are those enumerated in Bhuādi class, subdivision षटादिः (800). No doubt, there it is said that the roots ending in अमः are मित् (in अमन्ताअ). But a root is regarded मित् only with regard to the Causative णिह् affix, and not with regard to that णिह् of the Churādi class where the sense of the causative is not involved in it. Therefore this root is not मित् (VI. 4. 93).

The phrases सूर्यविभागा मुनिः and others like it are incorrect. Why do we say 'चिण् and krit only'? Observe दायाम, दायाम, चचाम ॥

जनिवध्योश्च ॥ ३५ ॥ पदानि ॥ जनि, वध्योः, च ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ जनि वधि इत्येतयोश्चिनि कृति च सृणिति यदुक्तं तत्र भवति ।

35. The Vriddhi is not substituted for the vowels of जन् and वध् before the Aorist-sign चिण् and the krit-affixes with an indicatory च् and ण् ॥

As अजनि and भयाधि with चिण्, and जनकः and वधकः (with णुल्), प्रजनः, वधः ॥ This rule refers to the separate and the distinct root वध and not to the substitute of हन् ॥ This we see in the line भक्षकश्चन विद्येत वधकोऽपि न विद्यते ॥ The form from हन् will be घातकः ॥ Moreover the substitute वध ends with अ i. e. it is of two syllables 'badha', and as such it also does not admit Vriddhi. (See II. 4. 42). The prohibition refers to चिण् and krit-affixes, therefore not here, as अजान गर्भ महिमानमिन्द्रम् ॥

अस्तिहीब्लीरीकन्यूयीक्ष्माय्यातां पुङ्गणौ ॥ ३६ ॥ अस्ति, ह्री, व्ली, री, कनूयी, क्ष्मायी, आताम्, पुङ्, णी ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ सर्वे निवृत्तमङ्गस्थेति वर्तते । अस्ति ह्री व्ली री कनूयी क्ष्मायी इत्येतेषामङ्गानामाकारान्तानां च पुणागमो भवति णी परतः ।

36. The augment पुङ् (प्) is added to the roots ऋ, ह्री, व्ली, री, कनूय, क्ष्माय, and to a root ending in long आ, when the affix णि (the Causative) follows.

As अपयति, हेपयति, क्लेपयति, रेपयति, क्लेपयति, क्ष्मापयति ॥ The anuvritti of every word other than अङ्ग (VI. 4. 1.) ceases. The य् of कनूय and क्ष्माय drops by VI. 1. 66. The guna takes place by VII. 3. 86. Of the roots ending in long आ, we have वापयति, वापयति ॥ The root ऋ (Bhu. 983) गतिप्रापणयोः, and ऋ (Juhotyādi 16) गतौ are both meant here. Similarly री includes रीङ् श्रवणे (Di-ādi 30), and री गातरिषणयोः (Kryādi 30). The augment is added at the end of

1324

जुक् AUGMENT.

[ Bk. VII Ch. III. §. 38

the preceding stem of root, and not to the affix. Being added to the root it becomes part of the root-stem, and in forming the reduplicate Aorist of such stems, the vowel before प is shortened by VII. 4. 1. If प were not the part of the stem, that vowel would not be shortened. Thus from बापयात; we have Aorist अहीरपत् ॥

शाच्छासाह्वाय्यावेपां युक् ॥ ३७ ॥ पदानि ॥ शा, छा, सा, ह्वा, व्या, वे पाम्, युक् ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ शा छा सा ह्वा व्या वे पा इत्येतेषामङ्गानां युगागमो भवति गो परतः ॥
वार्तिकम् ॥ युगागमस्तु तस्य वक्तव्यः ॥ वा० ॥ धृक् प्रीभोजुर्वक्तव्यः ॥

37. The augment युक् (य) is added to the verbal stems
शा, छा, सा, ह्वा, वे and पा before the affix ण (Causative).

As निशाययति, अवच्छाययति, अवसाययति, ह्वाययति, संध्याययति, वाययति, and पाययति॥
The word पा includes the root पा 'to drink'. (Bhu 972) प 'to dry' (Bhu 968), but not पा 'to protect' (Ad. 47): because the latter looses the शप् vikaraṇa.

Vārt:—The root पा 'to protect' takes the augment युक् before ण, as पालयति ॥

Vārt:—The roots धृक् and प्रीस् take the augment युक् before ण, as धूनयति, प्रीणयति ॥

All these augments are added to the roots, in order that VII. 4. 1. should cause the shortening of the vowel preceding these. Thus the Aorist of the above are: अहीरपत्, अपीपतत्, अचुधुनत्, अपीपिणत् ॥

The roots शा, छा, सा, ह्वा, व्या and पा are exhibited as ending in long आ their Dhātupāṭha forms are श, शा, छो, से, सो, ह्वे, व्ये and पै ॥ This indicates that these roots would have taken युक् by the last sūtra, the word आत् 'ending in long आ' means the roots which actually end in long आ, as well as those which get long आ by VI. 1. 45. This also indicates, that in this subdivision or section, the maxim of lakshaṇa protipadokta &c does not apply. Therefore when the roots इ with आप, and जि assume the form अधि-आ and जा before the affix ण by VI. 1. 48, the augment युक् is added to them, thus अध्याययति, जापयति ॥

वो विधूनने युक् ॥ ३८ ॥ पदानि ॥ वः, विधूनने, युक् ॥
वृत्तिः ॥ वा इत्येतस्य विधूननर्थे वर्तमानस्य युगागमो भवति गो परतः ।

38. वा gets the augment युक् (ज) before the affix
णि when the Causative has the sense of 'shaking'.

As पषेणोपवाजयति ॥ But आ वापयति केशात् when the sense is not that of shaking. This form could have been obtained from the root वज्र 'to move', (Bhu 271) with the affix ण in the ordinary way without any augment. The special augment ज् to वा indicates that this root will not take युक्, which it would have otherwise done by the last sūtra. The root वा belongs to Bhu. 969 [मोरे शोषण] ॥

त SUBSTITUTE.

लीलोजुंग्लुकावन्यतस्यां स्नेहविपातने ॥ ३९ ॥ पदानि ॥ ली, लोः, तुक्, लुकौ, अन्यतरस्याम्, स्नेह विपातने ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ ली लो इत्येतयोरङ्गयोरन्यतरस्यां तुक् लुक् इत्येतावागमौ भवतो नो परतः स्नेहविपातनेयं ॥

39. The roots ली and ला get optionally तुक् and लुक् augment respectively, before the affix णि, when the causative means 'the melting of a fatty substance'.

As वि लीनयति, वि लालयति, वि लाययति, or वि लापयति घृतम् ॥ The augment तुक् is added to ली when the root ends in long ई, and that also optionally. When the augment is not added, the regular causative लाययति is formed. But when ली gets the form ला by VI. 1. 51, it does not take the augment तुक् ॥ The root ली includes both ली and लीह of Kryādi and Divādi. The root ला includes ला 'to give' (adādi 49), and ला the form assumed by ली under VI. 1. 51. When लुक् is not added to ला, तुक् is added by VII. 3. 36. Why do we say when meaning 'to melt fat'? Observe only लोहे विलापयति, जटाभिरालापयते (I. 3. 70).

भियो हेतुमये युक् ॥ ४० ॥ पदानि ॥ भियः, हेतुमये, युक् ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ भी इत्येतस्य हेतुमयेऽयं युगागमो भवति नो परतः ॥

40. The augment युक् is added to the root भी before the affix णि, when fear is caused immediately owing to the agent of the Causative.

As युण्डो भीषयते, जटिलो भीषयते ॥ See I. 3. 68. Here also भी with long ई being employed in the sūtra, indicates that युक् is added then only, when the root has the form भी, but when it assumes the form भा by VI. 1. 56, the proper augment युक् will come: as युण्डो भापयते ॥ Why do we say 'when the agent of the causative is himself the direct cause of fear'? Observe कुञ्चिकयेन भाययति, for here कुञ्चिका causes fear and not the agent of the verb. The ई is vṛddhied and भाय substituted.

स्फायो वाः ॥ ४२ ॥ पदानि ॥ स्फायः, वः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ स्फाय इत्येतस्याङ्गस्य वकारादेशो भवति नो परतः ॥

41. For the final of the stem स्फाय is substituted व् in the causative.

As स्फाययति ॥

शदेरगतौ तः ॥ ४२ ॥ पदानि ॥ शदेः, अ गतौ तः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ शदे रङ्गस्यागतावयं वर्तमानस्य तकारादेशो भवति नो परतः ॥

42. For the final of the शदू is substituted व्, in the Causative, when it does not mean 'to drive'.

As पुष्पाणि शातयति, फलानि शातयति, but गाः शादयति गोपालकः ॥

रुहः पोन्यंतरस्याम् ॥ ४३ ॥ पदानि ॥ रुहः, पः, अन्यतरस्याम् ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ रुहः, पः, अन्यतरस्याम् ॥

43. प may optionally be substituted for the final of रुह in the Causative.

As श्रीहीन रोपयति or रौडयति ॥ According to Padamanjari this sūtra could be dispensed with. The form रोपयति could be obtained from the root रूप of Divādi class : which though meaning मोहन may be taken to mean 'grow' also; अनेकायत्वाद् धातुनाम् ॥

प्रत्ययस्यात्कात्पूर्वस्यात् इदाप्यसुपः ॥ ४४ ॥ पदानि ॥ प्रत्ययस्यात्, कात्, पूर्वस्य, अतः, इत, आपि, असुपः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ प्रत्ययस्यात्कात्पूर्वस्यात्, अतः, इत, आपि, असुपः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ प्रत्ययस्यात्कात्पूर्वस्यात्, अतः, इत, आपि, असुपः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ प्रत्ययस्यात्कात्पूर्वस्यात्, अतः, इत, आपि, असुपः ॥

44. इ is substituted for the अ which stands before the क् belonging to an affix, when the Feminine-ending आ follows, provided that, it does not come after a case-affix (i.e. when such a word in अक् does not stand at the end of a Bahuvrihi).

That which stands in an affix is called प्रत्ययस्य, i. e. क् must be the part of the affix. The अक् is changed into इक् in the feminine in आ ॥ As अटि-लिका, इण्डिका, युणिका, इत्तिका, कारिका, हारिका ॥ So also एतिका from एतद् + अकच् + आप् एतकद् + आप् ॥ The इ is then replaced by अ (VII. 2. 102). The क् must belong to the affix, therefore, not in इका from इक् शक्नोति ॥ The स् in प्रत्ययस्य is for the sake of distinctness, there is no affix which is only क् ॥ The rule applies to क्, therefore, not to नन्दना, रमणा ॥ The इ is substituted for the अ which precedes (पूर्वस्य) क्, and not the अ which follows क्, as पडुका, पडुका ॥ The क् must be preceded by short अ, therefore, not here नीका, नीका, nor in राका, धाका ॥ The substitution takes place when आ follows, therefore, not in कारकी ॥ The word आपि qualifies क् ॥ The क् should be followed by आ ॥ Obj. But in कारिका from कारक + आ, क् is not directly followed by आ, but by अ? Ans. When अ + आ = आ there is ekādeśa, the क् is followed by आ, there being no third letter intervening then. Obj. But an ekādeśa is sthānivat to what it replaces when a pūrvā-vidhi is to be applied, therefore there still exists the intervention. Ans. The express text of this sūtra will remove the intervention. Obj. Then इ should be substituted in रयकव्या and गंगकाव्या ॥ These words are formed by the affixes कव्यञ्च and काव्यञ्च, as रयाना समुहः, (IV. 2. 51) and गंगमिच्छाति आत्मनः (III. 1. 9) = रयकव्या and गंगकाव्या ॥ Here also before the क् of the affix, the अ should be replaced

BK. VII. CH. III. §. 45 ]

ई OF FEMININE.

1427

by ई, when the feminine affix आ is added: for there is no intervention between क् and आ (the intermediate letters being non-existent, as you say). Ans. We say that intervention is no intervention, when it consists of only one letter, which even does not actually exist, but only through the fiction of sthanivat. Therefore, the feminine of the above words will not take ई, as क् is not followed immediately (in the sense above expressed) by आप्, as रधकव्या and गगकाव्या, because in these actually many letters are heard as intervening between the क् and आप् ॥

Why do we say असुप्: 'provided that the feminine affix आप् does not come after a case-affix? Observe बहवः परिज्ञाजका अस्यां मधुरायां = बहुपरिज्ञाजका मधुरा ॥ Here आप् comes after the noun बहुपरिज्ञाजक which ends in a case-affix, and hence the अ of ज is not changed to ई ॥ The case-affix is elided by II. 4. 71, and it still exerts its influence by I. 1. 62. The word असुप्: is a प्रसज्यप्रतिषेधः (a simple prohibition of the particular matter specified without mentioning what is different from it): and not a पयुरासः or exception. Had it been a Paryudāsa, (सुपोऽन्यः = असुप्:) then आप् coming after a full word not having a case-affix, would have caused the ई substitution in the last example. Nor should असुप्: be explained as that in which there exists no case-affix. Had it been so, then in बहुनि चर्माण्यस्यां = बहुचर्मिका no ई ought to be added.

Vārt:—मामक and मरक should be enumerated, for the क् of these is not part of the affix: as मामिका, नरिका ॥ Here ममक is substituted for मम before the affix अण् (IV. 3. 3), to which is then added दाप् ॥ The word ममक takes long ई in the feminine only when it is a Name or in the Vedas (IV. 1. 30): therefore though मामक ends in अण्, it does not take ङीप् (IV. 1. 15) but दाप् (IV. 1. 4), नरान् कायति = नरक formed with the affix क् (अ III. 2. 3).

Vārt:—The rule applies to the words ending in रथक् (IV. 2. 98) and रथप्, (IV. 2. 104) in spite of the prohibition in VII. 3. 46. As वाशिणात्विका, इहत्विका ॥

The word in the sūtra is कात् the fifth case of क् ending in अ ॥ If then this be the condition, that the affix must end in ka क् and not in k क्, then the rule will not apply to एतिका ॥ Because here the augment is अकञ्च (अक्) with क्; the final अ in अकञ्च is for euphony only, and not a portion of the affix, as we find in निन्द्यकि, छिन्द्यकि, रन्ध्यकि ॥ The word कात् therefore, is construed to mean ending in the consonant क् ॥

न यासयोः ॥ ४५ ॥ पदानि ॥ न, या, सयोः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ या सा इत्येतयोरिकारदिशो न भवति ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ यत्तयोः प्रतिषेधे व्यकन उपसंख्यानम् ॥ वा० ॥ पावकादीनां छन्दसुपसंख्यानम् ॥

वा० ॥ आशिषि चोपसंख्यानम् ॥ वा० ॥ उत्तरपदयोपे चोपसंख्यानम् ॥

वा० ॥ शिवकादीनां चोपसंख्यानम् ॥ वा० ॥ तारका ज्योतिषुपसंख्यानम् ॥

वा० ॥ वर्णका तान्तव उपसंख्यानम् ॥ वा० ॥ वर्तका शकुनो प्राचामुपसंख्यानम् ॥

वा० ॥ अष्टका पितृदेवये ॥ वा० ॥ वा मुनकापुस्तकापुस्तारकाणामुपसंख्यानम् ॥

OF FEMININE.

[ Bk. VII. Ch. III. § 46

45. The इ is not substituted for the अ of य and स, with the augment क, when the feminine आ follows.

As यका, सका ॥ The या and सा simply stand for यद and तद, and the prohibition is not confined to the nominative case only, as the forms या and सा may lead one to think. न यद तदोः would have been a better sutra. The prohibition applies in every case, as यकामधीते, तर्का पचामहे ॥ Or यकायकामधिमहे (i. e. ऋचा गाधां च), and तर्का तकामपचामहे (i. e. ओपधीं शाकिनीं वा)

Vårt:—The affix व्यक्त (V. 3. 34) should be enumerated also along with यद and तद ॥ As उपत्यका, अधित्यका ॥

Vårt:—The feminine of पावक &c in the Veda does not take इ for अ ॥ As हिरण्यवर्णः शुचयः पावकाः, याहु अ लोमकाः, ऋचकाः &c. But पाविकाः, अलौमिकाः in secular literature.

Vårt:—So also in the affix वृद used in benediction: as जीवताद् जीवका, नन्वताद् नन्वका, भवताद् भवका ॥ See III. 1. 150.

Vårt:—So also when the second member is elided in a compound: as देवका, यज्ञका, the second member इत्त is elided, the fuller forms being देववृत्तिका, यज्ञवृत्तिका (अनजादो च विभाषा लोपो वक्तव्यः) See V. 3. 83 Vårt.

Vårt:—शिपक &c should be enumerated in this prohibition: as शिपका, ध्रुवका, पुत्रका, चटका ॥

Vårt:—तारका is formed when it means 'stars', but तारिका 'a maid-servant' from तारयति ॥

Vårt:—वर्णका is formed when it means 'a mantle or mask', but वर्णिका 'an expounder': as वर्णिका भायुरी लोकायते 'Bhāguri is a commentary of Lokāyata'

Vårt:—वर्तका 'a bird' according to the Eastern grammarians, but वर्तिका according to the Northern authorities. Why do we say 'when meaning a bird'? Observe वर्तिका भायुरी लोकायतस्य ॥

Vårt:—अष्टका when meaning a पितृदेवस्य ceremony, but अष्टिका खारी ॥ The ceremony related to Pitridevata is called Pitridevata, the affix is यद ॥ The former is derived from the root अश्व with the affix तकन् (अदनान्ति ब्राह्मणो ओपनमस्यो), the other is derived from the numeral अष्ट by the affix कन् (V. 1. 22).

Vårt:—Optionally सुतका, पुत्रका and वृन्दारका, the other forms are सुतिका, पुत्रिका, and वृन्दारिका ॥

उदीचामतः स्थाने यकपूर्वायाः ॥ ४६ ॥ पदानि ॥ उदीचाम, आतः, स्थाने, यक, पूर्वायाः, ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ उदीचामाचार्याणां मतेन यकारपूर्वायाः ककारपूर्वायाश्चातः स्थाने योऽकारस्तस्यातः स्थाने इकार-देशो भवति ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ यकपूर्वत्वे धात्वन्तप्रतिषेधः ॥

46. According to the opinion of Northern grammarians, इ is not substituted for that अ which is obtained by

BK. VII. CH. III. §. 47 ]

THE FEMININE १

1429

shortening the long आ of the feminine (under rule VII. 4. 13 before the affix क), which is preceded by a य् or a क् ॥

The mention of 'northern grammarians' makes this an optional rule. As इष्यका or इष्यिका, क्षत्रियका or क्षत्रियिका, षट्कका or षटकिका, मुष्कका, मुष्किका ॥ Why do we say preceded by य् or क्? Observe अश्वक-अश्विका only (from अश्व) ॥ The word यकपूर्वाया: is exhibited in the feminine, in order to indicate that the rule applies when the *feminine* affix आ is shortened to अ ॥ Therefore not here शुष्यिका from शुष्या (शुष्ये याति). So also शुष्यिका from शुष्या, where आ is part of the root या (see III. 2. 74).

*Vårt*:—Prohibition must be stated of the य् and क् being finals of a root. When the य् or क् preceding this अ, is the final of the root, the prohibition contained in the sutra, does not apply: as सुनीयका, सुयायिका, सुपाकिका, and अशोकिका ॥

Why do we say 'of long आ'? Observe सांकाश्ये भवा = सांकादियका ॥ The word संकाश्य is formed from संकाश by the affix ण्य (संकाशे निर्वृत्ते) ॥ Then is added the affix बुभ (IV. 2. 121). Here there is no shortening of a long आ, and hence no option is allowed. But in इष्यका or इष्यिका the long आ has been shortened. Because this word is thus derived: इषमर्हति = इष्या (इष्यादिश्याय: V. 1. 66). To this क् is added, and the long आ is shortened.

Why is the word स्थान used in the sutra, when by the general rule षष्ठी स्थान योग: this word would be understood here? The special mention is for the sake of pointing out that the अ which takes the place of आ is intended here: i. e. the इ replaces this short अ; but had the word स्थान not been used in the sutra the इ would have replaced the long आ ॥

अस्त्रैषाजाहाद्रास्वा नञ्पूर्वाणामपि ॥ ४७ ॥ पदानि ॥ अस्त्रा, एषा, अजा, शा, द्वा, स्वा, नञ्, पूर्वाणाम्, अपि ॥
वृत्ति: ॥ उर्वीषागात: स्थान इति वर्तते ॥ आत: स्थाने योकारस्तस्य इत्वं न भवति उर्वीषागाचार्याणां गतेन ॥

47. According to the opinion of Northern grammarians, इ is not substituted for that अ which is obtained by shortening the आ (before क by VII. 4. 13), of अस्त्रा, एषा, अजा, शा, द्वा (VII. 2. 102), and स्वा; even not then when the negative particle precedes them.

As भस्वका or भस्विका, अभस्वका or अभस्विका, एषका or एषिका, अजका or अजिका, झका or झिका, अझका or अझिका, इके or इके, स्वका or स्विका, अस्वका or अस्विका ॥ Of एषा and इि there are no examples with the negative particle. For if the compounding with नञ् takes place after the addition of the अकञ्, or on the contrary, if first अकञ् be added and then the नञ् compounding takes place, in both alternatives, the case-affixes must be added in order to substitute अ for the final by VII. 2. 102: and it is only when this अ is substituted that the fe-

1430

THE FEMININE १

[ Bk. VII. Ch. III. §. 49

minine दाप् can come. So that the case-affix is the principal ingredient, and दाप् comes after सुप्, and therefore by the prohibition of असुप्: in VII. 3. 44, there can arise no occasion for the substitution of इ ॥ Therefore अनिषका and अङ्क are the invariable forms of these words with the negative particle. स्व meaning agnates and property, takes the negative particle. भस्वा is a word which has no corresponding masculine form, and as such, by the following rule VII. 3. 48 it would not have taken इ; its special mention here indicates that it should be the secondary member of the compound here: as अविद्यमाना भस्वा यस्वा = अभस्वा, the Diminutive of which is अभस्वा or अभस्विका ॥ Here first the भस्वा is shortened as it is a secondary member (upasarjana), then when the Bahuvrihi is made, the feminine affix दाप् is added to this भापितपुंस्क word, then this आ is shortened before क by VII. 4. 13. This short अ (VII. 4. 13) does not come in the room of the आ which is ordained to come after a word having no corresponding masculine.

The force of अनि shows that the rule applies, when words other than नस also precede, and even when no words precede. As निर्भस्विका or निर्भस्वका, बहुभस्विका or बहुभस्वका ॥

Note:—The form इके is from the word इकि, dual number, the final इ is changed to अ (व्यदाधन्), then the feminine आ (दाप्) is added (इका), and then शी is substituted for औ ॥

अभापितपुंस्कान्च ॥ ४८ ॥ पदानि ॥ अ, भापितपुंस्कात्, च, ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अभापितपुंस्कादिहितस्यातः स्याने योकारस्तस्योदींचामाचार्याणांमतेन इकारदेशो न भवति ॥

48. According to the opinion of Northern Grammarians, इ is not substituted for an अ obtained from the shortening of the Feminine आ (VII. 4. 13), when to the feminine in long आ there is no equivalent masculine, even when the Negative particle precedes.

As खटुका or खटुका, अखटुका or अखटुका, परमखटुका or परमखटुका ॥ When before the affix कप्, the stem is shortened in a Bahuvrihi, this rule will apply (VII. 4. 15). There also, the अ must be substituted for the आ of a feminine word which has no corresponding masculine. But this rule does not apply when the negative compound is the synthesis of अविद्यमाना खट्वा अस्या = अखट्वा, अल्या अखट्वा = अखटुका ॥ Similarly अतिक्रान्ता खट्वा = अतिखट्वा, अल्या अतिखट्वा = अतिखटुका ॥

Note:—The word खट्वा is always feminine and has no corresponding masculine.

आदाचार्याणाम् ॥ ४९ ॥ आत्, आचार्याणाम् ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अभापितपुंस्काताः स्याने योकारस्तस्याचार्याणामाकारदेशो भवति ॥

BK. VII. CH. III. §. 51 ]

इ—इक ॥

1431

49. According to the opinion of other Teachers, आ is substituted for the अ which arose from the shortening of the feminine आ of a word which has no corresponding masculine form.

As खद्वाका, अखद्वाका or परमखद्वाका॥

Note:—The “Teachers” referred to here are either those other than the Northern Grammarians, or it may refer to the Teacher of Pānini, the plural being for the sake of respect. Thus there are three forms अखद्वाका, अखद्विका, and अखद्वाका ॥

टस्येकः ॥ ५० ॥ पदानि ॥ टस्य, इकः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अङ्गस्य निमित्तं यष्टः, कथाङ्गस्य निमित्तं, प्रत्यय, स्तस्य प्रत्ययस्य इक् इत्ययमविशो भवति ॥

50. For ट in the beginning of a Taddhita affix there is substituted इक् ॥

As आक्षिकः, शालाकिकः (इक् IV. 4. 1), लावणिकः (इक् IV. 4. 52). In the affixes इक्, इम् &c, if the affix is the consonant इ, and अ is only for euphony, then here also the अ is for pronunciation only: but if on the contrary, the aggregate इ (इ+अ) is the affix, then the same is the case here. This rule does not apply in Unādi affixes always, as कणैष् इः = कण्ठः (Un I. 103), for there is diversity (बहुल) in the Unādi.

माधितिकः (= मथितं पञ्चमस्य IV. 4. 51) is thus formed मथित + इक् = मथित् + इक् (VI. 4. 148 the अ is dropped). Now arises the doubt, should इक् be replaced by क as taught in the next aphorism VII. 3. 51, as it comes after a त् ॥ This substitution, however, does not take place, because it was इक् which caused the elision of अ, and now त् which became final by such elision cannot cause the destruction of इक् its producer (सन्निपातलक्षणो विधिरनमित्तं तद्विघातस्य). Or the elided अ (VI. 4. 148) may be considered as sthānivat, and would thus prevent क substitution.

There are two views about this इ ॥ Some say that the consonant इ only is the sthānī, and the अ is only for the sake of pronunciation. The others hold that इ, the consonant and the vowel are sthānī in the aggregate. In the first view, the rule would apply to the consonant इ at the end of roots like पइ in पइता, पइतु; in the other view the rule would apply to the affix अइच् in कर्मइ ॥ Hence, the commentary uses the word, that इ must be the cause of अङ्ग ॥

इसुसुत्तान्तात्कः ॥ ५१ ॥ पदानि ॥ इस्, उस्, उक्, त्, अन्तान्त्, कः, ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ इस् उस् इत्येवमन्तानामुगन्तानां तान्तानां चाङ्गानामुत्तरस्य तस्य क इत्ययमविशो भवति ॥
वार्तिकम् ॥ शेष उपसंख्यानम् ॥

51. क is substituted for ट after a stem ending in इस्, उस्, उ or ऊ, ऋ and त् ॥

As सार्पिकः, धातुष्कः, धातुष्कः, नैषाकर्तुष्कः, शाबरजन्तुष्कः, मातुष्कः, पैतुष्कः, औषधिः

1432

GUTTURALISATION

[ Bk. VII. Ch. III. § 53

तकः, शाक्तकः, याक्तकः ॥ The इस and उस are the affixes of that name, therefore not here, आशीषिकः (= आशिषा चरति), औषिका (= उषा चरति) ॥

*प्रेमः*—So also after वास, as वैष्कः (शोभ्यचरति) ॥

The word सापिकः is formed by इक् of नक्षत्र पण्ये, (IV. 4. 51) and स is changed to ष by इषः षः (VIII. 3. 39). भातुकः is by इक् of प्रहरण ॥ याक्तकः is by इक् of शोष्यति ॥ नैषाक्तकः &c by इक् of भवावार्ये ओवैशे इष ॥ मातुकः by इक् of तत आगतः, खतदम् ॥ औषाचतकः by इक् (IV. 2. 19) शाक्तकः by इक् of संतुष्ट (IV. 4. 12).

चजोः कु चिष्ण्यतोः ॥ ५२ ॥ पदानि ॥ चजोः, कु, चित्, ण्यतोः, ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ चकारजकारयोः क वर्गादिशो भवति चित् ण्यति च प्रत्यये परतः ॥

52. For the final च् or ज् of a root, there is substituted a corresponding guttural, before an affix having an indicatory घ्, and before ण्यत् ॥

As पाकः, त्यागः, रागः with घस्, and चाक्यम्, वाक्यम् and रेक्यम् with ण्यत् ॥ Compare VII. 3. 59.

न्यङ्कादीनां च ॥ ५३ ॥ पदानि ॥ न्यङ्कु, आदीनाम्, च, ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ न्यङ्कु इत्येवमादीनां क वर्गादिशो भवति ॥

53. The guttural is substituted in न्यङ्कु and the rest.

Thus न्यङ्कुः from नि + अञ्च + उ; So also मद्युः ॥

(1) By the sūtra नादञ्चः (Up I. 17), the affix उ is added to the root अञ्च preceded by नि ॥ (2) मद्युः is formed by adding उ to the root मद्यः (Up I. 7) (3) मद्युः, is formed by the affix उ added to the root अञ्च, the स् is elided, and र is vocalised (Up I. 28). (4 and 5) दूरपाकः, फलेपाकः formed by the अञ्च affix of पचादि class, (= दूर पच्यते स्वयमेव, फले पच्यते स्वयमेव) ॥ The vriddhi is by nipātana. The seventh case-affix is not elided in these compound words by VI. 3. 14. (6) क्षणेपाकः ॥ This word is read by some. Others read these as दूरपाकः, फलेपाकः with दाप् ॥ A third reading is दूरपाकः फलेपाकः, by the affix उ added irregularly. (7 and 8) तक and वक्र ॥ These are formed from the roots तञ्च and तञ्च with the affix रक् (Up II. 13). (9) व्यतिपङ्कः formed from व्यतिपञ्जति with पचादि अञ्च ॥ (10) अनुपङ्कः ॥ (11) अवसर्गः ॥ (12) उपसर्गः ॥ (13) मेषः ॥ (14) श्रपाकः ॥ (15) मांसपाकः ॥ (16) कपोतपाकः ॥ (17) उलूकपाकः ॥ (18) पिण्डपाकः formed by the affix अञ्च with an accusative word in construction as upapada. (19) अर्घः when it denotes a name meaning 'price'. This is formed from the root अर्घः with the affix घस् ॥ When it is not a name, the form is अर्घः ॥ (20 and 21) अवदाघः and निबाघः, when they are names meaning 'Summer or Hot season'. These are formed from the root रक् preceded by अव and नि ॥ But when they are not names, the forms are अवदाघः, निबाघः ॥ (22) न्यघोघः formed from the root रक् preceded by न्यक् and by adding the पचादि अञ्च ॥ The र् is changed to घ ॥ (23) वीहम् ॥ Formed from रक् with वि and the affix बिबप्, and र् changed to घ ॥ न्यघोघयति and विरोघयति ॥

1 न्यङ्कु, 2 मद्यु, 3 मद्यु, 4 दूरपाकः, 5 फलेपाकः, 6 क्षणेपाकः, 7 दूरपाकः, 8 फलेपाकः, 9 दूरपाकः, 10 फलेपाकः, 11 तक, 12 वक्र, 13 व्यतिपङ्कः, 14 अनुपङ्कः, 15 अवसर्गः, 16 उपसर्गः, 17 श्रपाकः, 18 मांसपाकः, 19 मूलपाकः, 20 कपोतपाकः, 21 उलूकपाकः, 22 संज्ञायां मेघनिबाधावदाधार्याः मेषः 23 न्यघोघः, 24 वीहम् ॥

BK. VII. CH. III. §. 56 ]

GUTTURALISATION.

1433

हो हन्तेगजिसेषु ॥ ५७ ॥ पदानि ॥ हः, हन्तेः, जिणत, नेषु, ॥
वृत्तिः ॥ हन्तेहकारस्य कवर्गदिशो भवति इति गति गति प्रत्यय परतो मकारे च ॥

54. A guttural is substituted for the ह in हन् before an affix having an indicatory ज, or ण and before न ॥

As घातयति with णिच्, घतिकः with ण्वलु, साघुप् तिन् with इम्, घातघातम् with ण्वलु, घातः with पम्, प्रन्ति, प्रन्तुम्, and अघ्न् before न ॥ Why do we specify ह? Otherwise the substitute would replace the final letter. Why of हन्? Observe प्रहारः, प्रहारकः ॥ ण and ण qualify the affixes, and न means the न of हन् which becomes joined with ह when the intermediate अ is dropped. This न comes in immediate contact with ह, because it is heard in pronouncing, and in writing. If the elided अ be considered as sthanivat, then ह can never be followed by न, for there will exist the intervention of this latent अ, but by virtue of the special text of this sutra, such an elided अ should not be considered as an intervention. And if ण, ण and न be all considered as qualifying the ह of हन्, still on the maxim य न नान्यवधानं तन व्यवहितेऽपि वचनप्रामाण्यात् therefore ण or ण are considered to come after ह though a portion of the root intervenes. But not so here, हनननिष्ठति हननीयति, add ण्वलु to this Denominative root, and we have हननायकः ॥

अभ्यासाच्च ॥ ५५ ॥ पदानि ॥ अभ्यासात्, च, ॥
वृत्तिः ॥ अभ्यासादुत्तरस्य हन्तिहकारस्य कवर्गदिशो भवति ॥

55. A Guttural is substituted for the ह in हन् after a reduplication also.

As जिपांसति, जङ्घयन्ति, अहं जधान ॥ The rule applies when such an affix follows which causes the reduplication of the stem (anga) हन्, therefore not here हननीयितुमिच्छति = जिहननीयिपति ॥

हेरचङि ॥ ५६ ॥ पदानि ॥ हेः, अ, चङि, ॥
वृत्तिः ॥ हिनोतेहकारस्याभ्यासादुत्तरस्य कवर्गदिशो भवति अचङि ॥

56. A guttural is substituted for the ह of हि (हिनोति) after a reduplication, but not in the Reduplicated Aorist.

As जिपीयति, प्र जेपीयते, प्रजिपाय; but प्राजीहयन् हूनम् in the simple Aorist. Obj. The word अचङि could be dispensed with from the sutra, in as much as चङ् can never come after the simple root हि, but after the causative of हि, and the causative stem of हि is a different verb than, हि. Ans. The fact of this word अचङि being employed in the sutra indicates the existence of the following maxim : प्रकृति महन् ज्यधिकस्यापि महान् “A radical denotes whenever it is employed in Grammar, not only that radical itself, but it denotes also whatever stem may result from the addition to it of the causative affix णि” ॥ Therefore we have प्रजिपायायिपति ॥

BK. VII. CH. III. §. 61

The word प्राज्ञियत् is the Aorist of the causative of हि, with चह्, the elision of णि, the shortening of the penultimate the reduplication, guttural change by कुहाइच्, and lengthening by दीर्घोत्तयोः ॥

सन्तिटोजैः ॥ ५७ ॥ पदानि ॥ सन्, लिटोः, जेः, ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ सन्ति लिटि च मयये जेरङ्गस्य योग्यासस्तस्मादुत्तरस्य कवर्गार्देशो भवति ॥

57. A guttural is substituted for the ज् in जि after a reduplication before the Desiderative affix सन्, and in the Perfect.

As जिगीपति, जिगाय ॥ Why in the Desiderative and Perfect only? Observe जेजीयते ॥ Though the root क्या also assumes the form जि by vocalisation (VI. 1. 16, 17) yet that जि is not to be taken here. That will form जिज्यतुः, जिज्युः ॥

विभाषा चेः ॥ ५८ ॥ पदानि ॥ विभाषा, चेः, ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ चिनोतेरङ्गस्य सन्तिटोरथासादुत्तरस्य विभाषा कवर्गार्देशो भवति ॥

58. A guttural is optionally substituted for the च् of चि after a reduplication in the Desiderative and Perfect.

As चिचांपति or चिकीपति, चिचाय or चिकाय ॥ But चेचीयते in other cases.

न कादेः ॥ ५९ ॥ पदानि ॥ न, कु, आदेः, ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ कवर्गार्देशोभजोः कवर्गार्देशो न भवति ॥

59. A guttural is not substituted for the final च् ज् of a root which begins with a guttural, before an affix having an indicatory घ and before ण्यत् ॥

As कुजः, खजः and गजः with घम्; कुज्यः, खज्यः and गज्यः with ण्यत् ॥ This is an exception to VII. 3. 52.

अजिवज्योश्च ॥ ६० ॥ पदानि ॥ अजि, वज्योः, च ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अजि अजि इलेतयोश्च कवर्गार्देशो न भवति ॥

60. A guttural is not substituted for the final or ज् of अज् and वज् before an affix having an indicatory घ and before ण्यत् ॥

This is an exception to VII. 3. 52. Thus समाजः, उदाजः, परिज्ञाजः and परिज्ञाञ्चम् ॥ There is no example of अज् with the affix ण्यत्, because by II. 4. 56, बी replaces अज् before all ārdhadhātuka affixes except घम् and अम् ॥ The च of the sūtra implies that the rule applies to other roots also not mentioned, as वाजः, वाज्यम् from वज् ॥

भुजन्मुखजो पाण्युपतापयोः ॥ ६१ ॥ पदानि ॥ भुज, न्युखजो, पाणि, उपतापयोः, ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ भुज न्युखज इलेतो शब्धो निपालेते यथासंख्यम् पाण्युपतापे च ॥

61. भुज 'an arm', and न्युज 'a kind of bodily disease', are irregularly formed, without any change of their ज before घञ् ॥

The word भुजः = भुज्यतेऽनेन, with घञ् (III. 3. 121). The irregularity consists in the absence of Guṇa, as well as of gutturalisation. न्युज्यताः शन्तेऽस्मिन् = न्युज्यताः from the root उञ् अजय (Tudādi 20). The irregularity consists in the non-changing of ज ॥ When not meaning 'an arm' and 'a disease', we have भोगः, समुद्रः ॥

प्रयाजानुयाजी यक्षाङ्गे ॥ ६२ ॥ पदानि ॥ प्रयाज, अनुयाजी, यक्ष, अङ्गे, ॥
वृत्तिः ॥ कृत्वप्रतिषेधोऽनुवतते ॥ प्रयाज अनुयाज इलेती निपात्यते यक्षाङ्गेऽनिषेधे ॥ प्रपूर्वस्य यजेयभि कृत्वाभावो निपात्यते ॥

62. प्रयाज and अनुयाज are irregularly formed with घञ्, when meaning a portion of a sacrificial offering.

These words are derived from यज् with घञ् without the guttural substitution; as पञ्च प्रयाजाः, षयोनुयाजाः, लभन्ते प्रयाजाना पश्चात् त्वं पुरस्तात् ॥ But प्रयागः and अनुयागः when not referring to portions of a sacrifice. The प्रयाज and अनुयाज are illustrative only. The guttural change does not take place with other prepositions &c. also, as उपयाजः, उपांशुयाजः, संयाजः, क्तुयाजः, as in the sentences एकादशोपयाजाः, उपांशु याजनन्तरा यजति, अटो पन्नो संयाजा भवन्ति, क्तुयाजे श्रान्ति ॥

वज्रेगेती ॥ ६३ ॥ पदानि ॥ वज्रेः, गतौ, ॥
वृत्तिः ॥ वज्रेरङ्गस्य गतौ वर्तमानस्य कवर्गार्दशो न भवति ॥

63. A guttural is not substituted for the palatal of घञ् in the sense of 'going'.

As वज्रस्य वज्रन्ति वणिजः, but वाङ्मयं काष्ठ = कुटिलं ॥ Why is गतौ used, when we kn w from the Dhatupāṭha (Bhuadi 204) that वञ्च means 'to go'? The specification shows that the roots possess many meanings other than those assigned to them in the Dhātupāṭha.

ओक उचः के ॥ ६४ ॥ पदानि ॥ ओकः, उचः, के, ॥
वृत्तिः ॥ उचेऽन्तोः के प्रत्यय ओक इति निपात्यते ॥

64. ओक is irregularly formed from the root उच् with the affix क (अ) ॥

The change of च् into क्, and the Guṇa are the irregularities. As योक्तः 'a bird, a tree'. The affix क is added under III. 1. 135. The क is added with the force of घञ् the Kāraka relation being that of Location &c. The घञ् affix would have given the form regularly, but then the word would have been acutely accented on the first syllable, but it is desired that the acute should be on the last. The words द्विवेकसः, जनैकसः &c are also irregular,

Others say that the prohibition applies to वच् only when it is preceded by प्र, and does not mean word or speech (VII. 3. 67) and not when it is preceded by any other preposition. As अविवाक्य-महरिते परन्ति ॥ This even in a very restricted sense, namely on the tenth day of the Daśarātra ceremony. In other places we have अविव. च्य ॥

As वाच्यमाह, अवाच्यमाह, but अवधुधितं वाक्यमाह ॥

कृस AFFIX.

1437

69. भोज्य preserves its palatal in the sense of 'eatable'.

The word is derived from भुज् with ण्यन् in the sense of 'able'. As भोज्य भोजनः 'eatable rice', भोज्या यवागुः 'eatable barley-gruel'. भक्ष्य here means anything which is fit for being eaten. When not having this sense, we have भोज्यः कञ्चनः ॥

धोळोपो लेटि वा ॥ ७० ॥ पदानि ॥ घोः, लोपः, लेटि, वा, ॥
वृत्तिः ॥ पुंसजकानां लेटि परतो वा लोपो भवति ॥

70. The final of दा and धा (धु roots) may optionally be elided in the Subjunctive (लेट्) ॥

As इधदृश्वा दाशुये Rig I. 35. 8. सामा वदद् गन्धर्वाय Rig X. 85. 41. But also यदग्निरग्नये दवान् ॥ The form दवान्, however, may also be deduced even when the final of दा is elided, for then by the आट् augment (III. 4. 94) we get this form. The word वा is therefore employed in the sūtra only for the sake of distinctness, for the sūtra without वा would have also given the above forms, as we have shown. Or the वा is used to remove the doubt which one may entertain to this effect "दवान् is the form which may be deduced by the general rule, since लोप is taught, this form will be excluded altogether and will never appear".

The form इधन् is thus evolved. We add तिप to the root धा; then the इ of ति is elided (III. 4. 97). दाशुये = यजमानाय रक्षानिदधात् ॥ Others say, the इधन् is the form of the root with the शल affix. इदन् is from the root दास ॥

Some say that वा is jñāpaka and indicates the existence of the following maxim:—अनित्यनागमशासनम् "the rule about augments is *anitya*". So that the augment आट् being *anitya*, we could not have got the form दवान् ॥ Hence the employment of the word वा ॥

ओतः दयनि ॥ ७१ ॥ पदानि ॥ ओतः, दयनि, ॥
वृत्तिः ॥ भोकारान्तस्याङ्गस्य दयनि परतो लोपो भवति ॥

71. A stem ending in ओ loses its final before the Present characteristic दयन् of the Divādi class.

As निञ्चति from शो, अवच्छयति from छो, अवधाति from शो, and अवस्थाति from शो ॥ The न् in ओन् is for the sake of euphony or ease of pronunciation.

According to Padamanjari, the sūtra should have been ओतः धाति, and thereby there would be the saving of half a mātrā, and also there would be no necessity of repeating the word धाति in VII. 3. 75.

कसस्याचि ॥ ७२ ॥ पदानि ॥ कसस्य, अचि, ॥
वृत्तिः ॥ कसस्याजादौ प्रत्यये लोपो भवति ॥

72. The अ of the Aorist characteristic कस is elided before an affix beginning with a vowel.

1438

[ Bk. VII Ch. III. §. 75

As अघुशाताम्, अघुशायाम्, अघुशि from the root दुइ ॥ Had the अ not been elided before आताम् and आयाम्, then इब must have been substituted for it according to VII. 2. 81. Why do we say before an affix beginning with a vowel? Observe अघुशत्, अघुशताम् ॥ Why do we say क्स and not only स? So that the elision should not take place here, as उस्ती, उस्ता; वस्ती, बस्ता; तृणती, तृणसः ॥

लुग्वा दुहदिहलिहगुहामात्मनेपदे दन्त्ये ॥ ७३ ॥ पदानि ॥ लुक्, वा, दुह, दिह, लिह, गुहाम्, आत्मनेपदे, दन्त्ये, ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ दुह विह लिह गुह इलेतेषामात्मनेपदे नत्यादि परतः क्सस्य वा लुग्वति ॥

73. The whole of the affix क्स is elided optionally before the personal endings of the Atmanepada beginning with a dental, after दुह, दिह, लिह and गुह ॥

As अदुग्ध or अघुशत, अदुग्धा or अघुशया; अदुग्धम् or अघुशध्वम्, अदुग्धहि or अघुशावहि, अदिग्ध or अधिशत, अतीह or अलिशत, अघुश or अघुशत ॥

Why दुह &c. only? Observe व्यत्यस्थत ॥ Why in the Atmanepada? Observe अघुशत only. Why before an affix beginning with a dental? Observe अघुशावहि only. Though the anuvritti of लोप was understood in this sutra; the employment of the term लुक् indicates that the whole of the affix is to be elided. For लोप would have elided only the final अ of स ॥ But even with the elision of अ alone we would have got all the above forms, except those in बहि ॥ For अ being elided, we have स् between इ (a consonant of झल् class) and a dental (which is also a letter of झल् class). This स् situate between two झल् will be elided by VIII. 2. 26. Nor can it be objected that the elided अ is sthanivat, for by पूर्ववर्तिसिंह VIII. 2. 1, such an elision cannot be sthanivat. Though इ is a dento-labial, yet it is included in the word dental. Had it not been meant to be so included, ती (letters of त class) would have been taken in the sutra. See III. 1. 45, for this Aorist-affix.

शामामहानां दीर्घः इयनि ॥ ७४ ॥ पदानि ॥ शामाम्, अष्टानाम्, दीर्घः, इयनि, ॥
वृत्तिः ॥ शामादीनामहानां दीर्घो भवति इयनि परतः ॥

74. Before the Present character इयन्, a long is substituted for the root-vowel in शम् and the seven roots that follow it.

As शाम्यति, शाय्यति, शाय्यति, शाय्यति, शाय्यति, शाय्यति, शाय्यति and माय्यति ॥ Why of these eight only? Observe अस्यति ॥ Why before इयन्? Observe अमति; the अयन् being optional after this root by III. 1. 70.

छिदुकुम्याचमां शिति ॥ ७५ ॥ पदानि ॥ छिदु, कुमु, आचमाम्, शिति, ॥
वृत्तिः ॥ दीर्घ इति वर्तते ॥ छिदु कुमु आचम् इलेतेषां दीर्घो भवति शिति परतः ॥

75. Before any other Present character (शित्), the root vowel of छिदु, कलम्, and आ-चम् is lengthened.

BK. VII. CH. III §. 78] SOME SUBSTITUTES.

1439

As क्षीषति, क्षामति, and क्षा क्षामति ॥ क्षमः lengthens its vowel before क्षमः by the last rule, the present rule produces this change before the affix क्षप् also, which it gets by III. 1. 70. क्षमः lengthens its vowel only when it is preceded by क्षा; therefore not here: क्षमति, विष्टमति or क्षमति ॥ The sutra is exhibited as क्षिष्कृक्ष क्षमा क्षिति in the original text of Pāṇini; the present form, owes its existence to the insertion of क्षा from the vārtika क्षीष्वमाङ्क क्षमः ॥

क्रमः परस्मैपदेषु ॥ ७६ ॥ पदानि ॥ क्रमः, परस्मैपदेषु, ॥
वृत्तिः ॥ क्षीष इति वर्तते ॥ क्रमः परस्मैपदेषु क्षिति परतो क्षीषो भवति ॥

76. The long is substituted in क्रम, before a क्षित् affix, in the Parasmaipada.

As क्षामति, क्षामतः, क्षामन्ति ॥ Why in the Parasmaipada? Observe क्षामते क्षादित्यः ॥ How do you explain the lengthening in क्षाम and क्षाम (Imperative 2nd Per. Sg.)? For when क्षि is elided by क्षुक्, (VI. 4. 105) then by I. 1. 63, the affix being dropped by a क्षु-elision, it would produce no effect and so there ought to have been no lengthening? This is no valid objection. The prohibition of I. 1. 63, applies to the क्षु stem after which the affix is elided. Here क्षम is not a stem or aṅga with regard to क्षि, but it is a stem with regard to क्षप्, as क्षम + क्षप् + क्षि ॥ Therefore, though क्षि is elided, the lengthening will take place by I. 1. 62, (प्रत्यय लक्षणम्) ॥

क्षु गमियमां छः ॥ ७७ ॥ पदानि ॥ क्षु, गमि, यमाम्, छः, ॥
वृत्तिः ॥ क्षितीति वर्तते ॥ क्षु गमि यम इत्येतेषां क्षिति प्रत्यये परतः छकारादिशो भवति ॥

77. छ is substituted for the final of क्षु, गम् and यम् before a Present-character (क्षित्) ॥

As क्षु, गच्छति, यच्छति ॥ The क्षु with the indicatory क्षु is taken here, (Tud. 59), and not क्षु of Divādi (19) class or of Kryādi class (53). There we have क्षुति and क्षुणाति respectively. Those who do not read the sutra as क्षु &c, but as क्षुमि &c, read the anuvṛtti of the word क्षु from VII. 3. 72 into this sutra; so that the क्षित् is qualified by the word क्षु, i. e. a क्षित् affix which is merely a vowel, and has no consonant in it; (and not a क्षित् affix which begins with a vowel). Therefore though क्षुमि is a क्षित् affix beginning with a vowel, yet as it contains a consonant, the क्षु substitution does not take place, as क्षुमि (III. 1. 83) The reading of the text according to Patanjali and Kātyayana is क्षुमियमां छः, and hence the necessity of the above explanation. The reading क्षु, though convenient, is not ārsha.

पाद्माध्मास्याक्षादाणहृदयतिसातिशदसदां पिबजिघधमतिष्ठमनयच्छपश्यच्छधीशी-
यसीदाः ॥ ७८ ॥ पदानि ॥ पा, धा, ध्मा, स्था, क्षा, दाण, हशि, अत्ति, सन्ति, शद,
सदाम्, पिब, जिघ, धम, तिष्ठ, मन, यच्छ, पश्य, क्षुच्छ, धी, शीय, सीदाः ॥

SHORTENING.

[BK. VII. CH. III. § 80]

वृत्तिः ॥ पा प्रा घुमा स्था प्रा बाणु हसि अर्ति सर्ति श्व सव इलेतेषां पिब जिघ्र धम तिष्ठ मन यच्छ पदय
कृच्छ धी-शीय सीद इलेते आवेशा भवन्ति शिति परतः ॥

78. Before a Present-character (शित्), the following substitutions take place :—पिब् for पा, जिघ्र for प्रा, धम for ध्मा, तिष्ठ for स्था, मन for झा, यच्छ for दा (दाण्), पदय for दृश, कृच्छ for कृ, धी for सु, शीय् for शदू and सीदू for सदू ॥

As पिबति, जिघ्रति, धमति, तिष्ठति, मनति, यच्छति, पदयति, कृच्छति, धावति, शीयते and सीदति ॥ पिब्+शप्+तिप् required Guṇa of the इ of पि by VII. 3. 86, it however does not take place on the maxim अङ्गवृत्ते पुनर्वृत्तावधिः “when an operation which is taught in the angādhikāra, has taken place, and another operation of the angādhikāra is subsequently applicable, this latter operation is not allowed to take place”. Or the substitute पिब is one which ends with झा, and is acutely accented on the first. It must be acutely accented on the first; otherwise by VI. 1. 162, the acute will be on the last पिब् ॥ Then when there is ekādeśa with शप्, the acute will be on the middle in पिबति, which is not desired. धी is substituted for सु when the sense is ‘to run, move quickly’; in any other sense, we have प्रसरति, अनुसरति ॥

ज्ञाजनोजो ॥ ७६ ॥ पदानि ॥ झा, जनोः, जा, ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ झा जन इलेतेषां अवेशो भवति शिति परतः ॥

79. Before a शित् affix, जा is substituted for झा and जन ॥

As जानाति and जायते ॥ The जन here belongs to Divādi class, meaning ‘to be produced’, and not जन of the Juhotyādi class. Why जा (long) and not झा, for this ज would assume the form जा by VII. 3. 101? This long आ of जा indicates the existence of the maxim given above in VII. 3. 78; and had ज been the substitute, VII. 3. 101, could not have lengthened it.

प्यादीनां ह्रस्वः ॥ ८० ॥ पदानि ॥ पू, आदीनाम्, ह्रस्वः, ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ पू इलेतेषां अवेशो भवति शिति परतः ॥

80. A short is substituted for पू &c, before a शित् affix.

The Pvādi roots form a subdivision of the Kryādi class, beginning with पूष् पयने (2) and ending with स्त्री गतौ (32). The स्वादि roots (VIII. 2. 44) are a portion of प्यादि (nos 13 to 32). Others hold that upto the end of the Kryādi class are Pvādi. Thus पुनाति, लुनाति, स्तुणाति ॥ Those who hold that Pvādi roots are upto the end of the Class, explain the non-shortening of जानाति (for झा would also then become Pvādi), by saying that the express

text of VII. 3. 79, substituting long आ prevents the shortening. They say had हा been also shortened, then merely ज substitute would have been enough and not आ; and this ज would have been lengthened in the case of जन् by VII. 3. 101, to form जायते ॥

मीनातेनिगमे ॥ ८१ ॥ पदानि ॥ मीनातेः, निगमे, ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ मीनातेरङ्गस्य शिति प्रत्यये परता द्रव्यो भवति निगमविषये ॥

81. In the Veda मो is shortened before a शित् affix.

As प्रमिनन्ति व्रतानि Rig. X. 10. 5. The न becomes ण (प्रमिनन्ति according to Kāśika) by VIII. 4. 15. Why in the Veda? Observe प्र मीणाति ॥

मिदेरगुणः ॥ ८२ ॥ पदानि ॥ मिदेः, गुणः, ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ मिदेरङ्गस्येको गुणो भवति शिति प्रत्यये परतः ॥

82. For इ in मिद्, there is substituted a guna before a शित् affix.

As मेधाति, मेधतः, मेधान्ति ॥ Why मिद् only? Observe स्विधान्ति, विन्धान्ति ॥ The root निमिदा belongs both to the Bhvādi and the Divādi classes. The Bhvādi मिद् will get guna before इष by virtue of VII. 3. 86, but the Divādi मिद् would not have got guna before इषन्, as this affix is इन् (I. 2. 4): hence the necessity of this sūtra. Before non इषन् affixes there is no guna, as मिधति, मामधति ॥

जुसि च ॥ ८३ ॥ पदानि ॥ जुसि, च, ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ जुसि च प्रत्यये परत इगन्तस्याङ्गस्य गुणो भवति ॥

83. Before the personal-ending जुस् (उस्) of the Imperfect, guna is substituted for the final इ, ई, उ, ऊ, ऋ, and ऋ, ल of the stem.

As अजुहृतः, अविभयुः, अविभरः, अजागरः ॥ This Personal ending is इन् according to I. 2. 4, and would not have caused guna (I. 1. 5), but for this sūtra. The ending जुस् (III. 4. 108) comes in the लङ् also. There, however, it does not cause guna. As चिन्तुः, सुनुतुः ॥ Here there are two इन् affixes, the augment यामुद, and the sārvadhātuka जुस्; and the यामुद prevents guna. The इक् is read into the sūtra from I. 1. 3.

सार्वधानुकाञ्चेधातुकयोः ॥ ८४ ॥ पदानि ॥ सार्वधानुक, आञ्चेधातुकयोः, ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ सार्वधानुके आञ्चेधातुके च प्रत्यये परत इगन्तस्याङ्गस्य गुणो भवति ॥

84. The Guna is substituted for the final इक् vowel of a stem before the affixes called sārvadhātuka and ārdhadhātuka (III. 4. 113 &c).

GUNA.

BK. VII. CH. III. §. 85]

As तरति, नयति, भवति; कर्तृ, चेत्, स्तोतु, ॥ Why sārvadhātuka and ārdhadhātuka affixes only? Observe अग्निस्वम् अग्निकाम्यति ॥ For had the sūtra been सङ् then the rule would have applied to affixes like सन् काम्यच &c which go to form Denominative verbs. सङ् includes all affixes beginning with सन् and ending with सङ् ॥ If the sūtra had been मस्ये, then the rule would have applied to the affixes like स्वम् &c. To exclude these cases, the two words sārvadhātuka and ārdhadhātuka are used. For exceptions See I. 1. 4, 5, 6.

जाग्रोऽविचिण्णलङ्कित्सु ॥ ८५ ॥ पदानि ॥ जाग्रः, अ, विच्, चिण्, णक्, ङित्सु ॥
वृत्तिः ॥ जाग्र इत्येतस्याङ्गस्य गुणो भवति अविचिण्णलङ्कित्सु परतः ॥

85. The Guṇa is substituted for the ऋ of the stem जाग्र, except before the affix वि, before the Aorist-character चिण्, before the Personal ending, णक् of the Perfect, and before an affix with an indicatory ऋ ॥

As जागरयति, with णक्, जागरकः (with णक्) साधुजागरी, जागरं जागरम् (with णक्) जागरो वर्तते (with षक्), जागरितः (with क्), जागरितवान् (with क्तक्) ॥ This is an exception to the Vṛiddhi rule of VII. 2. 115, and to the prohibition in I. 1. 5. When this guṇa is substituted, there does not take effect that rule, which causes Vṛiddhi of the penultimate short अ of जागर; (अत उपधायाः VII. 2. 116). Had that been the case, then the guṇa substitution would become simply useless, and the prohibition with regard to चिण् and णक् superfluous. Why do we say not before वि, चिण् and णक् and ङित्? Observe जागृवि: (with the affix वि, Unādi) अजागरि with चिण् which causes Vṛiddhi, and अजागरि with णक्, and जागृतः and जागरः with a ङित् (I. 2. 4) affix. Some hold that the ऋ in वि is for the sake of pronunciation only, and the prohibition applies to all affixes beginning with a व, such as क्त्, as अजागृवान्, here there is no guṇa. In अजागरः with जुस् the guṇa takes place by virtue of VII. 3. 83: for though it is a ङित् affix also, the prohibition ङित्सु of this sūtra does not affect it. Similarly अहं अजागर with णक् the optional guṇa VII. 1. 91 is also not prohibited by the णक् of this sūtra. In fact the phrase अविचिण् णक् ङित्सु is a Paryudāsa prohibition: for had it been a prasayya-pratishedha, then the guṇa before जुस् and the 1st Pers. णक् would also have been prohibited. In short this sūtra positively ordains guṇa of जागृ before every affix, other than वि, चिण्, णक् and ङित्, and if by any other rule these latter would cause guṇa, that guṇa is not prohibited. That is the result of Paryudāsa negation.

But if the sūtra be construed as a Prasayyapratishedha, then we shall apply the maxim अनन्तरस्य विधिर्वा भवति प्रतिषेधो वा ॥ The prohibition is therefore stated with regard to जाग्र in connection with the affixes वि, चिण्, णक् and ङित् ॥ But the Guṇa ordained by VII. 3. 84, 83 is not prohibited.

पुणन्तलघुपधस्य च ॥ ८६ ॥ पदानि ॥ पुक् अन्त, लघु उपधस्य, च, ॥
वृत्तिः ॥ पुणन्तस्याङ्गस्य लघुपधस्य च सार्वधातुकाद्विधातुकयोर्गुणो भवति ॥

Kārikā:—संयोगे गृहसंज्ञायां गुणो भेत्तुनं सिध्यति ।
विध्यपेक्षे लघोभासो कथं कुण्डिनं दुध्यति ॥
धातोर्हितुं कथं रञ्जे, स्वादिभ्रध्योर्निपातनात् ।
अनहोपशिरीर्यैर्वे विध्यपेक्षे न सिध्यतः ॥
अन्यस्तस्य यदाहाचि लङ्घ्यं तत्कृते भवेत् ।
कटुसनो यत्कृते कित्त्वं ज्ञापकं स्वाह्वयोर्गुणं ॥

86. Guna is substituted before a sārvadhāṭuka and an ārdhadhāṭuka affix, for the **इक्** vowels of the Causative stems which take the augment **प्** (VII. 3. 36), and for the short penultimate vowel of a root which ends in a single consonant.

As **ळेपयति**, **हेपयति**, **क्रोपयति**, **भेदनम्**, **छेदनम्**, **भेत्ता**, **छेत्ता** ॥ Of course the vowel should be laghu or light, before the addition of the affix; the heaviness caused by the addition of the affix, will not prevent guna. Thus **भिद् + तु**, though **द + तु = तु** causes the **इ** to become heavy, that will not prevent guna: for **विध्यपेक्षे लघु भङ्गम्** ॥ Obj: If this be so, why the forms **कुण्डित्**, **हण्डित्** are not incorrect, for in them also the vowel is laghu (the roots are **कुह्** and **हुह्**), and the augment **व्** is added afterwards by a Vidhi rule? Ans. The augment **व्** is added to the *root*, and becomes upadesivat. (See VII. 1. 58). Obj. If so, how do you cause Vṛiddhi in **रञ्ज्**, as in **रागः** with **पञ्च्**; as **रञ्ज् + पञ्च् = रञ्ज् + पञ्च्** (the **व्** being dropped by VI. 4. 27), for it is *after* the elision of **अ**, that the **अ** of **रञ्ज्** becomes penultimate and can admit of Vṛiddhi by VII. 2. 116? Ans. The exceptional forms **स्वः** from **स्वन्द् + पञ्च्**, and **अयः** from **अन्य + पञ्च्**, taught in VI. 4. 28, 29 teach by implication that roots of this form take Vṛiddhi as a *general* rule. Obj. If the **विध्यपेक्षे** maxim is not of universal application: though by VI. 4. 134, the **अ** of **अन्** &c. is elided in bha stems, like **राजन्** thus **राजा**; yet the **अ** should not be elided if you be consistent, in **अनह्** augment added by VII. 1. 75 to **दधि**, **अस्थि** &c. In fact, you could not get the forms **दधा सकृधा** &c. Moreover though there can be the lengthening of the penultimate in **सानन्—सानानि** (before **धि** affix Nom. Pl), yet not in the case of **कुण्डानि** from **कुण्ड** for here **व्** is added by another rule VII. 1. 72. If you say, the maxim is not of universal application, then there can be no guna of **इ** in **भिद्** to form **भेत्तु** ॥ Ans. The guna takes place in forms like **भेत्तु** &c, because the prohibition of the following rule VII. 3. 87, with regard to the affixes beginning with a *vowel*, proves by implication that before affixes beginning with a consonant, as **तु**, the guna also takes place. Obj. The prohibition in the case of vowel beginning affixes is for the sake of **लङ्**, to form **अनेनक्** ॥ This is derived from **निजिर्** (Juhotyadi 11), in the Imperfect, as **अ + निज् + शप् + लुप् + तिप्** then reduplication (VI. 1. 10), then guna of the redupli-

BK. VII. CH. III. §. 87]

cate, (VII. 4. 75), then लिप which had become न in the Imperfect, is elided by VI. 1. 68. Thus अनिज्+अतु+न=अ+निनिज्+न (VI. 1. 10)= अ निनिज्+न (VII. 4. 75)= अ निनिज् (VI. 1. 98)=अननक. The elided न produces its effect, the guna by VII. 3. 86. This is why अच् is taken in sūtra VII. 3. 87, namely अजान affixes do not cause guna, the हलाव affixes like न cause guna. You cannot therefore say that आच् in VII. 3. 87 is a jñāpaka. Ans. The sūtra वसिगुधिधुविशेषेः कुः (III. 2. 140) teaches the addition of तु to बर् &c, as गुध्वः; if this तु had not tended to cause the guna of the penultimate vowels of these roots, what was the necessity of making this affix a क्त? Similarly I. 2. 10 teaches that सन् (Desiderative) is क्त after roots ending in consonants. These rules show that words like भल &c get guna, and the final consonant of the root plus the initial consonant of the affix, does not make the root vowel heavy. Obj: The क्त of सन् is for the sake of the elision of the nasal, in धिप्सति, धाप्सति (VI. 4. 24). Ans. Let it be so, still the क्त of क्त is enough for us.

The 'upadhā short' must be the vowels of the इक् pratyāhāra. Therefore in भिन्ति, the penultimate is short अ (of ञम्) and it does not take guna. In fact, the word penultimate qualifies the word इक् understood. Others explain it by saying that पुगन्त is to be analysed by पुक्खिन्त 'in the vicinity of प्' ॥ The word अन्त means समीप, and means the इक् vowel in the proximity of पुक् ॥ The word लघुपथा should be analysed as लघ्वी उपथा and is a Karmadhāraya compound, and means 'a short or light penultimate'. The word पुगन्तलघुपथ is a Samāhara Dvandva.

नाभ्यस्तस्याचि पिति सार्वधातुके ॥ ५७ ॥ पदानि ॥ न, अभ्यस्तस्य, अचि, पिति, सार्वधातु के ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अभ्यस्तसंज्ञकस्याङ्गस्य लघुपथस्याजारी पिति सार्वधातुके गुणो न भवति ॥
वार्तिकम् ॥ बहुलं छन्दसीति वक्तव्यम् ॥

87. The guna is not substituted for the penultimate light इक् vowel in the reduplicated form of a root, before a Sārvadhātuka affix beginning with a vowel and having an indicatory प् ॥

As निनिजानि, अनिनिजम्; परि देवियाणि, पर्यवेदिषम् ॥ Why of a reduplicated root? Observe वेदानि ॥ Why beginning with a vowel? Observe निनेत्ति ॥ The word पितृ is read here for the sake of the subsequent sūtras like VII. 3. 92. For here in cases other than पितृ, guna will be prevented by डिन्त because of सार्वधातुकमपितृ ॥ Why a sārvadhātuka affix? Observe निनेज in the Perfect, the affixes of which are ārdhadhātuka (III. 4. 115). Why do we say a penultimate light vowel? Observe जुहुवानि, अजुहुवम् ॥

Vārt:— There is diversity in the Vedas. As जुजापत् the लेद् of जुहु ॥

The forms पञ्चशत, चाकशति, वावसीति: are irregular. स्पश्+लेद्=स्पश्+आद्+ते=स्पश्+शपवल्+आति=पस्पशति ॥
