The above forms are thus evolved. 1. ने निजानि is लेद (Imperative 1st Per Sing), the ग is changed to नि, the augment आट is added which is पत् (आह-समस्य पश्च III. 4. 92), ऋतु is substituted for शप्, then there is reduplication, then guna by VII. 4. 75. 2. अनानजम् is लङ्, the गप is changed to अन् ॥ 3. वशानि is 1st Pers. Sing. Imperative of बद् ॥ 4. ननान्क is 3rd Person singular of the Present. 5. ननज is the Perfect with णल which is ārdhādhtuka III. 4. 115. 6. ऊजायत् is the लट of जुपी प्रातसवनयोः (Tudādi 8), in the Parasmaipada, the इ of तिप is elided (III. 4. 97), then is added the augment अद् (III. 4. 94) then शप् is irregularly replaced by ऋतु, then reduplication.

In the words पस्पशाते &c. the reduplicate has been shortened, as a Vedic form, in the Intensive यद् लुक् ॥ चाकशीत् is from कामुवासि there is (यद् लुक्, लद्, तिप्, and इद् augment by यद्वा वा (VII. 3. 94). वावशीतीः is from वामुवीती, in the Intensive (यदुलुक्), लद्, शत्, दीप and शस i. e. it is the Accusative plural of the Feminine Present Participle from the Intensive root of वाश् ॥ The reading in the Kāsikā is वावशाते ॥ In these two काश् and वाश् the roots have been shortened. Or the above forms may be derived regularly, without shortening, from the roots कश् and वश् ॥

भूसुवोस्तिडि ॥ ८८ ॥ पदानि ॥ भूः सुवोः, तिडि ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ भूः सु इयेतयोस्तिडि सार्वधातुके गुणो न भवति ॥

88. भू and सू get no guna before an immediately following Personal ending which is Sārvadhātuka.

As अमृत, अमृः, अमुवमः, सुवे, सुवावहे, सुवावहे ॥ The सू refers to the Adādi root (21) in which the Present character is dropped, and does not refer to Divādi (24) or Tudādi (115) roots, because there the Present character ऋन् and श intervene between the Personal endings (तिङ्) and the root: and moreover the affixes ऋन् and श are ङिन् (I. 2. 4) and would not cause guna. Why do we say before तिङ्? Observe भवति where the guna takes place before शप् ॥ Why before a sārvadhātuka affix? Observe व्यति भविषीष्ठ, where the Benedictive is not a Sārvadhātuka (III. 4. 116), and the augment is of course considered as a portion of the personal ending. Why the guna is not prohibited in बामुवीति when the Intensive यद् is dropped, and the Personal ending is added directly to the root. Because the form बामुतु in VII. 4. 65 indicates by implication that guna takes place in यदुलुक् except in बामुतु ॥

But of सू we have सोयुवीति where guna has been prohibited in the Intensive, because there is no jñāpaka with regard to it.

The forms सुवे &c are the 1st Per. Imperative of सू ॥

उतो वृद्धिलुकि हलि ॥ ८९ ॥ पदानि ॥ उतः, वृद्धिः, लुकि, हलि ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ सार्वधातुके पित्तीति वर्तते ॥ उकागन्तस्याद्वृश्य वृद्धिभवति लुकि सति हनादि पित्ति सार्वधातुके ॥

89. A root ending in short उ, which has no Present

1446

GUNA

[ Bk. VII. Ch. III. § 92.

characteristic ( i. e. the vikaraṇa is dropped by luk elision ), gets vriddhi, before a पित्त Sārvadhātuka affix beginning with a consonant, but not if the stem is reduplicated.

Thus औति, औधि, औनि; औति, औधि, औनि, स्तौति, स्तौधि, स्तौनि ॥ Why ending in ऋ? Observe एति, एधि, एनि ॥ Why do we say whose vikaraṇa is elided by झुक? Observe पुनोति, पुनोति, पुनोति ॥ Why beginning with a हल? Observe श्रवाणि, श्रवाणि, the First Person of the Imperative is पित्त by III. 4. 92, Why before a पित्त affix? Observe पुनः, स्वतः ॥ The augment यासुद् being पित्त (III. 4. 103), prevents पित्त action in अपि स्तुयात् राजानम् ॥ The phrase नान्यस्तस्य should be read into the sūtra from VII. 3. 87: therefore Vriddhi does not take place here योयोति मोनोति ॥ Here there is luk-elision of ब्रह्म ॥

ऊर्णोतिविमापा ॥ ६० ॥ पदानि ॥ ऊर्णोतिः, विमापा ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ ऊर्णोतिविमापा वृद्धिर्भवति हताशे पित्ति सार्वधातुके ॥

90. Before a पित्त Sārvadhātuka affix beginning with a consonant, the final ऋ of ऊर्णु gets optionally vriddhi.

As प्रोणोति or प्रोणोति, प्रोणोति or प्रोणोति, प्रोणोति or प्रोणोति; but प्रोणोति before an affix beginning with a vowel.

गुणोऽपृक्ते ॥ ६१ ॥ पदानि ॥ गुणः, अपृक्ते ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ ऊर्णोतिविमापृक्ते हति पित्ति सार्वधातुके गुणो भवति ॥

91. Before a पित्त Sārvadhātuka affix which is a single consonant, Guna is substituted for the final of ऊर्णु ॥

As प्रोणोत, प्रोणोः ॥ Though the anuvṛtti of ह्यप् was understood in this sūtra from the last aphorism, the employment of the term अपृक्त implies the existence of the following maxim:—यस्मिन् विधि स्तवावावत् महते “when a term which denotes a letter is exhibited in a rule, in the form of a Locative case, and qualifies something else which likewise stands in the Locative case, that which is qualified by it must be regarded as beginning with the letter which is denoted by the term in question, and not as ending with it”.

तृणह इम् ॥ ६२ ॥ पदानि ॥ तृणहः, इम् ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ तृणह इत्येतस्यादृश्य इमागमो भवति हति पित्ति सार्वधातुके ॥

92. Before a पित्त Sārvadhātuka affix beginning with a consonant, इ is added after अ of the verbal stem तृणह ॥

As तृणहि, तृणेति, तृणेति, अतृणेह ॥ In the last example though the affix vanishes altogether, yet it produces its effect. Why beginning with a consonant? Observe तृणहानि ॥ Why a पित्त affix? Observe तृणः with तस ॥ The stem तृणह is formed from the root तृह (Rudhādi) with the vikaraṇa यम्, and is so exhibited in the sūtra in order to indicate that the augment इम् is added after the vikaraṇa यम् has been added, and that the root तृह of Tudādi class is not to be taken.

BK. VII. CH. III §. 95]

ईद AUGMENT.

1447

The above forms are thus derived :—

तूह + इनम् + तिप् = तृणह + इम् + ति = तृणह + ति = तृणह + ति (VI. 1. 87) = तृणह + ति (VIII. 2. 31) = तृणह + ति (VIII. 2. 40) = तृणह + ति (VIII. 4. 41) = तृणह with the elision of one इ (VIII. 3. 13). The form तृणहि is similarly formed by VIII. 2. 41, the इ being changed to क् before सि of सिप् ॥ अतृणह is the लङ् 2nd and 3rd Per. Sing.

ध्रुव ईद ॥ ६३ ॥ पदानि ॥ ध्रुवः, ईद ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ इ इत्येतस्मादुत्तरस्य हलादेः पितः सार्वधातुकस्य ईदागमो भवति ॥

93. Before a पितृ Sārvadhātuka affix beginning with a consonant, the augment ईद is placed after न् ॥

As ब्रवीति, ब्रवीधि, ब्रवीनि, अब्रवीत् ॥ But ब्रवाणि before such an affix beginning with a vowel, and हृतः before an affix which is not पितृ ॥

यङो वा ॥ ६४ ॥ पदानि ॥ यङः, वा, ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ यङ उत्तरस्य हलादेः पितः सार्वधातुकस्य ईदागमो भवति वा ॥

94. The पितृ Sārvadhātuka affixes, beginning with a consonant, optionally get the augment इद in the Intensive.

As लालपीति in शाकुनिको लालपीति, so also दुन्दुभिर्व्यवतीति, विधावद्रो वृषभो रोवतीति महादेवोभर्त्यो आविवेश ॥ (Rig. IV. 58. 3). Also not, as वर्धति चक्रम् and वर्धति ॥ These are all examples of the Intensive with the elision of यङ् ॥ When the stem retains यङ्, there can be no पितृ Sārvadhātuka affix beginning with a consonant after it, because then शप् will intervene between the affix and the stem. Hence no examples of the same can be given.

तुरुस्तुशाम्यमः सार्वधातुके ॥ ६५ ॥ पदानि ॥ तु, रु, स्तु, शमि, अमः, सार्वधातु के ॥
वृत्तिः ॥ तु इति सौचोयं धातुः, रु शब्ने हुम् स्तुतो शम उदशमे अम गत्याविषु इत्येत्येवः परस्य सार्वधातुकस्य हलादेवो इदागमो भवति ॥

95. A sārvadhātuka affix, beginning with a consonant, optionally gets ईद augment, after the roots तु, रु, स्तु, शम् and अम् ॥

The root तु (Adādi 25) means 'to increase', रु (Adādi 24) 'to make a sound', स्तु (Adādi 34) 'to praise', शम् 'to be satisfied', and अम् 'to go'. According to Kāśikā तु is a Sautra dhātu. Thus उत्तीति or उत्तवीति, उपतीति or उपपतीति, उपपतीति or उपपतीति, शाप्यध्वम् or शमीध्वम्, अभ्यमति or अभ्यमति ॥ शम् and अम् can then be followed by a consonant beginning sārvadhātuka affix, when they lose their Present character (vikaraṇa) as a Vedic anomaly (bahulam chhandasi).

The Apisālās read the sūtra as तुरुस्तुशाम्यमः सार्वधातुकावृच्छन्ति ॥ This will then become a विधि rule for the Vedic forms. The word सार्वधातुका is here exhibited in the feminine.

1448

ईद AUGMENT.

[ Bk. VII Ch. III. §. 98

The repetition of 'sārvadhātuka', though its anuvṛtti was present is for the sake of stopping the anuvṛtti of पित्र, and this rule applies to आपत् affixes also, as सुवीत, रामाच्छम् ॥

अस्तिसिचोऽपृक्ते ॥ ६६ ॥ पदानि ॥ अस्ति, सिचः, अ, पृक्ते ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अस्तित्वात् सिजन्ताच परस्यापृक्तस्य सार्वधातुकस्य ईदागमो भवति ॥

वातिकम् ॥ आहिमुवारीति प्रतिषेधः ॥

96. A single consonantal sārvadhātuka affix gets the augment ईद, after अस् (अस्ति) and after the Aorist character सिच् ॥

As आसात्, आसीः; अकार्यात्, असावीत् ॥ Why do we say a single-consonant affix? Observe आस्त, अकार्यम् ॥

Vārt:—Prohibition of the sthānivad-bhāva must be stated when आह् is substituted for इ (III. 4. 84), and भू for अस् (II. 4. 52), before the augment ईद ॥ Therefore not here आत्य and अनृत् ॥ The word आत्य is thus formed. आह्+सिप्=आह्+यत् (III. 4. 84)=आए+य (VIII. 2. 35)=आत्+य (VIII. 4. 55) =आतय ॥

बहुलं छन्दसि ॥ ९७ ॥ पदानि ॥ बहुलम्, छन्दसि ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अस्तिसिचोऽपृक्तस्य सार्वधातुकस्य ईदागमो भवति बहुलं छन्दसि विधेय ॥

97. In the Veda, a single consonantal Sārvadhātuka affix gets diversely the augment ईद, after अस् and सिच् ॥

As आप एवेव साललं सर्वमाः ॥ Here आः is used instead of आसीत्; but also अहंवासात् राचिः (See Maitr. S. I. 5. 12). So also with s-Aorist, as गोभिरक्षाः (Rig IX. 107. 9), प्रलङ्घनस्साः (Rig X. 28. 4). And अङ्गैषीर्मा पुत्रक, the अह् is not elided though मा is added (VI. 4. 75). अक्षाः and अस्साः are examples of सिच् without इद. Compare VIII. 2. 73.

The word आः is the लङ् of अस्, there is added सिप्, then यप् is elided, then सू is changed to र्, and it is turned to visarjaniya. The words अक्षाः and अस्साः are derived from the roots सत् (संबलम्) and स्सत् (छद्मगती), in the Aorist, the सिच् is elided (VI. 1. 68), the सिच् is elided by VIII. 2. 24, and the इ of the roots is changed to visarga. The augment ईद is not added as a Vedic irregularity.

रुद्रश्च पञ्चभ्यः ॥ ९८ ॥ पदानि ॥ रुद्रः, च, पञ्चभ्यः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ रुद्राश्रयः परस्य सार्वधातुकस्य हलाद्रेपृक्तस्य ईदागमो भवति ॥

98. After रुद्र and the four roots that follow it, comes the augment ईद to a sārvadhātuka affix consisting of a single consonant.

As अरोवात्, अरोवीः, अस्वपीत् and अस्वपीः, अश्वसीत्, अश्वसीः, प्राणीत्, प्राणीः, अजशीत्, अजशीः ॥ Why of these five only? Observe अजाग्र, भवान् ॥ Why an aprikta affix? Observe रोविति ॥ The word रुद्रः is singular, though it ought to have been plural.

BK. VII. CH. III §. 102.]

LENGTHENING.

1449

अङ्गार्यगालवयोः ॥ ९९ ॥ पदानि ॥ अद्, गार्य, गालवयोः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ रुद्रादिभ्यः पञ्चभ्यः परस्य अपृक्तस्य सार्वधातुकस्याङ्गार्यो भवन्ति गार्यगालवयोर्मतेन ॥

99. According to the opinion of Gārgya, and Gālāva, the augment अद् comes before a Sārvadhātuka affix consisting of a single consonant, after the above five roots रुद् &c.

As अरावत्, अरोदः, अस्वपत्, अस्वपः, अश्वसत्, अश्वसः, प्राणत्, प्राणः, अजशत्, अजशः ॥
The names of Gārgya and Gālāva are mentioned for honoris causa.

The mention of these names is not for the sake of 'option' (विकल्पार्थम्). Because the very injunction about अद्, would make the ईद of the preceding sūtra optional. The mention of more than one Achārya in the sūtra is also for this very reason.

अदः सर्वेषाम् ॥ १०० ॥ पदानि ॥ अदः, सर्वेषाम् ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अद् भक्षण अस्मादुत्तरस्यापृक्तस्य सार्वधातुकस्याङ्गार्यो भवति सर्वेषामाचार्यार्णा मतेन ॥

100. After अद् 'to eat', comes the augment अद् before a Sārvadhātuka affix consisting of a single consonant, according to the opinion of all grammarians.

As आवत् and आवः ॥ Before a non-aprikta we have अत्ति, अस्ति ॥ The word सर्वेषाम् makes it a necessary rule and not optional, like the last.

अतो दीर्घो यजि ॥ १०१ ॥ पदानि ॥ अतः, दीर्घः, यजि ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अकारान्तस्याङ्गस्य दीर्घो भवति यमादौ सार्वधातुके परतः ॥

101. The long आ is substituted for the final अ of a Tense-stem, before a Sārvadhātuka affix beginning with व् or म (lit. a consonant of यज् pratyāhāra).

As पञ्चानि, पञ्चाः, पञ्चाः, पञ्चानि, पञ्चाः, पञ्चाः ॥ Why 'for the अ only'? Observe चितुवः, चितुमः ॥ Why before a यज् consonant (semivowels, nasals and झ and म) only? Observe पञ्चतः, पञ्चाः ॥ Why a 'Sārvadhātuka'? Observe अङ्गना, केशवः ॥ Some read the anuvṛtti of तिङ् into this sūtra, from VII. 3. 88 so that the lengthening takes place only before Personal-endings. According to them before कुसु there is no lengthening, as भववान् ॥

The word भववान् is thus formed. To भू is added कुसु, then comes शप्, treating kvasu as a sārvadhātuka under III. 4. 117; the reduplication of the root ending in शप् is prevented, because the word dhātu is used in VI. 1. 8 which ordains reduplication of a root only, and not of a root plus a vikaraṇa like the form भव (भू-शप्) ॥ Those who do not read the anuvṛtti of तिङ् in this sūtra, but only of the word सार्वधातुके, they explain the form भववान् as a Vedic anomaly.

सुपि च ॥ १०२ ॥ पदानि ॥ सुपि, च ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अतो दीर्घो यमीयतुवर्तते । सुपि च यमादौ परतो ऽकारान्तस्याङ्गस्य दीर्घो भवति ॥

1450

SHORTENING.

[BK. VII. CH. III. § 105.]

102. Before a case-ending beginning with य or भ (lit a consonant of यज् Pratyāhāra), the final अ of a Nominal-stem is also lengthened.

The whole of the phrase अती वीचों यज् is understood here. Thus वृक्षाय, प्लक्षाय, वृक्षाभ्याय, प्लक्षाभ्याय ॥ But अग्निभ्याय where the stem ends in इ, and वृक्षस्य प्लक्षस्य where the affix does not begin with a यज् consonant.

बहुवचने झलयेत ॥ १०३ ॥ पदानि ॥ बहुवचने, झलि, एत ॥
वृत्तिः ॥ बहुवचने झलयो सुपि परतोऽकारान्तस्याङ्गस्य एकारादेशो भवति ॥

103. Before a case-ending beginning with भ or स (lit. a झल् consonant), in the Plural, ए is substituted for the final अ of a Nominal-stem.

As वृक्षेभ्यः, प्लक्षेभ्यः, वृक्षेषु, प्लक्षेषु ॥ Why in the Plural? Observe वृक्षाभ्याय, प्लक्षाभ्याय ॥ Why before a case-affix beginning with a झल् consonant? Observe वृक्षाभ्याय (the lengthening here is by VI. 4. 3). Why a case-affix? Observe यजभ्याय, पचभ्याय ॥

ओसि च ॥ २०४ ॥ पदानि ॥ ओसि, च ॥
वृत्तिः ॥ ओसि परतोकारान्तस्याङ्गस्य एकारादेशो भवति ॥

104. Before the case-ending ओस्, ए is substituted for the final अ of a Nominal-stem.

As वृक्षयोः (Gen. dual) स्वं, प्लक्षयोः स्वम्, वृक्षयोः (Loc. dual) as वृक्षयोर्निधेहि, प्लक्षयोर्निधेहि ॥

आङ् चापः ॥ १०५ ॥ पदानि ॥ आङ्, चें, आपः ॥
वृत्तिः ॥ आङ् इति पूर्वाभ्यायनिर्देशेन तृतीयैकवचनं गृह्यते । तस्मिन्नाङ् परतवकारादेति च आवन्तस्याङ्गस्यैकारादेशो भवति ।

105. Before the case-endings ओस् and before आ of the Instrumental, ए is substituted for the final आ of the Feminine-affix.

आङ् is the name given to the affix दा, the Ins. Sg. by the ancient grammarians. As खटुया, मालया, खटुयोः, मालयोः, बहुराजया, कारीषगन्ध्या, बहुराजयोः, कारीषगन्ध्ययोः ॥ Why the आ of the Feminine affix only? Observe कीलालपा ब्राह्मणेन कीलालपोः ब्राह्मणकुलयोः ॥ Where ever की or आप् is employed in Grammar, they mean the long forms ई and आ, and not when they are shortened, therefore, not here, अतिखटुन ब्राह्मणकुलेन ॥

The word कीलालपा is derived from कीलालं पिबाति with the affix विच् (III. 2. 74). In the Ins. Sing. the final आ is elided by VI. 4. 140. Had therefore, आ only been used in the sūtra, instead of आप्, there would have been ए substitution in the case of कीलालपा also; for the लेप् rule VI. 4. 140 would find its scope in कीलालपः पश्च &c, and would be debarred here by the present sūtra.

BK. VII. CH. III. § 108 ]

GUNA IN FEMININE

1451

The maxim **इषाव् महणोऽश्वमेधम्** is necessary, because otherwise on the maxim of sthānivadbhāva, the short substitutes of **इ** and **आ** would also be included. In fact, in the sūtra prohibiting sthānivad bhāva, we find this vārtika **इषाव् महणोऽश्वम्**: 'A short (not long) substitute of **इ** and **आ** is not sthānivat'.

**संवृद्धौ च ॥ १०६ ॥ पदानि ॥ सम्बुद्धौ, च ॥**

वृत्तिः ॥ आप इति वचते । संवृद्धौ च परत आबन्तस्याङ्गस्य एत्वं भवति ॥

106. **ए** is substituted for the final **आ** of a Feminine stem, in the Vocative Singular.

As हे खंडे, हे बहुराजे, हे कारीषगन्ध्ये ॥

**अम्बार्थनयोऽहस्वः ॥ १०७ ॥ पदानि ॥ अम्बार्थ, नयोः, हस्वः ॥**

वृत्तिः ॥ संवृद्धाविति वचते । अम्बार्थानामङ्गानां नयन्तानां हस्वो भवति, संवृद्धौ परतः ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ इलकवतीनां प्रतिषेधो वक्तव्यः ॥ वा० ॥ छन्दसि वेति वक्तव्यम् ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ ततो हस्वो वा डिसंबुद्धोरिति वक्तव्यम् ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ छन्दस्येव हस्व त्वामिष्यते ॥ मातृणां मातच् पुण्यार्थमर्हते ॥

107. A short vowel is substituted in the Voc. Sg. for the **आ** of the feminine, in the sense of 'mother, mother-dear', as well as for the long vowel of the Feminines called Nadi (I. 4. 3 &c).

As हे अम्ब ! हे अक् ! हे अङ् ! हे कुमारि ! हे शार्ङ्गरि ! हे ब्रह्मवन्धु ! हे वीरवन्धु !

*Vārt:*—Prohibition must be stated when the endearing terms denoting mother have an uncombined **इ**, **ल** or **क**, as हे अम्बाडे ! हे अम्बाल ! हे अम्बिक ! But हे अक् and हे अक् where the **ल** and **क** are conjunct.

*Vārt:*—Optionally so in the Veda: as हे अम्बाड ! or हे अम्बाडे ! हे अम्बाल ! or हे अम्बाले, हे अम्बिक ! हे अम्बिके ॥

*Vārt:*—A feminine stem formed with the affix **तल** optionally becomes short before the Loc. Sg. and Voc. Sg. As देवते भक्तिः or देवतायां भक्तिः, हे देवत ! or हे देवते ॥ This shortening takes place in the Veda only.

*Vārt:*—In a Bahuvrīhi compound ending with **मातृ**, there is substituted **मातृ** for **मातृ** in the Voc. Sg. when the word means a son worthy of such a mother. As हे गार्गामाते !—मात्रां व्यवहृशमर्हति ईशार्पनीयत्वाद् यः पुनः ॥ This debars the **कप** affix of V. 4. 153. The **क** of **मातृ** makes the final acute.

**हस्वस्य गुणः ॥ १०८ ॥ पदानि ॥ हस्वस्य, गुणः, ॥**

वृत्तिः ॥ संवृद्धाविति वचते । हस्वोन्तस्याङ्गस्य गुणो भवति संवृद्धौ परतः ॥

108. For short **इ** and **उ** final in a nominal-stem, a **guṇa** is substituted in the Vocative Singular.

As हे अम्ने, हे वायो, हे पदो ॥ But there is no **guṇa** in हे कुमारि, हे ब्रह्मवन्धु, because **इ** and **उ** were shortened specifically, and to substitute **guṇa** for them

18

1452

GUNA OF FEMININE.

[ Bk. VII. Ch. III. §. III

would make their shortening a useless operation. Moreover, had guna been intended in the case of these nadi words, the sūtra would have been अम्बायानाइस्वः, २ नशीइस्वयोर्गुणः ॥

जसि च ॥ १०९ ॥ पदानि ॥ जसि, च ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ जसि परतो ब्रह्मान्तस्याङ्गस्य गुणो भवति ॥

वातिकेतुः ॥ जसादिषु छन्दसि वावचने वाक्, गो चाङ्गुपधाया ब्रह्म इत्येतस्मात् ॥

109. Before the affix अस् of the Nom. Pl., Guna is substituted for the final short vowel of a nominal stem.

As अम्बयः, वायवः, पदवः, घेनवः, बुन्दवः ॥

Vārt:—All these rules upto the end of this chapter are of optional application in the Veda. As अम्बे or अम्ब, पूर्णा वरीं or पूर्णा वरीं, अधा शतकत्वः or शतकत्वः, पञ्चे भूयः or पञ्चे भूयः, किंकिषीय्या or किंकिषीविना ॥

The forms वरीं and वरीं could have been regularly obtained by the optional use of ङीप् (कृषिकारावन्तिनः) ॥ शतकत्वः is formed by adding अस् to शतकतु without guna of ङ, and ङ being changed to ङ ॥ The rule of lengthening the prior vowel (VI. 1. 102) which would have otherwise come, in the absence of guna does not take place, as a Vedic option (VI. 1. 106). किंकिषीय्या is the Instrumental singular, the ना of VII. 3. 120 does not come. The word किंकिषीवि is formed by Unādi nipātan (कृषिभुवि &c Un IV. 56).

ऋतो ङिसर्वनामस्थानयोः ॥ ११० ॥ पदानि ॥ ऋतः, ङि, सर्वनामस्थानयोः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ गुण इति वर्तते ऋकारान्तस्याङ्गस्य ङी परतः सर्वनामस्थाने च गुणो भवति ॥

110. Guna is substituted for the final ऋ of a stem, in the Locative singular and in the Strong cases.

As मातरि, पितरि, आतरि, कर्तरि; मातरी, पितरी, आतरी, कर्तरी, कर्तारः ॥ For the long in कर्तरी and कर्तारः see VI. 4. 11. The त् in ऋत् is for the sake of facility of utterance.

Because before ङि and strong cases, it is impossible for a stem to end in a long vowel ऋ nor a dhātu noun can so come, since in that case, long ऋ would be changed to ङ् by VII. 1. 100, and in forms like कर्तृणि there is तुव् ॥

घेङिति ॥ १११ ॥ पदानि ॥ घेः, ङिति, ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ ध्यन्तस्याङ्गस्य ङिति प्रत्यये परतो गुणो भवति ॥

111. For the इ and ङ of the stems called घि (I.4.3.) Guna is substituted in Dative, Ablative and Genitive Singular.

As अम्बये, वायवे, अम्नेः, वायोः, (VI. 1. 110). Why of घि stems? Observe सख्ये, पये ॥ Why in the Singulars of the Dat. Abl. and Loc. only? Observe अग्निः-भ्याम् ॥ The word case ending (छुपि) is understood here also, as the counter-examples are पट्टी, कुरुतः ॥

The word पट्टी is formed by adding ङीप् to पट्ट (IV. 1. 44). ङीप् is not a case-affix, though it is ङित् and is added to पट्ट which is घि ॥ कुरुतः is no proper example: for though तस् which is added to कुरु, is ङित्, it is only so by atidēsa (सार्वधातुकमवित्), and moreover कुरु is not घि ॥

BK. VII. CH. III. §. 116]

आबू AUGMENT.

1453

आण्णधाः ॥ ११२ ॥ पदानि ॥ आड, नधाः, ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ मघन्तादङ्गादुत्तरस्य डितः प्रत्ययस्याजागमो भवति ॥

112. The augment आड is added to the case-endings of the Dat. Abl. and Gen. Sg. after the stem called Nadi (I. 4. 3. &c.).

As कुमायै, किशोयै, ब्रह्मबन्धै, धीरबन्धै, कुमायाः, किशोयाः, ब्रह्मबन्धाः, धीरबन्धाः ॥

याजापः ॥ ११३ ॥ पदानि ॥ याद, आपः, ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ आबन्तादङ्गादुत्तरस्य डितः प्रत्ययस्य याजागमो भवति ॥

113. The augment याद is added to the Dat. Abl. and Gen. Sg. after a Feminine stem ending in आ ॥

As खट्टायै, बहुराजायै, कारीपगन्धायै, खट्टायाः, बहुराजायाः, कारीपगन्धायाः ॥ But in the compound अतिखट्ट, (from खट्टामतिकान्तः), this rule does not apply, on the maxim ऊषाह् महणेऽपिḥ as the आ has been shortened here. Even when the word अतिखट्ट assumes the form अतिखट्ट in the Dative by VII. 3. 102, the affix does not take the augment याद, because this long आ is a lākshanika आ only, while the आ of the sūtra is a pratipadokta (लक्षणप्रतिपदोक्तयोः पतिपदस्येव) ॥

सर्वनाजः स्यादुस्त्वध ॥ ११४ ॥ पदानि ॥ सर्वनाजः, स्याद, हस्वः च, ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ सर्वनाज आबन्तादङ्गादुत्तरस्य डितः प्रत्ययस्य स्याजागमो हस्वध भवति ॥

114. After a Pronominal stem ending in long आ of the Feminine, the Dat. Abl. and Gen. Sg. receive the augment स्याद and the आ of the stem is shortened.

As सर्वस्यै, विश्वस्यै, यस्यै, तस्यै, कस्यै, भवत्यै, भवत्याः, सर्वस्याः, विश्वस्याः, यस्याः, तस्याः, कस्याः, भवत्यै भवत्याः ॥

But अहस्यै where the stem does not end in long आ of the Feminine.

विभाषा द्वितीयातृतीयाश्च्याम ॥ ११५ ॥ पदानि ॥ विभाषा, द्वितीया, तृतीया-श्च्याम, ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ द्वितीया तृतीया इत्येताभ्यावुत्तरस्य डितः प्रत्ययस्य विभाषा स्याजागमो भवति ॥

115. After द्वितीया and तृतीया the Dat. Abl. and Gen. Sg. may optionally get the augment स्याद before which the आ is shortened.

As द्वितीयस्यै or द्वितीयायै; तृतीयस्यै or तृतीयायै, द्वितीयस्याः or द्वितीयायाः, तृतीयस्याः or तृतीयायाः ॥

डेराज्ञधात्रीश्चः ॥ ११६ ॥ पदानि ॥ डेः, आम, नदी, आप्, नीश्चः, ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ मघन्तादानन्ताश्रीत्येतस्माच्चोत्तरस्य डेरामित्ययमादिशो भवति ॥

116. For the ending इ of the Loc. Sg. there is substituted आम, after a stem called Nadi (I. 4. 3. &c), after the Feminines in आ, and after नी ॥

1454

GIII DECLENSION.

BK. VII. CH. III. §. 119

As कुमायाम्, किशोराम्, गौराम्, ब्रह्मबन्धाम्, धीरबन्धाम्, सद्गुणाम्, बहुराज्ञायाम्, कारी-
प्रमाण्यायाम्, नी-प्रमाण्याम्, सेनानाम् ॥

The word प्रामणी is formed by कृप् affix added under III. 2. 61, the न
is changed to ण by अम प्रामाण्याम्; and the यण substitute in the Locative is by
VI. 4. 82.

इदुन्नयाम् ॥ ११७ ॥ पदानि ॥ इत, उन्नयाम्, ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ इकारोकाराभ्यां नदीसंज्ञकाभ्याहुत्तरस्य डेरामार्दिशो भवति ॥

117. After the Feminine nadi words ending in इ
and उ short, आम is substituted for the इ of the Loc. Sg.

As कृत्याम्, धेन्वाम् ॥ See I. 4. 6.

The word नदी is understood here also. Obj. If this be so, it is not a
really separate sutra, because it is included in the last, and these forms could
be obtained by the last sutra: so that we ought to make only one sutra of 117
and 118, as इदुन्नयाम् ॥ Ans. We could not have done so, for then in the
case of कृति and धेनु, the औ would have come and not आ, in this way. The आम would
have found scope in nadi words like कुमायाम्, the औ would have undisputed
scope in पत्यो and सख्यो; but in the case of कृति when getting the designation
नदी the औ would have come, being subsequently taught, and the form would
have been कृत्यो instead of कृत्याम् ॥

औत ॥ ११८ ॥ पदानि ॥ औत ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ इदुन्नयाहुत्तरस्य डेरोकारार्दिशो भवति ॥

118. After a stem ending in इ or उ short, and which
is not a Nadi or a Ghi, औ is substituted for the इ of the Loc. Sg.

As सख्यो, पत्यो ॥

In the case of नदी words आम is taught by the previous sutras; in the case
of धि words औ preceded by अ substitution of धि letters will be taught in the
next sutra, so by the rule of exclusion, the present sutra applies to words other
than nadi and ghi.

अधधेः ॥ ११९ ॥ पदानि ॥ अत, च, घेः, ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ औविति वर्तते धिसंज्ञकादुत्तरस्य डेरोकारार्दिशो भवति तस्य च घेरकारार्दिशो भवति ॥

119. After a Ghi (I. 4. 7) stem ending in short इ
or उ, औ is substituted for the इ of the Loc. Sg. and अ is sub-
tituted for the final of such Ghi stem.

As अग्नी, वायो, कृतो, धेनो, पटी ॥ The short अ is substituted, in order to
prevent the दाप affix in the Feminine. Those who read 118 and 119 combi-
ned as औतध धेः translate it thus: 'After every other stem ending in इ and उ
(i.e. which is not a Nadi), औ is substituted for the Locative Singular इ, whereby
for the final of Ghi stems, अ is substituted'. They do so on the analogy of the
sutra कर्तुः व्यक् सलोपम् (III. 1. 11).

BK. VII. CH. III. §. 120]

GHI DECLENSION.

1455

आङो नाऽस्त्रियाम् ॥ १२० ॥ पदानि ॥ आङः, ना, अ स्त्रियाम् ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ घेरस्तस्याङ्गो नामावो भवति अस्त्रियाम् ॥

120. ना is substituted for the ending आ of the Instrumental singular, after the Ghi stems, when they are not Feminine.

As अग्निना, वायुना, पटुना ॥ Why do we not say आङो ना पुंसी 'ना is substituted for आ in the Masculine'? Ans. In order to form the neuter Instrumentals also, as षष्ठा, जतुना ॥ Obj. These can be formed by the augment नु under rule VII. 1. 73, and not by the ना of this sutra. Ans. But अङ्गुना will not be so formed as अङ्गुना ब्राह्मणकुले ॥ Because नु substituted for नु of अङ्गुना VIII. 2. 80 is considered as asiddha or non-existent (VIII.2.1) for the purposes of the application of VII. 1. 73, and as अङ्गुना cannot take नु, it will take ना by this rule. Why do we say "not in the Feminine?" Observe क्त्या, पेन्ता ॥

ॐ।

## अथ सप्तमाध्यायस्य चतुर्थः पादः ।

### BOOK SEVENTH.

#### CHAPTER FOURTH.

जौ चङ्युपधाया हस्वः ॥ १ ॥ पदानि ॥ जौ, चङि, उपधायाः, हस्वः, ॥
वृत्तिः ॥ अङ्गस्येति वर्तते चङ्युपं जौ यदङ्गं तस्योपधाया हस्वो भवति ॥
वार्तिकम् ॥ उपधायाः हस्वे जौणिच्युपसंख्यानम् ॥

1. A short is substituted for the vowel, standing in a penultimate position, in the Causative stem, when the affix चङ् (sign of the Reduplicate Aorist of the Causatives) follows.

As अचीकरत्, अजीहरत्, अलीलवत्, अपीपठत् ॥ Here the rules of reduplication and shortening of the penultimate both present themselves simultaneously. The rule about shortening, being subsequent in order, is applied first, and then the reduplication takes place. Thus कारि+अत्=कार्+अत् (जि being elided VI. 4. 51)=कर्+अत् (shortening VII. 4. 1)=चकर्+अत् (VI. 1. 11)=चिकर्+अत् (VII. 4. 93, 79)=चीकरत् (VII. 4. 94). The necessity of maintaining this order will appear from the following considerations. The Causative stem of अद् is आदि; the Aorist of which is आदि+चङ्+त्=आद्+अत् (VI. 4. 51). Now if reduplication took place first we shall have आदिद्+अत् (I. 1. 59 the elided इ will be present for the purposes of reduplication) and as the penultimate is short already, the form will be आदिदत्, which with the augment अ will be अ+आदिदत्=आदिदत् ॥ This is a correct form, so far as it goes; but when the augment is elided in connection with the negative मा, the form will be मा भवान् आदिदत्, the correct form however is मा भवान् आदिदत् with a short अ, which can be formed if we shorten first and then reduplicate, as आद्+अत्=अद्+अत्=आदिद्+अत्=आदिदत्, which with the augment अ, will be आदिदत् ॥ In fact, though the reduplication of the second syllable (VI. 1. 2) is a *nitya* rule, because it applies even where a penultimate is shortened and where not, yet the rule about shortening takes effect first, because the author has himself indicated this, by making the root

BK. VII. CH. IV §. 1]

AORIST SHORTENING.

1457

ओण have an indicatory ऋ in the Dhātupāṭha (See VII. 4. 2 about ऋचित् verbs). For had the reduplication taken place first in the case of ओण (Bhu. 482), as ओणिण, there would be no long vowel to be shortened, and there would be no necessity of the prohibition (VII. 4. 2).

Obj: Why do we say 'in the Causative'? The ऋ Aorist is formed of Causatives only (See III. I. 48), the only exceptions being the simple roots णि, ङ्, ञ्, ण्, ण् and णि, none of which have any vowel in the penultimate and ण् and ण् have already short upadhā. The sūtra ण्ङ्, ण्, ण् would have been enough. Ans. Had the sūtra been, as proposed, then it would have meant, 'that which is penultimate when ण् follows, should be shortened'. Therefore in the Aorist of the Causative of ङ्, we have ङ्+णि+ण्+ङ्+ङ्=ङ्+ङ्+ङ् here the penultimate with regard to ण् is ऋ, which would be shortened, debarring Vriddhi and ण् substitute, and there would have come the ण् substitute instead. But that is not the case. We have ण्, and not ण्, and not ण्, similarly, in the Aorist of the Causative of ङ्, we shall have ङ्+ङ्+ङ्, and ण् being shortened we have ङ्+ङ्+ङ्, so that we cannot add the augment ण् (VII. 3. 36), and form ण्, and from ण्. And the forms like ण्, would not at all admit of shortening.

Why do we say when ण् follows? Observe ण्, for the present Tense. Why do we say of the penultimate? Observe ण्, and ण्, where the penultimate being a consonant, there can be no shortening. Had the word penultimate been not used, the vowels of these would be shortened. And the word 'upadhā' is also absolutely necessary for the sake of the subsequent sūtras like VII. 4. 4, and it prevents shortening in the above case, which would have otherwise taken place, on the maxim ण्, which qualifies I. 1. 67.

Vārt:—The rule of shortening of the penultimate applies to the ऋ Aorist of the Causative of the Causative i. e. to the double Causative even. Thus ण्, for the present Tense. Otherwise ण्, and ण्, where the penultimate being a consonant, there can be no shortening. Had the word penultimate been not used, the vowels of these would be shortened. And the word 'upadhā' is also absolutely necessary for the sake of the subsequent sūtras like VII. 4. 4, and it prevents shortening in the above case, which would have otherwise taken place, on the maxim ण्, which qualifies I. 1. 67.

2. The shortening of the penultimate of the stem, before the causative affix, in the reduplicated-Aorist, does not take place, when it is a (Denominative) stem, which has lost

1458

AORIST SHORTENING.

[BK. VII. CH. IV. §. 4]

a simple (end vowel of the Nominal-stem), before the Causative sign and also not, when it is the verb शास्त्र, or a root which has an indicatory ऋ ॥

The word अग्लोपिन् means literally a stem, in which a simple vowel (अक् pratyāhāra) or a portion containing an अक् vowel has been dropped. As the final vowels of Denominative stems are so elided before the Causative sign णि, the sūtra has been translated accordingly. Thus अममालन् = मालामाख्यन्; अममालन् = मातरमाख्यन्; अमरराजन् = राजानमतिकान्तवान्, अमलुल्लामन् = लोमान्यदुमुदवान् ॥ Where a simple अक् vowel alone is elided, as in the case of माला, there the elided आ being sthānivat, would prevent the shortening, the आ of माँ not being then considered penultimate. So that अग्लोपिन् could be spared from the sūtra, since the sthānivad-bhāva would prevent shortening. But where an अक् vowel plus a consonant is dropped, as in राजन् and लोमन्, there the sthānivad-bhāva does not apply (I. 1. 57), hence the necessity of employing the term अग्लोपिन् in the sūtra. Similarly अशशासन् with शास्त्र; and अब्बापन् from बापु, अय्यापन् from बापु, and अडुवीकन् from वीक ॥ See III. 1. 21 and 25.

आजमासमापदीपजीवमीलपीडामन्यतरस्याम् ॥ ३ ॥ पदानि ॥ आज, मास, माप, दीप, जीव, मील, पीडाम्, अन्यतरस्याम् ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ आज मास माप दीप जीव मील पीड इतेतेषामङ्गानां जी चङ्गुपधाया इन्तो भवत्यन्तरस्याम् ॥
वात्तिकम् ॥ काण्याहीतां वेति वक्तव्यम् ॥

3. The shortening of the penultimate of the Causative stem, in the reduplicated Aorist, is optional in the following:—bhrāj, bhās, bhāsh, dīp, jīv, mīl and pīḍ.

As अविभजन् or अवभाजन्, अवीमसन् or अवमासन्, अवीमपन् or अवमापन्, अवी-दिपन् or अविदीपन्, अजीजिपन् or अजिजीपन्, अमीमिलन् or अमिमीलन्, अमीपिडन् or अमिपीडन् ॥ The Dhātupāṭha reads आज (Bhu. 194) and मास (Bh. 655). The indicatory ऋ is unnecessary and not countenanced by Pāṇini, as shown in this sūtra. Had they been ऋपिन्, they would have been governed by the last aphorism.

Vārt:—The words काणि, वाणि, राणि, हेदि, लोपि should be enumerated: as अचकाणन् or अचीकणन्, अराणन् or अरीरणन्, अशभाणन् or अशिभणन्, अवभाणन् or अवीभणन्, अजीहिदन्, अजिहिदन्, अलुलोपन् or अलुलुपन् ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ पिबतेरङ्गस्य जी चङ्गुपधाया लोपो भवति अभ्यासस्यकारादेशो भवति ॥

4. The penultimate vowel, in the Causative stem of पा 'to drink' is elided in the Aorist, and for the vowel of the Reduplicate there is substituted long ई ॥

SHORT क् SUBSTITUTE.

As पा+णि+अत्=पाय+इ+अत् (VII. 3. 37)=पाय+अत् (VI. 4. 51)=पय+अत् (VII. 4. 8)=पय+अत् (I. 1. 59)=पीयत् (VII. 4. 4). Thus अपीयत्, अपीयत्, अपीयत् ॥ When the penultimate आ is elided, there remains प which cannot be reduplicated as having no vowel, but the elided आ is considered as sthānivat and thus पा is reduplicated. Sūtra VII. 4. 80 establishes by implication the principle that the substitutes caused by णि are sthānivat. Thus भू+णि=भावि; in reduplicating, this भा will not be reduplicated, but भू, as बुभावि, भा=भू by sthāinvad-bhāva.

तिष्ठतेरित् ॥ ५ ॥ पदानि ॥ तिष्ठतेः, इत् ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ तिष्ठतेरङ्गस्य गो चन्द्रपपाया इकारदेशो भवति ॥

5. Short इ is substituted for the penultimate vowel of the Causative stem of स्था in the Aorist.

Thus अतिष्ठित्, अतिष्ठिताम्, and अतिष्ठित् ॥ The form is thus evolved. स्था+णिच्+अत्=स्थाप्+इ+अत् (VII. 3. 36)=स्थाप्+अत् (VI. 4. 51)=स्थिप्+अत् (VII. 4. 5)=तिष्ठित् ॥

जिघ्रतेवी ॥ ६ ॥ पदानि ॥ जिघ्रतेः, वा ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ जिघ्रतेरङ्गस्य गो चन्द्रपपाया इकारदेशो वा भवति ॥

6. Short इ is optionally substituted for the penultimate vowel of the Causative stem of प्रा in the Aorist.

As अजिघ्रित् or अजिघ्रपत्, अजिघ्रिताम् or अजिघ्रपताम्, अजिघ्रिपत् or अजिघ्रपत् ॥ Thus प्रा+णि+अत्=प्राप्+इ+अत् (VII. 3. 36)=प्रिप्+इ+अत् (VII. 4. 6)=प्रिप्+अत् (VI. 4. 51)=जिघ्रिपत् ॥ When इ is not substituted, आ is shortened by VII. 4. 1.

उच्छ्रेत् ॥ ७ ॥ पदानि ॥ उः, छ्र्त् ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ गो चन्द्रपपाया ऋवर्णस्य स्थाने वा ऋकारदेशो भवति ॥

7. Short ऋ is optionally substituted for the penultimate ऋ and ऋ of a Causative stem, in the reduplicated Aorist.

This debars the इ (VII. 3. 101), अर् (VII. 3. 86), and आ (VII. 2. 114) substitutes. Thus अचिकीतत् (VII. 1. 101) or अचिकीत् from क्त् (Chur 111): अवचीत् (VII. 3. 86), or अवीत्; अममाजत् (VII. 2. 114) or अमीयजत् ॥ Though the इ, अर् and आ substitutes are antaranga operations, they are prohibited by the express text of this sūtra. The short ऋ is substituted even for a long ऋ: the त् of ऋ shows that, as in अचीकतत् (VIII. 2. 77). In fact, this ऋ substitute does not take place after the operations of इ, आ and अर् substitutions have taken effect, but it is a form which suspends the operation of all those rules.

नित्यं छन्दसि ॥ ८ ॥ पदानि ॥ नित्यम, छन्दसि ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ छन्दसि विधेये गो चन्द्रपपाया ऋवर्णस्य स्थाने ऋकारदेशो भवति नित्यम ॥

As अयीवृधत्, अयीवृधताम् and अयीवृधम् ॥

दयतेर्दिगि लिटि ॥ ९ ॥ पदानि ॥ दयतेः, दिगि, लिटि ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ दयतेरङ्गस्य लिटि परतो दिगीत्ययनादेशो भवति ॥

As अय दिग्ये, अय दिग्याले, अय दिग्यिर ॥ The root देह 'to protect' (Bhu. 1011) is to be taken, and not दय 'to give' (Bhu. 510), for that root forms its Perfect by आय (Periphrastic Perfect) as taught in III. 1. 37. The substitute दिगि debars reduplication.

ऋतश्च संयोगादेर्गुणः ॥ १० ॥ पदानि ॥ ऋतः, च, संयोग-आदे, गुणः ॥

वात्तिकम् ॥ संयोगादेर्गुणविधाने संयोगोपधमङ्गं क्रमये कर्तव्यम् ॥

10. A root ending in short ऋ, and preceded by a conjunct consonant, gets Guṇa in the Perfect.

As सस्वरतः, सस्वरः from स्व, दध्वरतः, दध्वरः from ध्व, सस्वरतः, सस्वरः from स्व ॥ Why do we say ending in ऋ? Observe चिशियतः, चिशियः ॥ Why do we say beginning with a conjunct consonant? Observe चकतः, चकः ॥ This sūtra ordains Guṇa where there was prohibition by I. 2. 5 read with I. 1. 5. But this does not debar the Vṛiddhi caused by णह (VII. 1. 115). In fact, that prior rule supersedes this posterior rule, as सस्वर, दध्वर, सस्वर ॥ The word लिटि is to be supplied in the sūtra, the rule does not apply to Nishthā &c., as सस्वरः, सस्वरः ॥

Vārt:—For the sake of ऋ, the guṇa should be stated even where the double-consonant is in the penultimate position and not in the beginning. As संचस्करतः, संचस्करः ॥ See VI. 1. 135. On the maxim पूर्व धातुः साधनेन युज्यते पञ्चादुपसर्गेण 'a root is first developed fully and then the preposition is added to it'; we first develop ऋ in the Perfect by reduplication, which gives us चक+अतुस्, then we add the preposition as संचक+अतुः, then we add सूद though the reduplicate intervenes, by VI. 1. 136 and 137, as संचक+अतुः, now the root assumes a form in which the penultimate begins with a double consonant, and applying the vārtika we make guṇa, and get संचस्करतः ॥

It is by this consideration that in संस्कृपीट, उपस्कृपीट, the सूद augment being Bahiranga and consequently considered as non-existent (asiddha), there is no इद augment added by VII. 2. 43.

ऋच्छत्युताम् ॥ ११ ॥ पदानि ॥ ऋच्छति, ऋ, ऋताम् ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ ऋच्छतेरङ्गस्य ऋक्ष्येतस्य ऋकारान्तानां च लिटि परतो गुणो भवति ॥

11. There is gūṇa in the Perfect of ऋच्छ, ऋ and roots ending in long ऋ.

As आनच्छ, आनच्छतु:, आनच्छु: from ऋच्छ, आर, आरतु:, आर: from ऋ, and नि चकरतु:, नि चकर:, नि जगरतु:, नि जगर: from कृ and गु ॥ ऋच्छ not having a light vowel in the penultimate, would not have received gūṇa by VII. 3. 86, this sūtra ordains it; roots in long ऋ never received gūṇa, but इर substitution; this ordains gūṇa. The Vriddhi of VII. 2. 115 supersedes this rule, within its own jurisdiction, a prior superseding the posterior: as निचकार, नि जगर ॥

शुद्धर्मा हस्यो वा ॥ १२ ॥ पदानि ॥ शु, दु, प्राम, हस्व:, वा, ॥
वृत्ति: ॥ शु, दु, दु इत्येतेषामज्ञानां लिटि परतो वा हस्यो भवति ॥

12. In शु, 'to injure' (IX. 18) दु 'to tear' (IX. 23) and पु to protect' (IX. 19) the vowel may optionally be shortened in the Perfect.

As वि शश्वत: by shortening or वि शश्वत:, by gūṇa, which prevents ए and abhyāsalopa (VI. 4. 126) वि शश्व: or विशश्वत:, विशश्वत: or विशश्वत:, विशश्व: or विशश्वत:, निपश्वत: or नि पश्वत:, नि पश्व: or नि पश्व: ॥ Why is the word 'short' made optional in the sūtra, and not the word 'gūṇa'; for in the absence of gūṇa, the long ऋ would have become र before अत: by यणादेश:, and we would have got the forms विशश्वत:, विशश्व: by the regular rules of 'sandhi'? The word 'short' is used in the sūtra, in order to debar the इर and उर alternatives. Had the sūtra been 'शु दु प्रा वा' the alternative examples would have been with इर (VII. 1. 101) as शिशिरत: विशिरत: and उर (VIII. 2. 77) as पिशुरत: ॥ Some say this sūtra is unnecessary. The above forms like वि शश्वत:, विशश्व:, &c. can be regularly obtained from the roots आ 'to cook', आ 'to abuse', and आ 'to fill' and as the roots have many other senses, besides those assigned to them in the Dhātupāṭha, the roots आ, आ and आ will give the meanings of शु, दु, and पु ॥ If that were so, the form विशश्वान् with the affix कुण्ड could not be formed, for we should have either विशश्वान् from शु root or विशश्वान् from आ root but never विशश्वान् ॥ So the rule about shortening is necessary.

केऽण: ॥ १३ ॥ पदानि ॥ के, अण:, ॥
वृत्ति: ॥ के प्रत्यये परतो ऽणो हस्यो भवति ॥

As इका, (VII. 3. 47) कुमारिका, किशोरिका, ब्रह्मबन्धुका ॥ Why आ, ई and ऊ only? Observe गोका, गोका ॥ The words इका, धाका are irregular being formed by Uṇādi diversity, with the affix क added to रा and धा (Uṇ III. 40) By the following sūtra, the rule does not apply to the affix कष; it therefore implies that कष is governed by this rule, though it has the anubandha क ॥ Kātyāyana would confine this rule to the Taddhita क, and not the kṛit क of the

वृत्तिः ॥ कपि प्रत्यये परतो ऽणो द्रव्यो न भवति ॥

14. But before the samāsanta affix कप coming after Bahuvrīhi compounds, the अण vowels are not shortened.

As बहुकुमारीकः, बहुवृथ्वीकः, बहुवधुकः, बहुलक्ष्मीकः ॥ The shortening ordained by I. 2. 48 even does not operate when कप follows.

For had there been upasarjana shortening (I. 2. 48), the present sūtra would be useless. Therefore, the very existence of this sūtra debars every sort of shortening. Obj. The present sūtra would not be useless, for it will find scope where there is no shortening of the upasarjana by I. 2. 48: namely before non-feminine affixes, as बहुवयागुकः; but there should be shortening in feminine affixes. Ans. The shortening of I. 2. 48 will not take place before कप affix. Because the affix कप will first be added to the second member in the sense of the compound, and then the word so ending in कप will be compounded with the first member. So there is no pratipadika left which ends in a feminine affix, and therefore I. 2. 48, does not apply, because the pratipadika now left is one ending in the affix कप and not in a feminine affix.

आपोत्यतरस्याम् ॥ १५ ॥ पदानि ॥ आपः, अन्यतरस्याम् ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ आवन्तस्यादृश्य कपि द्रव्यो न भवत्यत्यतरस्याम् ॥

15. Optionally the feminine stem in आ is not shortened before कप ॥

As बहुवदुकः or बहुवदुकः, बहुनालकः or बहुनालाकः ॥

ऋद्धयो ऽङि गुणः ॥ १६ ॥ पदानि ॥ ऋ, दृशः, अङिः, गुणः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ ऋवर्णान्तानां दृशेष अङि परतो गुणो भवति ॥

16. Guṇa is substituted for the vowel of the root, before the affix अङ्, in the roots ending in ऋ or ऋ, as well as in दृश ॥

As शकलाङ्गुष्ठकोऽकरत्, अङ्गे तेभ्योऽकरं नमः, असरत्, आरत्, अवशत्, अवशताम्, अवशत् ॥ The affix अङ् means the Aorist-character अङ् of which the above examples are given. It also is the krit-affix (III. 3. 104), of which we have ऋ—जरा ॥

The word अकरत् is अङ् Aorist formed from ऋ by III. 1. 59. The word असरत् is from ऋ (III. 1. 56). अवशत् by VI. 1. 57.

As आस्यत्, आस्यताम्, आस्यन् ॥ See III. 1. 52.

अयतेरः ॥ १८ ॥ पदानि ॥ अयतेरः, अः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अयतेरङ्गस्याकारदेशो भवत्यङ् परतः ॥

18. The अ is substituted for the final of अि in the अङ् Aorist.

As अयत्, अयताम्, अयन् ॥ For the अ of the stem and the अ of the affix, there is the single substitute of the last by VI. 2. 97. See III. 1. 58.

पतः पुम् ॥ १९ ॥ पदानि ॥ पतः, पुम् ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ पतेरङ्गस्य पुमागमो भवत्यङ् परतः ॥

19. The augment ए is added after the vowel of the root पत् in the अङ्-Aorist.

As अपसत्, अपसताम्, अपसन् ॥ The पत् takes the अङ् Aorist as it has an indicatory ङ् in the Dhātupāṭha (III. 1. 55).

वचउम् ॥ २० ॥ पदानि ॥ वचः, उम् ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ वचेरङ्गस्य अङ् परतः उमागमो भवति ॥

20. The augment उ is added after the अ of वच् in the अङ्-Aorist.

As अयोचत्, अयोचताम्, अयोचन् ॥ See III. 1. 52.

शीङः सार्वधातुके गुणः ॥ २१ ॥ पदानि ॥ शीङः, सार्वधातुके, गुणः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ शीङोऽङ्गस्य सार्वधातुके परतो गुणो भवति ॥

21. For the vowel of शी, there is substituted guṇa, when a Sārvadhātuka affix follows.

As शेते, शयाते, शेरते, but शिश्वे before the ārdhadhātuka affix (III. 4. 115). Though these sārvadhātuka affixes were ङ्गि (I. 2. 4) and would not have caused guṇa (I. 4. 5), they do so by virtue of the present sūtra. The word शीङ् is read in the sūtra with the anubardha ङ्, in order to indicate that the rule does not apply to यङ् ङ्क् as शेहीतः, शेहयाते ॥

अयङ् यि क्ङ्गिति ॥ २२ ॥ पदानि ॥ अयङ्, यि, क्ङ्गिति, ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ यकारादि क्ङ्गिति प्रत्ये परतः शीङोऽङ्गस्याक्ङ्गित्ययमादेशो भवति ॥

22. Before an affix beginning with यु and having an indicatory ङ् or ङ्, there is substituted अय् for the ई of शी ॥

As शय्यते with यक्, शाशय्यते with यङ्, प्रशय्य and उपशय्य with ल्यप् which being the substitute of वल्या is कित् ॥ But शिश्वे where the affix is ए, and शेयम् where the affix is यत् (neither कित् or ङ्गि) ॥

उपसर्गाङ्गस्व ऊहतेः ॥ २३ ॥ पदानि ॥ उपसर्गात्, हस्वः, ऊहतेः ॥

LENGTHENING.

[ Bk. VII Ch. IV. §. 26

वृत्तिः ॥ उपसर्गादुत्तरस्य ऊहतेरङ्गस्य इस्यो भवति यकारादौ कङ्किति ॥

23. The short is substituted for the ऊ of ऊह when a Preposition precedes it, and an affix beginning with यू with an indicatory क् or ङ् follows.

As समुदाते, प्रप्युदाते, समुदा, अभ्युदाते, अभ्युदा ॥ But ऊहते without Preposition. Why do we say of ऊह? Observe समीहते ॥ Why do we say 'before य'? Observe समुहितम् ॥ Why do we say having indicatory क् or ङ्? Observe अभ्युदा: with यद् ॥ Of course the shortening takes place of ऊ (or अण् vowel, the word अण् being understood here from VII. 4. 13), and not when it assumes the form ओ, as आ ऊहते = ओहाते, समीहते ॥

एतेलिङि ॥ २४ ॥ पदानि ॥ एतेः, लिङि ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ एतेरङ्गस्योपसर्गादुत्तरस्य लिङि यकारादौ कङ्किति परतो इस्यो भवति ॥

24. The short is substituted for the vowel of the stem इ (एति) before the augment यास् in the Benedictive, when a Preposition precedes it.

As उदियात्, समियात्, अन्वियात् ॥ This is an exception to the following sutra by which a long would have been substituted. But इयात् without a Preposition. The अण् (VII. 4. 13) is understood here also. Therefore ए form of इ will not be shortened, as आ-इयात् = एयात्, समेयात् ॥

अकृत्सावेधातुकयोर्दीर्घः ॥ २५ ॥ पदानि ॥ अकृत्, सावेधातुकयोः, दीर्घः, ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अकृत्सावेधातुकयोः, दीर्घः, ॥

25. A long is substituted for the final vowel of the stem, before an affix beginning with a य having an indicatory क् or ङ्, when it is not either a Krit or a Sārvadhātuka affix.

Thus प्रहायते, सुखायते, and दुःखायते with the Denominative affix कयह according to III. 1. 12 and 18. धीयते and स्तूयते with the Passive यक्, वेधीयते and सोदूयते with the Intensive यक्, and धीयात् and स्तूयात् in the Benedictive (See III. 4. 116). But प्रकृत्य and प्रहृत्य where the affix ल्यप् is krit, and had the vowel been lengthened by this subsequent rule, the antecedent तुक् augment would have been debarred (VI. 1. 71). And चितूयात् and सुतूयात् where the Personal endings of the Potential are sārvadhātuka. The phrase कङ्किति is understood in this sutra, so there is no lengthening before non-kit and non-kit affixes, as, उरया, धृणुया, formed by या under VII. 1. 39.

चू च ॥ २६ ॥ पदानि ॥ चू, च ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ चू, च ॥

26. A long is substituted for the final vowel of the stem, before the Adverbial affix च्वि (V. 4. 50).

BK. VII. CH. IV. §. 29]

GUNA.

1465

As शुचि करोति, शुचि स्नात्, शुचि भवति, पद् करोति, पद् स्यात्, पद् भवति ॥ The च draws in the anuvṛtti of the phrase 'non-krit, and non-sārvadhātuka' from the last sūtra, which though not of any direct use in this aphorism, is necessary for the sake of subsequent ones. See VII. 4. 32 for words ending in अ ॥

रीङ् ऋतः ॥ २७ ॥ पदानि ॥ रीङ्, ऋतः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ चावति वचते ॥ अकृत्सार्वधातुकयोरिति च ॥ ऋकारान्तस्याङ्गस्य अकृयकारेऽसार्वधातुके यकारे च परतो रीङ् इत्ययमादेशो भवति ॥

27. री is substituted for the final short ऋ of a stem, before an affix beginning with य, when it is not a Krit nor a Sārvadhātuka affix, and before the adverbial affix ण्वि ॥

The anuvṛtti of किङ् is, however, not understood in this sūtra; that of ण्वी and अकृत्सार्वधातुकयोः is present. Thus मानीयति and पिचीयति with क्यच (III. 1. 8), मानीयते, पिचीयते with क्यङ् (III. 1. 11). चेकीयते with यङ्, मानीयतः with ण्वि ॥ The किङ् and किङ् not being understood here, we have पितुरागतं = पिच्यम् (IV. 3. 79), which is thus formed पितु-।-यन् = पिची+।-य = पिच-।-य (ई being elided by VI. 4. 148). Why do we say short ऋ? Observe चेकीयते, from क् विशेपे, with यङ्, ऋतइद् धातोः and इलिच् lengthening. निजैगिल्यते from क् and गु ॥

रिङ् शयगुलिङ् धु ॥ २८ ॥ पदानि ॥ रिङ्, श, यक्, लिङ् धु ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ ऋकारान्तस्याङ्गस्य श यक् इत्येतयोरि ण्वि च यकारादो असार्वधातुके परतो रीङ् इत्ययमादेशो भवति ॥

28. For the final short ऋ of a root, there is substituted रि, before the Present-character अ (श), before the Passive-character य, and before the augment यास् in the Benedictive.

The word लिङ् in the aphorism is qualified by the phrase यकारादो असार्वधातुके ॥ A Liḥ affix which begins with a य and is not a Sārvadhātuka, is necessarily the augment यास् of the Benedictive. Thus श-आ द्वियते and आ द्वियते (the य comes by VI. 4. 77). यक्-क्रियते, द्वियते ॥ लिङ्-क्रियात् and द्वियात् ॥ This short रि debars the long री of the last. The word non-Sārvadhātuka being understood, the rule does not apply to the Potential, as बिच्याम् ॥ The यि (VII. 4. 22) is understood here also, therefore when the Benedictive affix does not begin with य, the rule does not apply, as कृधीष्ट, हृधीष्ट ॥

गुणोत्तिसंयोगाद्योः ॥ २९ ॥ पदानि ॥ गुणः, अर्त्ति, संयोगाद्योः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ ऋतो यकि लिङ् इति वर्तते ॥ शय्यत्रासंभवाऽप्रवृत्ते ॥ गुणा भवत्यर्थः संयोगादीनाङ्करान्तानां यकि परतो, लिङ् च यकाराद्यसार्वधातुके ॥

29. Guṇa is substituted for the final ऋ in the root ऋ (अर्त्ति), and in those roots ending in ऋ, in which

GUNA

[ Bk. VII. Ch. IV. § 30.

the vowel is preceded by a conjunct consonant, when the Passive character यक् or the Benedictive augment यास् follows.

The words ऋतः, यकि and लिङि are understood here. Not so the word वा as its anuvṛtti is impossible. Thus अयते, अयात्, अयते and अयात् ॥ This is an exception to I. 1. 5. In सं स्कियते and संस्कियात् (VI. 1. 135), there is no Guṇa, either because in स्क् the augment स् is considered as Bahiranga and therefore asiddha, or because it is considered as no part of (or non-attached to) क्, and therefore स् क् is not a root beginning with a conjunct consonant. See however VII. 4. 10, where in forming संस्करतु, स्क् is considered as a root beginning with a conjunct consonant. See also Mahābhāshya on VI. 1. 135. The यि (VII. 4. 22) is understood here also; the Benedictive affix must begin with य, therefore not here स्वृष्टि, व्यृष्टि ॥ The word non-sarvadhātuka is also understood here, the rule does not apply to the Potential, as इय्यात्, there is ślu substitution of śap, reduplication, then there is इ substitution in the reduplicate by VII. 4. 77, then इयक् by VI. 4. 78.

यङि च ॥ ३० ॥ पदानि ॥ यङि, च ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ यङि च परतो अर्चेः संयोगादिभ ऋतो गुणो भवति ॥

वात्तिकम् ॥ न न्दाः संयोगादय इति द्विवचनप्रतिषेधो यकारपरस्य नेष्यते ॥

वा० ॥ इन्तेहिसायां यङि प्रीभावो वक्तव्यः ॥

30. Guṇa is substituted for the final ऋ of the root ऋ (अति) and in those roots, ending in short ऋ, in which the vowel is preceded by a conjunct consonant, when the Intensive character यङ् follows.

As अरायते, सास्ययते, वाध्ययते, सास्ययते ॥ The root ऋ takes यङ् according to a Vārtika under Sūtra III. 1. 22, with Guṇa we have ऋ+य=अर्थ ॥ By VI. 1. 2, the second member is reduplicated, in spite of the prohibition in VI. 1. 3, for according to Patanjali ई followed by य is not governed by that prohibition. So we have अर्थ, and according to VII. 4. 60, the य is dropped, and we have अर्थ, and by VII. 4. 83, we get अर्थ ॥ This is an exception to I. 1. 5.

Vārt:—In the Intensive of इम् 'to kill', स्त्री is substituted for इम् as जेम्नोयते ॥ The substitute is with a long ई, had it been with a short इ, that might also have been lengthened by VII. 4. 25. Not doing so, however, indicates the existence of the maxim संज्ञापूर्वकविधेरानित्यत्वम् 'A rule is not universally valid, when that which is taught in it is denoted by a technical term'. It is through this that स्वार्थभुवः is formed from स्वार्थभूः; because the Guṇa taught by VI. 4. 146, does not take place here before the Taddhita affix अण्, in as much as that rule VI. 4. 146, is taught by employing the technical term गुणः in ओर्गुणः instead of ओरोत्, hence that rule is anitya, and we have उयक् ॥

As शुक्ली करोति, शुक्ली भवति, शुक्ली स्यात् ॥ खट्टी करोति, खट्टी भवति and खट्टी स्यात् ॥

क्यचि च ॥ ३३ ॥ पदानि ॥ क्यचि, च, ॥

33. Long ई is substituted for the final अ or आ of a Nominal stem, before the Denominative affix क्यच् ॥

As पुत्रीयति, पदीयति, खट्टीयति, मालीयति ॥ This is an exception to VII. 4. 25. The separating of this aphorism from the preceding, is for the sake of the subsequent aphorism.

वृत्तिः ॥ अशनाय उदन्य धनाय इलेतानि पिपास्यन्ते बुभुक्षा पिपासा गर्दे इलेतयेयेषु ॥

34. The Denominative roots अशनाय, उदन्य and धनाय are irregularly formed, when they respectively mean 'to be hungry', 'to be thirsty', 'to be greedy'.

Thus अशनायति from अशन-।क्यच्, आ instead of ई; the other form being अशनायति who is not hungry at the time, but wishes to get food for some future occasion, and therefore when not meaning 'to be hungry'; उदन्यति 'he is thirsty', उदन् being substituted for उदक; in any other sense we have उदकायति, who wants water for purposes of bathing &c. धनायति 'he is greedy'; in any other sense, धनायति who is poor, and therefore wishes to get riches.

दुरस्युद्रविणस्युर्वृणयति रिषण्यति ॥ ३६ ॥ पदानि ॥ दुरस्युः, द्रविणस्युः, वृषण्यति, रिषण्यति, ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ दुरस्युः द्रविणस्युः वृषण्यति रिषण्यति एतानि छन्दसि निपात्यन्ते ॥

36. In the Veda दुरस्यु, द्रविणस्यु, वृषण्यति and रिषण्यति are irregularly formed.

As अविधोना दुरस्युः (= दुर्दीयति with the affix कयच् added to दुष्ट), द्रविणस्यु विघ्न्यया (द्रविणीयति, here द्रविणम् is substituted for द्रविण similarly). वृषण्यति = वृषीयति (वृषण substituted for वृष) ॥ रिषण्यति = रिष्टीयति (रिषण substituted for रिष्ट) ॥

As देवायन्तो यजमानाः सुस्रायन्तो हवामहे ॥ Why in the Yajus? Observe देवाञ्जिगाय सुस्रयुः ॥ Why do we say in the Kāthaka? Observe सुस्रयुरिदमासात् ॥

कव्यध्वरपूतनस्याचि लोपः ॥ ३९ ॥ पदानि ॥ कवि, अध्वर, पूतनस्यः, ऋचि, लोपः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ कवि अध्वर पूतना इत्येतेयामङ्गानां कयचि परतो लोपो भवति ऋचि विषये ॥

39. In the Rig Veda, the final of कवि, अध्वर and पूतना is dropped before the Denominative कयच् ॥

As कव्यन्तः सुस्रनसः (not in the Rig Veda), अध्वरयन्तः (not in this case in the Rig Veda). पूतनयन्तस्तिष्ठन्ति (not in this connection in the Rig. Veda). The examples given above are of Kāśikā: according to Pro. Bohtlingk none of them are from the Rig Veda. The following are given by Bhattoji Dikshita in his Siddhanta Kaumudi: स पूर्वया निबिदा कव्यताशोः (Rig I. 96. 2), अध्वरयुं वा मधुपाणिव (Rig X. 41. 3), इमयन्तं पूतनयु ॥

BK. VII. CH. IV. §. 42]

हि SUBSTITUTION.

1469

धतिस्यतिमास्थामिति किति ॥ ४० ॥ पदानि ॥ धति, स्यति, मा, स्थाम्, इत, ति, किति ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ धति स्यति मा स्था इलेतेषामङ्गानामिकारादेशो भवति तकारादौ किति प्रत्यये परतः ॥

40. Short इ is substituted for the final of दो, दो, मा and स्था, before an affix beginning with त् and having an indicatory क् ॥

As निर्वितः and निर्वितवान्; अवसितः and अवसितवान्, मितः and मितवान्; स्थितः and स्थितवान्, all with क् and क्तवत् ॥ Why before त्? Observe अवदाय ॥ Why before a किंतु affix? Observe अवदाता with तृक् ॥

शाछोरन्यतरस्याम् ॥ ४१ ॥ पदानि ॥ शा, छोः, अन्यतरस्याम् ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ शा छा इलेतयोरन्यतरस्यामिकारादेशो भवति तकारादौ किति प्रत्यये परतः ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ इलेतेरिवे व्रते नित्यमिति वक्तव्यम् ॥

*Kārikā*:—देवजातो गतो माह इतियोगे च सन्धिः ।

नियस्ते न विभाष्यन्ते गवाक्षः संचितव्रतः ॥

41. Short इ is optionally substituted for the final of शा (शो) and छा (छो), before an affix beginning with त् and having an indicatory क् ॥

As निश्चितं or निशातम्, निश्चितवान् or निशातवान्; अवच्छितं, अवच्छितवान् or अवच्छातं, अवच्छातवान् ॥ The शा *always* takes the इ when it means a vow: as संचितो ब्राह्मणः = संचितव्रतः ॥ The rule of this sūtra thus becomes a vyavasthita vibhāshā. Other examples of such vyavasthita vibhāshā are to be found in VIII. 2. 56, where वात and वाण past participles are formed with त or ण, but वात is *only* employed in names as देवजातः &c, and never वाण, while in denoting action both forms are valid: similarly by VIII. 2. 21, गल and गर are both formed, but गल *alone* is used when 'neck' is meant, and गर *alone* when 'poison' is indicated; optionally both when an action is meant. Similarly by III. 1. 143, माह and मह are formed, but माहः is *only* used when 'a crocodile' is meant, and महः *alone* is employed when a 'planet' is indicated. Similarly the addition of the Present Participle affix मह and वाणम् under III. 2. 126, is debarred when इति is added, as इति इति पलायते, वर्धतीति धावति ॥ In all the above examples, the option though taught generically, should be limited to specific cases; as also in the examples गवाक्षः 'a window', and गोऽसम् 'cow's eye' (VI. 1. 123) and संचितव्रतः ॥ In short, we should limit a general vibhāshā to a vyavasthita-vibhāshā, on the maxim व्यवस्थितविभाषा विज्ञानात् सिद्धम् ॥

दधातेहिः ॥ ४२ ॥ पदानि ॥ दधातेः, हिः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ दधातेहस्य हीत्ययमादेशो भवति तकारादौ किति प्रत्यये परतः ॥

42. हि is substituted for धा (दधाति) before an affix beginning with त् and having an indicatory क् ॥

1470

GHU DECLENSION.

[BK. VII. CH. IV. §. 46]

As हितः, हितवत्, हित्वा ॥

जहातेऽपि किं ॥ ४३ ॥ पदानि ॥ जहातेः, च, किं ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ जहातेऽप्य ह्येव्यमादिशो भवति क्तुमव्यये परतः ॥

43. हि is substituted for हा (जहाति) before क्त्वा ॥

As हित्वा राज्यं वनम् गतः, हित्वा गच्छति ॥ The rule does not apply to हा
जिहीते ॥ There we have ह्यावा गतः ॥

विभाषा छन्दसि ॥ ४४ ॥ पदानि ॥ विभाषा, छन्दसि ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ जहातेऽप्य विभाषा ह्येव्यमादिशो भवति छन्दसि विषये क्तुमव्यये परतः ॥

44. हि is optionally substituted for हा before क्त्वा
in the Chhandas.

As हित्वा शरीरं यातव्यं, or ह्यावा also. The long ई of VI. 4. 62 does not take
place also as a Vedic irregularity.

सुधितवसुधितनेमधितधिष्वधिषीय च ॥ ४५ ॥ पदानि ॥ सुधित, वसुधित, ने-
मधित, धिष्व, धिषीय, च ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ सुधित वसुधित नेमधित धिष्व धिषीय इयेतानि छन्दसि विषये निपात्यन्ते ॥

45. These five Vedic forms are irregularly formed,
सुधित, वसुधित, नेमधित, धिष्व and धिषीय ॥

Of these five, सुधित, वसुधित and नेमधित are formed from the root धा with
the affix क्त, preceded by सु, वसु and नेम ॥ As गर्भ माता सुधितम् (=सुधितम्), वसुधित-
मनो सुधिति (=वसुधितम्), नेमधिता बाधन्ते (=नेमधिता) ॥ धिष्व is Imperative 2nd Per.
Sg. of धा, there is no reduplication, as धिष्व सोमम्=धस्स ॥ धिषीय is Benedictive
Atmanepada 1st Per. Sg. of धा, the regular form being धासीय ॥

दो दद् धीः ॥ ४६ ॥ पदानि ॥ दः, दत्, धीः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ वा इयेतस्य युत्पन्नकस्य वदित्ययमादिशो भवति सकाशादि किंति प्रत्यये परतः ॥

46. For दा, when it is a Ghu (I. 1. 20), there
is substituted दद् before a कित affix beginning with त् ॥

As इणः, दत्तवान्, वृत्तिः ॥ Why of हा? Observe धीतः, धीतवान् from धेह्;
and the long ई is by VI. 4. 66. Why when it is a Ghu? Observe दातं बहि: from
दाप् 'to cut', and अवदातं दुर्लभं from देप् 'to cleanse'. The substitute is दप् ending
in ध, according to an *Ishti*.

*Kārikā*:—तान्ते दोषो दीर्घत्वं स्याद्, दान्ते दोषो निष्ठा नत्वम् ।

धान्ते दोषो धस्स प्राप्निस्, धान्तेऽ दोष स्तस्मात् धान्तम् ॥

If the substitute be दद् ending in त्, then it would require the
lengthening taught in VI. 3. 124. (N. B. The sūtra दन्ति should be interpreted
as 'the vowel of the Preposition is lengthened before a substitute of हा which
ends in त्', in order to make this objection applicable. That sūtra however
is capable of another interpretation). If the substitute be दद् ending in द्
then the Nishthā त् would be changed to न by VIII. 2. 42: as in भिद्+त=
भिन्नः ॥ If the substitute be दप् ending in ध्, then by VIII. 2. 40; the
Nishthā त् would be changed to ध् ॥ Hence the substitute is दप् ॥ If

BK. VII. CH. IV. §. 48]

1471

however, the *sūtra* VI. 3. 124, is interpreted as “the vowel of a preposition is lengthened before a substitute of **र्** which *begins* with **त्**”, then the substitute may be **र्** also without any harm. Even if the substitute be **र्** or **र्**, the apprehended **र्** and **र्** substitutions will not take place, on the maxim **सन्निपातलक्षणो विधि रेनिमित्तं तद्विघातस्य** ॥

The following are exceptions to VII. 4. 47, अवहं, विद्वं, प्रवं, सुवं, अनुवं and निबलं ॥ Or the words अव &c, here are not Upasargas. See I. 4. 57.

*Kārikā*:—अवहं विद्वं च प्रवं चादिकर्मणि ।

सुवं मनुवं च निबलं निबलं ॥

The word आदिकर्मणि qualifies pradatta only. The word च shows that regular forms अवहं, विद्वं, प्रवं, &c also are valid.

अच् उपसर्गात्: ॥ ४७ ॥ पदानि ॥ अच्:, उपसर्गात्, तः ॥

वृत्ति: ॥ अजन्तादुपसर्गादुपसर्गादुपसर्गादुपसर्गादुपसर्गादुपसर्गादुपसर्गादुपसर्गादुपसर्गादुपसर्गादुपसर्गादुपसर्गादुपसर्गादुपसर्गादुपसर्गादुपसर्गादुपसर्गादुपसर्गादुपसर्गादुपसर्गादुपसर्गादुपसर्गादुपसर्गादुपसर्गादुपसर्गादुप

47. **त्** is substituted for the **ghu** **र्** before a **किं** affix beginning with **त्**, when a Preposition ending in a vowel precedes it.

The examples under the present *sūtra* are प्रवं, अवहं, नीचं, परीचं ॥ For the lengthening see VI. 3. 124. Why do we say ‘ending in a vowel’? Observe निबलं, सुवं, ॥ Why ‘after an Upasarga only’? Observe र्वि, र्व, मधु, र्व ॥ Why ‘the **र्** called Ghu’? Observe अवहं, सुवं from र्व ॥

*Obj.* The word उपसर्गात् in the *sūtra* is in the Ablative case, and by I. 1. 67, the substitute **त्** should replace only the *first* letter of **र्**, how does it replace the *whole*?

*Ans.*—The word अच्: is to be repeated in the *sūtra*, one अच्: being in the Ablative case and qualifying उपसर्गात्, and the other अच्: being in the Genitive case, showing the *sthānin* to be अ, as “after an Upasarga ending in a vowel, **त्** is substituted *for the vowel* of **र्**”. Or the word अच् may be read into this *sūtra* from VII. 4. 32. Or उपसर्गात्: consists of three **त्**s, the substitute being **त्**, and being a substitute of more than one letter, it replaces the *whole* of **र्** (I. 1. 55). In the following *sūtra* अपोनि, the अच्: in the Ablative case is understood, and therefore **त्** replaces only **र्** ॥

*Vārt*:—After a Preposition ending in a vowel, **त्** is substituted for **र्** (र्), when **र्** would have been substituted otherwise for its final by VII. 4. 40. As अवहं, प्रवं, सुवं, ॥

अपो नि ॥ ४८ ॥ पदानि ॥ अप्:, नि: ॥

वृत्ति: ॥ अप्, प्रवं, ॥

48. **त्** is substituted for the final of the stem अप् before a case-ending beginning with **र्** ॥

1472

ELISION.

[BK. VII. CH. IV. §. 53]

As अन्ध्याम्, आङ्गः, अङ्गः ॥ Why beginning with a अ? Observe अङ्गः ॥

In the Veda, त् is substituted before अ, for the final of स्ववस्, from छ् + अङ् + अङ्गः; meaning सोभनमवेष्याः; स्ववस् from the root तु meaning स्वं त्वो श्रेयाः; मास and उपस्, as स्ववङ्गः, स्ववङ्गः, माङ्गिरिदा इन्द्रो वृचहा, सदुपङ्गिरजायथाः ॥ The word मास becomes मास by VI. I. 63.

सः स्याङ्गधातुके ॥ ४६ ॥ पदानि ॥ सः, सि, आङ्गधातुके ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ सकारात्मकस्यासकाराशा आङ्गधातुके परस्परकारादिशो भवति ॥

49. त् is substituted for the final स् of a root before an Ārdhadhātuka affix beginning with स् ॥

As वत्स्यति, अवत्स्यत्, विवत्स्यति, जिवत्स्यति ॥ Why do we say 'when ending in स'? Observe वत्स्यति ॥ Why do we say 'beginning with स'? Observe वासः, वासः ॥ Why an ārdhadhātuka? Observe आस्से, वस्से, from आस् 'to sit' and वस् 'to cover'; both Ādādi roots.

तासस्त्योर्लोपः ॥ ५० ॥ पदानि ॥ तास्अस्त्योः, लोपः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ तास्सेस्त्य सकारस्य सकारादि प्रत्यये लोपो भवति ॥

50. The final स् of तास् (the character of the second Future) and that of अस् 'to be', is elided before an affix beginning with स् ॥

As कर्त्तासि, कर्त्तासे, स्वमसि, व्यति से ॥ See VI. 4. III. In से the अ and स् both of अस् have been elided, the अ by VI. 4. III, and स् by the present sūtra, so that the mere suffix से remains, which however here is a finite verb: hence the स, is not changed to प ॥ See VIII. 3. III.

रि च ॥ ५१ ॥ पदानि ॥ रि, च ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ रेफादि च पत्यये परतः तासस्त्योः सकारस्य लोपो भवति ॥

51. The स् of तास् and अस् is dropped before an affix beginning with a र् ॥

As कर्त्तासि, कर्त्तासः, अध्येतासि, अध्येतासः ॥ The स् of अस् 'to be' is elided in the Perfect, because it is there that a र् beginning affix can follow it. Thus व्यतिरे (See VI. 4. III). According to the reading of Padamanjari, there can be no example of अस् ॥ अस्तेरुवाहरणं न प्रवृत्तिं, रेफादिरसम्भवात् ॥

ह पति ॥ ५२ ॥ पदानि ॥ हः, पति ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ तासस्त्योः सकारस्य हकारादिशो भवति एति परतः ॥

52. For the स् of तास् and अस् there is substituted ह् before the personal-ending प ॥

As कर्त्तासि, and व्यति हे from अस् ॥ See VI. 4. III. The ह् substitution does not take place before the Personal ending एष् (III. 4. 8), as एषामासे ॥ The reason of this is that the ए referred to in this sūtra, is that ए which can come after तास्; and that very ए should also come after अस् ॥ The ए that can

LONG ६ ॥

come after तात् is the 1st Person singular ए; and not this ए of the Perfect 3rd Person singular. Others say, this even sārvadhātuka, and therefore not here
छुतोइं त्वां प्रेक्षामासे ॥

यीवणयोर्दीधीवेभ्योः ॥ ५३ ॥ पदानि ॥ यि, इवणयोः, दीधी, वेभ्योः ॥
वृत्तिः ॥ यकारादाविवर्णादौ च परतो दीधीवेभ्योर्लोपो भवति ॥

53. The final of दीधी and वेवी falls before an affix beginning with य, इ or ई ॥

Thus आदीध्य and अविव्य गतः, आदीध्यते, and अविव्यते before य ॥ आदीधित्, आवेवित्; आदीधीत् and आवेवीत् ॥ Why before य, इ or ई? Observe आदीध्यनम् and अविव्यनम् ॥ The long ई in वी is a sūṭṭa वैचित्र्य, for विवर्णयोः would have been enough.

सनि मीमाधुरमलभशकपतपदामच इस् ॥ ५४ ॥ पदानि ॥ सनि, मी, मा, पु, रम, लम, शक, पत, पदा म, अचः, इस् ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ सनि प्रत्यये सकारादौ परतो मी मा पु रम लम शक पत पद इलेतेषामङ्गानामचः स्थाने इस्त्रिय-गादिशो भवति ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ सनि राधो हिंसायामच इस्त्रकव्यः ॥

54. इस् is substituted for the root-vowel of मी, मा, वा and धा (पु), रम, लम, शक, पत and पद when the Desiderative सन् beginning with स् (i. e. not taking the augment इ) follows.

The मी includes मीनाति (Kryādi 4), and मिनोति (मि of Svādi 4) for मि assumes the form मी by VI. 4. 16 Thus मिस्त्रति, प्रमिस्त्रति ॥ The मा denotes all the roots which assume the form मा, on the maxim गामादा प्रहणेवविषेषः 'The terms गा, मा or वा when they are employed in Grammar denote both the original roots गा, मा and वा and also the roots which are changed to गा, मा and वा' ॥ They are मा and माङ माने, and मेङ् प्रणिबाने ॥ Thus मिस्त्रते, अप मिस्त्रते ॥ पु—विस्त्रति, धि—स्त्रति; रम—आरिप्स्रते, लम—आलिप्स्रते, शक—शिक्ष्रति, पद—पिस्रति, पद—प्रपिस्रते ॥ In the roots that end in a vowel, the स् of इस् is changed to त् by VII. 4. 49, and in the roots that end in a consonant, this स् is dropped, according to VIII. 2. 29. The reduplication falls by VII. 4. 58.

Why do we say 'when the Desiderative follows'? Observe वास्त्वति ॥ The word सि is understood here from VII. 4. 49, so the rule will not apply when the Desiderative takes the augment इद्, as प्र पातपाति ॥ Here पद optionally takes इद् under the vārtika तनिपतिविरिज्ञाणामुपसंख्यानम् ॥

Vārt:—The इस् comes after the root-vowel of राध in the Desiderative, when the sense is that of to injure. As प्रति रिस्त्रति ॥ Why do we say when the sense is that of 'to injure'? Observe आरि रास्त्वति ॥

आपह्वप्युधामीत् ॥ ५५ ॥ पदानि ॥ आप्, झप्, ऋधाम्, ईत् ॥
वृत्तिः ॥ आप् झपि ऋध इलेतेषामङ्गानामच ईकारादिशो भवति सनि सकारादौ परतः ॥

1474

REDUPLICATE ELISION

[BK. VII. CH. IV. §. 58]

55. For the vowel of the roots आप्, झपि and ऋध् there is substituted long ई before the सन् of the Desiderative, when it begins with स् ॥

Thus आप्—ईप्सति, झपि—झीप्सति, ऋध्—ईप्सति (I. 1. 51.). The reduplication is dropped by VII. 4. 58. In the Causative stem झपि there are two vowels, the इ (णि) is dropped by pūrva-vipratishedha (the prior debarring the subsequent) according to VI. 4. 51, and ई substituted for अ according to the present sūtra. The word सन् is to be read into the sūtra, otherwise प्राप्सति ॥ The सन् must begin with स् i.e. should not take the इद augment, as in जिज्ञपथिपति, अर्द्धिपति ॥ The roots झपि and ऋध् are optionally सेद् in the Desiderative by VII. 2. 49.

दम्भ इच्च ॥ ५६ ॥ पदानि ॥ दम्भः, इत, च ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ दम्भेऽच इकारदेशो भवति चकारादीच सति सकारादि परतः ॥

56. For the vowel of the root दम्भ there is substituted इ as well as ई before the सन् of the Desiderative, when it begins with स् ॥

As धीप्सति or धिप्सति ॥ But दिशाम्पति before the सेद्सन् ॥ The reduplication falls off by VII. 4. 58.

मुचोऽकर्मकस्य गुणो वा ॥ ५७ ॥ पदानि ॥ मुचः, अकर्मकस्य, गुणः वा ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ मुचोऽकर्मकस्य गुणो वा भवति सति सकारादि परतः ॥

57. When मुच् has an Intransitive signification, Guṇa is optionally substituted for its vowel before the anit सन् of the Desiderative.

By I. 2. 10, after a root ending in a consonant, the सन् is like कित् and does not cause Guṇa. The present sūtra ordains it optionally. As मोक्षते or मुमुक्षत वत्सः स्वर्गमेव ॥ In the Transitive there is one form only, as मुमुक्षति वत्सं देवदत्तः ॥ मुच् becomes Intransitive when it has a Reflexive significance, or when it expresses a mere action. The reduplication is elided by VII. 4. 58.

59. A short is substituted for the long vowel of the reduplicate.

As डुडोकिपते, तुचोकिपते, डुडोके, तुचोके, अडुडोकत्, अनुचोकत् ॥

Vārt:—The shortening takes place before affixes other than अच् (III. 1. 134). Before अच्, the roots चर्, चल्, पत् and वद् are reduplicated, and the augment अच् added to the reduplicate. See VI. 1. 12 Vārt. This augment when added to the reduplicate, is not to be shortened by this rule: and because this is not to be shortened, also indicates that the consonants of the reduplicate other than the first are also not dropped: as चराचर्, चलाचल्, पत्-पत्, वदावद् ॥

हलादिः शेषः ॥ ६० ॥ पदानि ॥ हल् आदिः, शेषः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अभ्यासस्य हलादिः शिष्यते अनाविलुप्यते ॥

60. Of the consonants of the reduplicate, only the first is retained, the remainders are dropped.

As जग्लौ, मल्लौ, पपाच्, पपाङ्, आह, आहतु, आहुः ॥ This rule ordains the retention of the initial consonant, if any, and elision of the non-initials in the reduplicate. If the root begins with a vowel as अह्, there being no initial consonant, in अह् अह्, the इ will be elided of course. The word हलादिः should not be construed as a Genitive Tatpurusha ‘first among the consonants’, for then in अश्+लिह्=अश् अश्, the ए only would be elided, and क् retained.

The word शेषः or शिष्यते here means अवस्याप्यते ‘is retained’. The word हलादिः is not a compound. For had it been a compound, then if it is a Karma-dhāraya, the word आदि should stand first; if it be a Genitive compound then the first among compound consonants would be retined and we could not get the form आनस from अश्. The word abhyāsa is to be taken in the sense of jāti or kind, i.e. in the jāti which is collectively called abhyāsa, the consonant that stands first in respect to abhyāsa, is retained, and not the consonant standing

[ Bk. VII. Ch. IV. §. 62

in any other portion of it. So that all consonants, where ever they may be situate in the body of an abhyāsa, whether in the beginning or middle or end, are dropped, except one with which the abhyāsa begins. Thus if the abhyāsa begins with a simple consonant, it is retained; if it begins with a conjunct consonant, the first is only retained; and if the consonant or consonants are not in the beginning they are all dropped.

Others say, the word शेषः here means “retention along with the cessation of others”. Therefore, though literally the word शेषः or retention appears to be the principal word in this sūtra, yet as a matter of fact, it is secondary, because the injunction is not with regard to retention, but with regard to cessation. The rule is not “Retain the first consonant”; but “Drop every consonant but the first, if there be a first consonant”. Or the sūtras 59 and 60, may be combined and read thus: हस्योऽहम् “The abhyāsa becomes short and also without consonant”. आविशेषः “The first consonant is retained”. Or the sūtras may be divided thus:—

1. (1) ‘A short vowel is substituted in the abhyāsa’.
2. (2) ‘The consonants of abhyāsa are all elided’.
3. (3) The first is retained.

The sūtras 59 and 60 must be joined by sandhī “हस्योऽहम्” and then we shall be able to read an elided अं between हस्य and हम्, as if it was a compound of हस्य and अहम् ॥

61. Of a reduplicate, the hard consonants (aspirate and unaspirate) when preceded by a sibilant, are only retained, the other consonants are elided.

As चुदच्योतिषति, from śchyutir ksharaṇe, तिष्ठांसति, पिस्पन्तिषते ॥ Why do we say ‘when preceded by a sibilant’? Observe पपाच ॥ Why do we say hard consonants? Observe सखौ ॥

Vārt:—It should be said rather, a hard consonant preceded by a hard consonant or a sibilant is only retained: and the खं consonants are elided: as in उच्छिष्टषति, here उछ् becomes उच्छ् by the augment त् (तुक्); in the reduplicate the च् should be elided, and छ् retained out of छ्; and not च् retained and छ् elided; for the च् represents त्, and if this were retained, it would be त् and not च् that would be heard: for by VIII. 2. 1, the change of त् to च् is asiddha for the purposes of this rule.

वृत्तिः ॥ तस्मादतोऽभ्यासादिर्धिमुतादुत्तरस्य द्विहलोऽनस्य तुडागमो भवति ॥

71. After such a lengthened आ of the reduplicate, there is added the augment तुद् (न) to the short अ of the root which ends in a double consonant.

As from अञ्च्-आ अञ्च्=आन् अञ्च्, which with the affixes of the Perfect gives us, आनङ्ग, आनङ्गतु:, आनङ्गुः ॥ From अञ्-आनञ्, आनञ्-आनञ्, आनञ्-आनञ् ॥ Why do we say 'containing two consonants'? Observe आह, आहतु:, आहुः ॥

With regard to तुद् augment, क् is considered like र्, as आनृधतु:, आनृधुः ॥ This proceeds on a vārtika to be found under the Pratyāhāra sūtra ऐ ओच् ॥ The vārtika is तुवृधि-लवेश-विनामाच् क्कारे प्रतिषेधातव्यं ॥ The examples of लवेश are क्त्वः, क्त्वप्रवान्; (See VIII. 2. 18) and of विनाम are कर्तृणाम् and भर्तृणाम् ॥

अश्रोतेश्व ॥ ७२ ॥ पदानि ॥ अश्रोतेः, च ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अद्विहलयं आरम्भः ॥ अश्रोतेश्व दीर्घमुतादभ्यासादुत्तरस्य तुडागमो भवति ॥

72. After the lengthened आ of the reduplicate of अश् (अशोति), comes the augment तुद् (न) before the short अ of the root in the Perfect.

This applies to a case where the root does not contain a double consonant. Thus व्यानशे, व्यानशाते, व्यानशिरे ॥ The rule applies to अश् (Svādi 18) and not to अश् (Kryādi 51); there we have आश, आशतु:, आशुः ॥

भवतेरः ॥ ७३ ॥ पदानि ॥ भवतेः, अः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ भवतेरभ्यासस्याकारविशो भवते लिटि परतः ॥

73. अ is substituted for the vowel of the reduplicate of भू in the Perfect.

As बभूव, बभूवतु:, बभूवुः, बभूवे ॥ Why do we say 'in the Perfect'? Observe बुभूपति and बेभूयते ॥

The word भवते: is shown in the sūtra in the Active Voice, therefore the rule will not apply to Passive and Reflexive forms; as अनुवुभूवे क्त्वलो देव-इतेन ॥ This opinion of Kāśikā, however, is not endorsed by later Grammarians

ससुवेति निगमे ॥ ७४ ॥ पदानि ॥ ससुव, इति, निगमे ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ ससुव इति निपात्यते सुतेलिटि परसेपदं दुगागमो ऽभ्यासस्य चालं निपात्यते ॥

74. In the Veda स्सूव is irregularly formed in the Perfect.

It is derived from सू ॥ Thus स्सूव स्थविर विपश्चिताम् otherwise सूवु ॥ Rig. IV. 18 10.

This word स्सूव might well have been included in sūtra VII. 4. 65.

निजां त्रयाणां गुणः स्तौ ॥ ७५ ॥ पदानि ॥ निजाम्, त्रयाणाम्, गुणः, स्तौ ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ निजादीनां त्रयाणामभ्यासस्य गुणो भवति स्तौ सति ॥

75. Guṇa is substituted for the vowel of the reduplicate, in the Reduplicated Present form (इलु) of निज्, विज् and विप् ॥

Thus नैनैकि, वैवैकि, वैवैहि ॥ The word त्रयाणां could have been spared in this sūtra, as these three roots stand at the end of a subdivision, and निजां would have denoted these three without the word trayāṇam. The word is however used here for the sake of the subsequent sūtra. Why do we say in the reduplicated Present form? Observe निजे in the Perfect.

भूजामित् ॥ ७६ ॥ पदानि ॥ भूजाम्, इत् ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ भूतादीनां त्रयाणामभ्यासस्यकारवेशो भवति स्तौ सति ॥

76. In the Reduplicated Present-form of the three roots भू, मा (माङ्) and हा (ओहाङ्), इ is substituted for the vowel of the reduplicate.

As बिभक्ति, निमीते, (VI. 4. 113) जिहीति ॥ The word 'three' is understood here, therefore not in ओहाङ्—अहाति ॥ The rule applies in the Reduplicated Present system (इलु) only: therefore not in बभा ॥

अस्तिपिपत्योश्च ॥ ७७ ॥ पदानि ॥ अस्ति-पिपत्योः, च ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अस्ति पिपन्ति इत्येतयोरभ्यासस्यकारवेशो भवति स्तौ ॥

77. इ is substituted for the vowel of the reduplicate of भू and पू in the Reduplicated Present-form.

As इयर्ति (VI. 4. 78) पूमम्, पिपति सोमम् ॥

बहुलं छन्दसि ॥ ७८ ॥ पदानि ॥ बहुलम्, छन्दसि ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ छन्दसि विषये ऽभ्यासस्य स्तौ बहुलमिकारवेशो भवति ॥

78. इ is diversely substituted in the Veda, for the vowel of the reduplicate, in the Reduplicated Present-form.

As पूणो विवहि (from वश), जनिमा विवक्ति (from वच), वशं न माना सिपक्ति (from सच), and जिघति सोमम् ॥ But also इयाति, जजनम्, इधनम् as in इयातीत्येवं ह्य्यात्; जजनमिन्द्रं माता यद्वीरं इधनम् धनिहा ॥ All these three roots belong to Juhotyādi class.

सन्यतः ॥ ७९ ॥ पदानि ॥ सनि, अतः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ सनि परतोकारान्ताभ्यासस्यकारवेशो भवति ॥

79. १ is substituted for the final short अ of the reduplicate in the Desiderative.

As पिपशति, थियशति, (VIII. 2. 36; 41) तिष्ठासति, पिपासति ॥ Why do we say in the Desiderative? Observe पपाच ॥ Why do we say “for the अ”? Observe लुप्यति ॥ Why do we say ‘short अ’? Observe पापविषते the Desiderative of the Intensive पापविषते ॥

ओः पुयणज्यपरे ॥ ८० ॥ पदानि ॥ ओः, पु-यण-जि-अपरे ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ सन्तति वसंत इष्विति च ॥ उवर्णान्ताभ्यासस्य पवं यण जकार चावर्णपरे परत इकारविषो भवति सानि प्रलये परतः ॥

80. १ is substituted for the final उ or ऊ of a reduplicate, before a labial, a semi-vowel and before ज्, when अ or आ follows these consonants, in the Desiderative.

The word पु-यण-जि is the Locative singular of the samāhāra dvandva compound of those three words—पुं, यण and ज् ॥ The samāsānta affix ऽच् (V. 4. 106) does not come, as these affixes are anitya. The word अ-पर means that after which is the letter अ ॥

Thus: 1. Labial:—पिपविषते, पिपावशिषति, बिभावशिषति; 2. Semi-vowel:—थियविषति, थियावशिषति, रिरावशिषति, लिलावशिषति; 3. ज्—जिजावशिषति from the root जु ॥

The word पिपविषते is from पु which gets इद augment in सन् (VII. 2. 74), then there is gūṇa, and अत् substitutions, but these latter being sthanivat for reduplication (I. 1. 59), पु is doubled: and for ऊ there is substituted इ by the present sūtra. पिपावशिषति is the Desiderative of the Causative of पु ॥ बिभावशिषति is the Desiderative of the Causative of भु ॥ थियविषति is the Desiderative of पु ‘to mix’, which is सेद् by VII. 2. 49. थियावशिषति is the Desiderative of the Causative of this root. The words रिरावशिषति and लिलावशिषति are the Desiderative of the Causatives of रीति and लुमाति ॥

This sūtra indicates the existence of the following maxim:—अद्विष्वन निमित्ते-प्रपि णो स्थानिषद् भवति, “though not the cause of reduplication, the substitute which takes place when णि follows, becomes like the original”. Thus in बिभावशिषति we have भावि+सन् from भु+णि+सन्, here the आव substitute caused by णि is sthanivat to ऊ, otherwise there would be no उ in the reduplicate to be operated upon by the present sūtra. See VI. 1. 31 also. Why do we say “for the उ or ऊ”? Observe पापविषते, the Desiderative of which will be पापविषति ॥ Why do we say “followed by a labial, semi-vowel or ज्”? Observe अव नुनावशिषति, according to Padamanjari it is अव तुता वशिषति from the sūtra root तु ॥ लुहावशिषति ॥ Why do we say ‘when these consonants are followed by an अ’? Observe लुभ्यति ॥

अवति-शृणोति-द्ववति-प्रवति-द्ववति-व्यवतीनां वा ॥ ८१ ॥ पदानि ॥ अवति-शृणोति-द्ववति-प्रवति-द्ववति-व्यवतीनाम ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अवति शृणोति द्रवति प्रवति द्रवति ध्ववति इयेतेपामभ्यासस्य ओरवर्णपरे यणि वा इकारविषो भवति सानि परतः ॥
